## Acceptance criteria (verbatim from the design doc)

### R1: Word-budget ratchet for skill text
`skill-lint` fails when any markdown file under `skills/` exceeds its recorded budget or repeats a long sentence within itself, so the cut is enforced from the first commit rather than promised at the end.

The budgets live in one table inside `tests/skill-lint.mjs`, one row per file, starting at the 2.9.0 counts so the gate is green before any cut lands; R6 tightens them to the achieved counts. The restatement rule flags a sentence of 12 words or more appearing twice inside one file — measured green today, so it is a pure regression guard for the editorial rule that a rule is stated once per file and pointed to afterwards.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Given the repository before any cut, When `npm run check` runs, Then it passes and the budget table names all eleven markdown files under `skills/` with their 2.9.0 word counts.
- Given a skill markdown file edited to hold one more word than its budget, When `npm run check` runs, Then it exits non-zero and the failure names the file, its budget, and its actual count.
- Given a markdown file added under `skills/` that the budget table does not list, When `npm run check` runs, Then it exits non-zero naming the unbudgeted file.
- Given a copy of the kit in a scratch directory whose skill file repeats a 12-word sentence, When `skill-lint` runs against that copy, Then it exits non-zero naming the file and the repeated sentence.

### R5: Fidelity and cost probe recorded
Six recorded runs — the baseline kit (commit `dfe0dd0`, version 2.9.0) and the slimmed kit, three trials each on one fixture task — show whether workflow behavior regressed, and which way session token cost moved; either direction is a finding to report, never a reason to reject the report.

The runs are real agent sessions, so the human authorizes provider, model, network, and spend before each one; the kit prepares the protocol, fixture, and validator but never invents a provider command. This is the topic's one human-run step, which is why the requirement carries a full checkpoint. If the runs cannot happen, this requirement is `⏭` and the ship gate stops there — a fabricated or fixture-derived report is never acceptable evidence.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Given two recorded conditions of three trials each, When the probe validator runs, Then it exits zero only if both commits are present and distinct, all six trials have a transcript and a usage file, every trial carries a verdict and an evidence pointer for each of the five assessments, the recorded token totals recompute from the raw usage lines, and no candidate trial regresses an assessment against baseline.
- Given a candidate trial missing one assessment verdict, When the validator runs, Then it exits non-zero and names the trial and the missing assessment.
- Given a trial whose usage lines do not sum to its recorded total, When the validator runs, Then it exits non-zero and names both the recorded and the recomputed value.
- Given the two conditions, When the probe report is read, Then it shows both medians and the spread of each condition, so a reader can see the noise beside the comparison.
- Given a candidate median above the baseline median, When the validator runs, Then the report still validates and the validator prints the difference and its direction as a finding — a negative cost result is recorded, not rejected. (amended 2026-10-14, ADR 0009)

## Keep-list (protected clauses)

These classes are never cut. K1, K2, K4, K5, and K6 are already machine-checked, which is why the cut is safe to attempt at all; K3 is the one class that rests on the human read.

| Class | What it covers | What enforces it |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | Every string the test suite pins verbatim — 1,278 harvested literals, ~2,059 words | the vitest suite inside `npm run check` |
| K2 | Tag vocabularies and their resolution rules (`### Checkpoints`, `### Review`, `### Feature review`, and the auto-resolution) | pinned markers in the vitest suite |
| K3 | Decision-record clauses: the informed-stop and ship-gate wording recorded by ADR 0003 and ADR 0006 | the human read of the diff at each slice's stop |
| K4 | The cross-file boilerplate — root check, discovery recipe, tool-freedom clause, canonical codemode sweep script | `skill-lint` check 13b (verbatim identity across files) |
| K5 | Command and format contracts in `references/` — progress-file template, packet sections, digest shape, design-format contract | pinned markers and the prescription sweep |
| K6 | The tool-freedom wording the prescription sweep classifies as sanctioned | `prescription-sweep.mjs` inside `npm run check` |

## The five editorial rules

These are the cut rules; R6 copies them into `AGENTS.md` unchanged.

- **E1 — Cut preamble, not instruction.** Every sentence states a trigger, an action, or a concrete example. Motivation and summary sentences go, unless removing the reason invites a wrong action (keep "never `cd`", drop "this matters because").
- **E2 — Delete what a competent agent already does.** No reminders to read the file it must read, to be careful, or to keep things consistent in the abstract. Non-obvious house rules stay.
- **E3 — One home per rule, per file.** The first mention is complete; later mentions are a pointer. Cross-file duplication stays, because each skill loads on its own.
- **E4 — Shortest carrier wins.** If a table row, a command, or a list item says it in fewer words than the prose, use the carrier. Prose is for judgment that cannot be tabulated; rare-path detail moves into `references/` rather than being deleted.
- **E5 — Never cut a contract or a decision record.** The keep-list above survives verbatim; only the explanation around it is slimmed.

## Probe mechanics

The kit lives in `tests/evals/skill-slimming/`: a protocol file, a fixture task description, a validator, and a README. It mirrors the R4 harness's safety rules — no credentials in the repo, no guessed provider command, human authorization before every run — while dropping its large/control matrix.

- **Conditions.** Baseline is commit `dfe0dd0` (the pre-slim main head, version 2.9.0); the candidate is this topic's slimmed commit. Each condition runs the same fixture task three times in fresh sessions: six runs, no more.
- **Fixture.** One small but real slice that exercises the full pipeline — design, then execute with a feature gate, then finalize — so the probe observes the phase stops and the approval behavior, not just prose.
- **Assessments.** The five the R4 protocol established: vertical-slices, approval, current-only-design, predecessor-grounding, premature-finalize-blocking. Each trial records a verdict and an evidence pointer into its own transcript.
- **Accounting.** `usage.mjs` recomputes totals from the provider-exported usage lines; the validator rejects a recorded total that disagrees with the recomputation, so the numbers cannot be hand-typed.
- **Verdict.** No candidate trial may regress an assessment, and the candidate median total tokens must be below the baseline median. The report shows both medians and both spreads, so the reader sees the noise rather than a bare claim.
- **Honesty.** The deterministic size claim (words) and the observed cost claim (tokens, six runs) are reported as two separate facts; a smaller corpus that costs more tokens per session is a finding, not a failure to hide.

## Approaches considered

**Cut the unpinned prose versus re-anchor the pin surface.** Re-anchoring would move the ~2,059 pinned words onto a smaller marker vocabulary, freeing more text to rewrite. It lost on measurement: 86.6% of the corpus is already unpinned, so the pins bound almost nothing, while re-anchoring would touch the suites that currently guarantee behavior for no additional cut.

**One de-duplicated boilerplate versus keeping it inline.** De-duplication would recover 509 words by pointing each skill at a shared statement. It lost because the skills load independently, the boilerplate sits at gates where a pointer is fragile, a settled decision already rejected it, and `skill-lint` check 13b asserts the verbatim identity — the gain is 3% for a real regression risk.

**Six-run probe versus the 16-run matrix versus two runs versus the suite alone.** The 16-run matrix costs roughly three times as much for the same question; two runs cannot separate skill-text savings from task variance; the suite alone proves pins, not behavior. Six runs give a median and a spread at a cost the human can authorize in one sitting. The task-level savings claim is deliberately kept separate from the deterministic word claim, because a terse skill that makes an agent loop costs more tokens than it saved.

**Ratchet versus one-off measurement.** A one-off cut has no way to stay cut: the corpus already grew 28% after a pass that judged it lean. Budgets in `skill-lint` cost one table and fail loudly.

**A new keep-list checker versus the existing gates plus a human read.** A dedicated checker would duplicate what the suite and `skill-lint` already assert (K1, K2, K4, K5, K6) and still could not judge K3, which is prose about decisions. The human read of the diff remains the only honest test for K3.

**Words versus lines as the unit.** Lines depend on wrapping and on how an editor reflows a paragraph, so a line-count target would reward re-wrapping rather than editing. Words are stable, comparable across files, and trivially checked.

**One design doc, one PR versus an umbrella of per-file docs.** The work is one cohesive change to one class of files with one verification story; splitting it by file would multiply the ceremony around a single mechanical pass.

+# ADR 0009: The cost probe reports direction — it does not require it
+
+Date: 2026-10-14
+Status: accepted
+
+## Context
+
+R5 of the skill-slimming topic ran the fidelity/cost probe: six authorized agent sessions, the baseline kit (`dfe0dd0`, 2.9.0) and the slimmed kit, three trials each on one fixture task. Behavior held — all five assessments passed in all six trials, no regression. Cost did not: the candidate median was 2,021,740 tokens against the baseline's 1,995,148, a rise of 26,592 (+1.3%), with within-condition spreads of 266,689 (13%) and 554,058 (27%).
+
+The design's R5 criterion required "the candidate median total tokens are below the baseline median". The validator therefore rejected a report that was complete, honest, and fully recomputable — because the hypothesis it measured did not hold.
+
+## Decision
+
+A probe report validates on **structure and verifiable numbers only**: both commits present and distinct, six trials each with a transcript and a usage file, every trial carrying a verdict and an evidence pointer for each of the five assessments, token totals recomputed from the raw usage lines, and no candidate trial regressing an assessment against baseline.
+
+The **direction** of the cost comparison is a finding the validator prints (with the delta), never a validity property. A candidate median above the baseline median validates and is reported as a negative result.
+
+## Why
+
+A validator that encodes the hoped-for direction turns a measurement into a verdict on the hypothesis. It then rewards re-running until the numbers look right, which is the one thing an evidence harness must never do.
+
+The measurement also explains why the original expectation was never testable at this sample size. About 95% of every trial's tokens are context re-read on each turn, so a session's cost is approximately turns x context. The whole skill corpus is roughly 20k tokens of a context that reaches 72k-96k, about 22%. The 16.3% word cut therefore removes ~3.3k tokens, a ~3.7% effect on the session total, against a 13-27% noise band. Three trials cannot resolve it in either direction.
+
+## Rejected alternatives
+
+- **Keep the criterion and mark R5 failed.** It would report "the slimming made sessions costlier" from a +1.3% difference whose spread is ten times larger — an unsupported claim, and the opposite error from the one the criterion was written to prevent.
+- **Add trials until the direction flips.** Choosing the sample size after seeing the result converts the probe into a search for a favourable number. If more trials are ever run, they get their own pre-declared protocol and their result is reported whatever it says.
+- **Drop the cost claim entirely.** The size claim (words) and the cost claim (tokens) stay two separate reported facts, which is what the design already promised; the second one is now measured and reported without a required sign.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- The probe's value becomes the finding it produces, not a threshold it clears: the word cut bought no measurable token saving, and behavior fidelity is unaffected.
+- Any future probe keeps the structural checks; only the direction is informational.
+- The gap between "smaller corpus" and "cheaper sessions" is now documented: the lever for cost is turns and context volume, not prose length.

+# ADR 0010: Word budgets ratchet from measured counts, not a target percentage
+
+Date: 2026-10-14
+Status: accepted
+
+## Context
+
+The skill-slimming topic set out to cut every skill markdown file to 70% of its 2.9.0 word count. Measured against the pins, that target held for two of the eleven files and failed for the rest: the reference files are contract text end to end (`design-format.md` finished at 87% of its count, `progress-format.md` at 78%, `review.md` at 76%), and the SKILL.md files landed between 0% and 27% depending on how much of each was pinned prose.
+
+The first pass of the same kind, in August, judged the corpus "already lean" and left no gate behind it. The corpus then grew 28%.
+
+## Decision
+
+`skill-lint` holds the ratchet, and both the lint table and the feature E2E use the same numbers:
+
+- a **per-file budget** = the file's measured count plus 10% headroom, rounded up;
+- a **corpus ceiling** = the measured total plus 10% headroom, rounded up (14,143 words).
+
+Exceeding either fails by file name and count. The aggregate claim reported for this topic is what was achieved — a 16.3% cut, 15,360 to 12,857 words — not a target that was missed.
+
+## Why
+
+**A ratchet beats a percentage.** The value of these budgets is that the corpus cannot drift back up unnoticed. A percentage of a historical count encodes an editorial ambition; it does not encode anything about the file. When the ambition and the contract conflict, the contract wins and the number has to move, so a percentage target either blocks legitimate contract text or gets waived — and a waived gate teaches the next agent that these gates are negotiable.
+
+**The measured floor is the honest ceiling.** Ten percent headroom is enough for a clarified sentence and too little for a new section, which is the shape of change the gate should force into a design decision.
+
+**The corpus claim is a measurement, not a promise.** Reporting "16.3% smaller" beside "no measurable token saving" (ADR 0009) keeps both facts visible; a rounded claim of "30% leaner" would have been false.
+
+## Rejected alternatives
+
+- **Keep the 70% per-file target and mark the requirements failed.** It would report an unmet number that no further editing could reach without deleting pinned contracts — a target, not an outcome.
+- **Drop budgets entirely and rely on review.** That is the state that produced the 28% regrowth.
+- **Budget the corpus only.** A total lets one file balloon while another shrinks to compensate, which is exactly how a heavy file gets heavier.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- The gate is a ratchet: every future slimming pass lowers the numbers, and no pass can raise them without a recorded decision.
+- Per-file budgets are now derived data — they are regenerated from the measured counts when skill text changes, and the lint table and the E2E must move together.
+- The topic's stated goal changes shape: from "cut 30%" to "hold the achieved floor and report what the cut bought", which the probe answered honestly.
diff --git a/docs/lessons.md b/docs/lessons.md
index 33bcbb9..cd6ebad 100644
--- a/docs/lessons.md
+++ b/docs/lessons.md
@@ -32,6 +32,7 @@ Retire rules that no longer apply during finalizing.
 - **A new content lint's first run over a live corpus surfaces stragglers — reconcile each, never exempt silently.** Expect sites the design inventory missed. Every failure gets an explicit decision: frame the sentence, or deliberately pin the recipe in the rule's allowlist with a comment saying so. The pins are policy and extending them is a reviewed decision — a catch-all exemption to make the run green silently deletes the policy.
 - **Generating a code file whose content contains markdown fences: write it from a JSON-encoded literal, not a template literal.** Nested backtick escaping (fences inside template literals) is corrupt-prone and fails only at transform time, several steps after the write. Hand the literal content through a non-evaluated channel (a data parameter) and keep generator code free of backtick soup.
 - **Widening a prose lint to a new fence language is a lint-surface change — extend the checker in the same change as the first content it will read.** Text inside a fence language the checker cannot parse is unclassified, so a rule violation written in the new syntax passes silently and the guarantee the lint advertises is weaker than it reads. Add the language to the extractor and land fixtures for its shapes before, or together with, the first real block; the checker and the content are one change, not two.
+- **A pinned-prose census must harvest regex-pinned phrases, not only string literals.** Tests often assert a contract sentence through `expect(source).toMatch(/some exact sentence/)`; a harvest that collects only quoted literals reports those sentences as free text, and a rewrite deletes them (observed: eight contract phrases in one skill file broke the suite after a literal-only census called them unpinned). Extract phrases from regex literals too, and treat a failing assertion — not the census — as the authority on what is pinned.
 - **Exact-text edits match the whole line, not a prefix of it.** An oldText that matches only the line prefix replaces the prefix and leaves the suffix appended after the new text (observed: a timestamp landed as `<new>T<old-suffix>`). Anchor on the complete line — or a span bounded on both ends — and verify the touched line after the edit.

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+const target = process.argv[2];
+const pins = new Set();
+const add = (s) => { if (s && s.length >= 20) pins.add(s); };
+const unquote = (raw) => { try { return JSON.parse('"' + raw.replace(/"/g, '\\"') + '"'); } catch { return null; } };
+const harvest = (src) => {
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/"((?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*)"/g)) add(unquote(m[1].replace(/\\\\/g, '\\')));
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/`([^`]{20,})`/g)) add(m[1]);
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/\/((?:[^\/\\\n]|\\.){20,})\/[gimsuy]*/g)) {
+    const body = m[1].replace(/\\([().\[\]{}*+?^$|/])/g, '$1');
+    for (const part of body.split('|')) add(part.replace(/[\[\](){}*+?^$]/g, '').replace(/\\s[+*]/g, ' ').trim());
+  }
+};
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/markers.mjs', 'utf8'));
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/skill-lint.mjs', 'utf8'));
+for (const f of readdirSync('tests')) {
+  if (!/\.(mjs|ts)$/.test(f) || ['markers.mjs', 'skill-lint.mjs', 'prescription-sweep.mjs'].includes(f)) continue;
+  const src = readFileSync(join('tests', f), 'utf8');
+  if (src.includes('skills/')) harvest(src);
+}
+const pinList = [...pins];
+for (const target of process.argv.slice(2)) {
+  const text = readFileSync(target, 'utf8');
+  const cov = new Array(text.length).fill(false);
+  for (const p of pinList) { let i = text.indexOf(p); while (i !== -1) { for (let k = i; k < i + p.length; k++) cov[k] = true; i = text.indexOf(p, i + 1); } }
+  const offsets = [];
+  let off = 0;
+  for (const line of text.split('\n')) { offsets.push(off); off += line.length + 1; }
+  const total = text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;
+  const pinnedWords = Math.round(total * (cov.reduce((a, b) => a + (b ? 1 : 0), 0) / text.length));
+  console.log('== ' + target + ': ' + total + ' words, ~' + pinnedWords + ' pinned (' + (100 * pinnedWords / total).toFixed(0) + '%), free ~' + (total - pinnedWords));
+  console.log('   longest lines with the least pinned content:');
+  const rows = text.split('\n').map((l, i) => {
+    const t = l.trim();
+    const words = t.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;
+    if (words < 25) return null;
+    const base = offsets[i];
+    const linePinned = cov.slice(base, base + l.length).reduce((a, b) => a + (b ? 1 : 0), 0);
+    const share = l.length ? linePinned / l.length : 0;
+    const freeWords = Math.round(words * (1 - share));
+    return { i: i + 1, words, freeWords, t };
+  }).filter(Boolean).sort((a, b) => b.freeWords - a.freeWords).slice(0, 12);
+  for (const r of rows) console.log('   ' + String(r.freeWords).padStart(4) + ' free/' + String(r.words).padStart(3) + 'w L' + String(r.i).padStart(3) + '  ' + r.t.slice(0, 105));
+}

+import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+const files = [];
+const walk = (d) => { for (const e of readdirSync(d)) { const p = join(d, e); if (statSync(p).isDirectory()) walk(p); else if (/\.md$/.test(e)) files.push(p); } };
+walk('skills');
+const pins = new Set();
+const add = (s) => { if (s && s.length >= 20) pins.add(s); };
+const unquote = (raw) => { try { return JSON.parse('"' + raw.replace(/"/g, '\\"') + '"'); } catch { return null; } };
+const harvest = (src) => {
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/"((?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*)"/g)) add(unquote(m[1].replace(/\\\\/g, '\\')));
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/`([^`]{20,})`/g)) add(m[1]);
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/\/((?:[^\/\\\n]|\\.){20,})\/[gimsuy]*/g)) {
+    const body = m[1].replace(/\\([().\[\]{}*+?^$|/])/g, '$1');
+    for (const part of body.split('|')) {
+      const phrase = part.replace(/[\[\](){}*+?^$]/g, '').replace(/\\s\+|\\s\*/g, ' ').trim();
+      add(phrase);
+    }
+  }
+};
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/markers.mjs', 'utf8'));
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/skill-lint.mjs', 'utf8'));
+for (const f of readdirSync('tests')) {
+  if (!/\.(mjs|ts)$/.test(f) || ['markers.mjs', 'skill-lint.mjs', 'prescription-sweep.mjs'].includes(f)) continue;
+  const src = readFileSync(join('tests', f), 'utf8');
+  if (src.includes('skills/')) harvest(src);
+}
+const pinList = [...pins];
+console.log('pin pool (literals + regex phrases): ' + pinList.length);
+console.log('file'.padEnd(56) + 'base'.padStart(6) + 'pinned'.padStart(8) + 'free'.padStart(7) + '70%cap'.padStart(8) + 'freeAfterCap'.padStart(13));
+let totals = { base: 0, pinned: 0, cap: 0 };
+for (const f of files) {
+  const base = spawnSync('git', ['show', 'HEAD~1:' + f], { encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout || readFileSync(f, 'utf8');
+  const cov = new Array(base.length).fill(false);
+  for (const p of pinList) { let i = base.indexOf(p); while (i !== -1) { for (let k = i; k < i + p.length; k++) cov[k] = true; i = base.indexOf(p, i + 1); } }
+  const words = base.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;
+  const pw = Math.round(words * (cov.reduce((a, b) => a + (b ? 1 : 0), 0) / base.length));
+  const cap = Math.floor(words * 0.7);
+  totals.base += words; totals.pinned += pw; totals.cap += cap;
+  console.log(f.replace('skills/pwk-', '').padEnd(56) + String(words).padStart(6) + String(pw).padStart(8) + String(words - pw).padStart(7) + String(cap).padStart(8) + String(words - pw - cap).padStart(13));
+}
+console.log('TOTAL base ' + totals.base + ' | pinned ' + totals.pinned + ' | 70% cap ' + totals.cap + ' | free-after-cap ' + (totals.base - totals.pinned - totals.cap));

@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+// Pinned phrases present in a skill file: test string literals AND regex-pinned phrases.
+// Usage: node pins-for.mjs <repo-relative path>
+import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+const target = process.argv[2];
+const pins = new Set();
+const add = (s) => { if (s && s.length >= 20) pins.add(s); };
+const unquote = (raw) => { try { return JSON.parse('"' + raw.replace(/"/g, '\\"') + '"'); } catch { return null; } };
+const harvest = (src) => {
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/"((?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*)"/g)) add(unquote(m[1].replace(/\\\\/g, '\\')));
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/`([^`]{20,})`/g)) add(m[1]);
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/\/((?:[^\/\\\n]|\\.){20,})\/[gimsuy]*/g)) {
+    const body = m[1].replace(/\\([().\[\]{}*+?^$|/])/g, '$1');
+    for (const part of body.split('|')) {
+      const phrase = part.replace(/[\[\](){}*+?^$]/g, '').replace(/\\s\+|\\s\*/g, ' ').trim();
+      add(phrase);
+    }
+  }
+};
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/markers.mjs', 'utf8'));
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/skill-lint.mjs', 'utf8'));
+for (const f of readdirSync('tests')) {
+  if (!/\.(mjs|ts)$/.test(f) || ['markers.mjs', 'skill-lint.mjs', 'prescription-sweep.mjs'].includes(f)) continue;
+  const src = readFileSync(join('tests', f), 'utf8');
+  if (src.includes('skills/')) harvest(src);
+}
+const text = readFileSync(target, 'utf8');
+const hits = [...pins].filter((p) => text.includes(p)).sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length);
+let words = 0;
+for (const h of hits) words += h.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;
+console.log(target + ': ' + hits.length + ' pinned phrases present, ~' + words + ' pinned words, ' + text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length + ' total');
+for (const h of hits) console.log('  ' + JSON.stringify(h.length > 130 ? h.slice(0, 130) + '…' : h));
diff --git a/docs/plans/2026-10-14-skill-slimming-2/pins-lost.mjs b/docs/plans/2026-10-14-skill-slimming-2/pins-lost.mjs

index 0000000..7268fdd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/plans/2026-10-14-skill-slimming-2/pins-lost.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+// Pins present in the committed version of a file but missing from the working copy.
+// Harvests BOTH quoted string literals and regex-pinned phrases (a test that asserts an
+// exact sentence with toMatch(/.../) pins that sentence just as hard as toContain("...").
+import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+const target = process.argv[2];
+const pins = new Set();
+const add = (s) => { if (s && s.length >= 20) pins.add(s); };
+const unquote = (raw) => { try { return JSON.parse('"' + raw.replace(/"/g, '\\"') + '"'); } catch { return null; } };
+const harvest = (src) => {
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/"((?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*)"/g)) add(unquote(m[1].replace(/\\\\/g, '\\')));
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/`([^`]{20,})`/g)) add(m[1]);
+  // regex literals: strip escapes, then keep each literal alternative long enough to be prose
+  for (const m of src.matchAll(/\/((?:[^\/\\\n]|\\.){20,})\/[gimsuy]*/g)) {
+    const body = m[1].replace(/\\([().\[\]{}*+?^$|/])/g, '$1');
+    for (const part of body.split('|')) {
+      const phrase = part.replace(/[\[\](){}*+?^$]/g, '').replace(/\\s\+|\\s\*/g, ' ').trim();
+      add(phrase);
+    }
+  }
+};
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/markers.mjs', 'utf8'));
+harvest(readFileSync('tests/skill-lint.mjs', 'utf8'));
+for (const f of readdirSync('tests')) {
+  if (!/\.(mjs|ts)$/.test(f) || ['markers.mjs', 'skill-lint.mjs', 'prescription-sweep.mjs'].includes(f)) continue;
+  const src = readFileSync(join('tests', f), 'utf8');
+  if (src.includes('skills/')) harvest(src);
+}
+const old = spawnSync('git', ['show', 'HEAD:' + target], { encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout;
+const now = readFileSync(target, 'utf8');
+const lost = [...pins].filter((p) => old.includes(p) && !now.includes(p));
+console.log('LOST from ' + target + ': ' + lost.length + '  (pin pool ' + pins.size + ')');
+for (const p of lost) console.log('  [' + p.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length + 'w] ' + JSON.stringify(p.slice(0, 150)));

 ## Deviation records
 
+- **The effective pin surface is much larger than the pinned-word share.** Tests assert prose *fragments* (`/number each question/i`, `/passes immediately, probe why/`, `/every requirement's Done cell is terminal/`), and each fragment pins the sentence that carries it. The corrected census puts pinned words at ~15% of the corpus, yet a deletion-led rewrite of 12 heavy lines in `pwk-brainstorming` removed only 8% — the sentences around those fragments are effectively fixed. Closing the last stretch to a 30% cut would require re-anchoring fragment assertions to behavior (a test-side change the design deliberately excluded), which is its own topic, not a bigger editing pass.
+- **R2 per-file ceilings are measured, not fixed at 70% (human decision, Option 1).** `pwk-executing-tasks` landed at 2,884 words — 73.2% of its 2.9.0 count, a 26.8% cut — with the full suite green. It did not reach the designed 2,755 (70%). Cause: the baseline census harvested test *string literals* but not assertions written as regex patterns, so it reported eight contract phrases as free text; each restoration cost words back. The same census now harvests regex-pinned phrases (pin pool 1,278 → 1,541; pinned words 2,059 → 2,290). Decision: each file is slimmed to its true floor with the suite green, the ratchet and the acceptance budgets are set from the achieved numbers, and the aggregate target is **≥25%** with 30% reported rather than required. Evidence: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-skill-slimming-2/pin-census-v2.mjs` (per-file pinned/free/slack) and `pins-for.mjs` / `pins-lost.mjs` (the corrected harvesters).
+
+- **R5's cost criterion was amended: the validator reports the direction, it does not require it (ADR 0009).** The probe measured a candidate median of 2,021,740 against the baseline's 1,995,148 (+1.3%), with within-condition spreads of 266,689 (13%) and 554,058 (27%). The original criterion required the candidate median to be *below* the baseline's, so the validator rejected a report that was complete, honest, and fully recomputable — on the direction of its result. Decision: a report validates on structure and verifiable numbers only, and the direction is printed as a finding. Cause of the non-result: ~95% of a trial's tokens are context re-read, the skill corpus is ~22% of the context, so a 16.3% word cut is a ~3.7% effect against a 13–27% noise band — unmeasurable at three trials. Rejected: keeping the criterion and failing R5 (which would assert "slimming made sessions costlier" from noise), and adding trials until the direction flipped. Human decision 2026-10-14 (Option b).
+
+- **R4's 70% per-file cut is unreachable for three of the five reference files; the topic aggregate misses even the relaxed target (measured 2026-10-14).** Achieved, against each file's 70% ceiling:
+
+  | File | 2.9.0 | Now | Cut | 70% cap | |
+  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
+  | `umbrella.md` | 402 | 275 | 31.6% | 281 | ✅ inside |
+  | `resume.md` | 646 | 449 | 30.5% | 452 | ✅ inside |
+  | `review.md` | 804 | 607 | 24.5% | 562 | ✖ over |
+  | `progress-format.md` | 1,298 | 1,007 | 22.4% | 908 | ✖ over |
+  | `design-format.md` | 1,498 | 1,308 | 12.7% | 1,048 | ✖ over |
+
+  Every cut preserved the pinned phrase set (`pins-lost.mjs` → 0 lost per file) and the suite (300 pass; only this topic's three unbuilt E2E scenarios red). Cause: once the explanatory sentences are gone these files are rules end to end — `design-format.md`'s block rules, `progress-format.md`'s row vocabulary and digest fill rules, `review.md`'s packet-helper CLI contract — each machine-pinned or keep-list K5 contract. The cuttable prose measures 15–25%, not 30%. The corpus therefore lands at ~12,860 of 15,360 words — **a 16.3% cut**, below the design's 30% and below the ≥25% set as the relaxed target in the R2 deviation (Option 1). Decision needed: accept the measured floors (budgets from achieved numbers, as R2/R3) with the aggregate claim reduced to what was achieved, or extend scope (e.g. re-anchoring pinned assertions off prose — a design non-goal). **Human decision (2026-10-14, Option 1): accept the measured floors.** R4 closes ✅ with the deviation recorded; at R6 the budget table and the acceptance budgets are set from the achieved counts plus 10% headroom, and the aggregate claim is reduced to the achieved ~16%.
+

-1. **Mark the requirement 🔄** (Done column), read its `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags, and check `docs/lessons.md` for a rule that applies to this slice.
-2. **Write a meaningful test (red), then implement (green)** — TDD discipline. Encode the requirement's acceptance criteria as a real test through the public interface; run it; confirm it fails; implement to green. Skip the per-slice test only when the slice has no independent observable behavior (the feature E2E covers it). Follow the meaningful-test rules: (1) **Test observable behavior** — assert on what the feature produces or changes (a return value, persisted/updated data, an emitted event, an HTTP response) through its public interface; these assertions keep passing as the implementation changes. (2) **Write a per-slice test when the slice has its own observable behavior** — when a slice is pure config or a trivial extraction, the feature E2E covers it and a per-slice test is unnecessary. (Mirrored in `pwk-brainstorming` and `docs/lessons.md`.)

With the default `none`, show the red→green inline and proceed.
-4. **Regression check after each commit** — run the **full existing suite**. This is what catches cross-requirement regressions (a later requirement breaking an earlier one's test). The **feature E2E stays red until the last requirement lands**; you may run it to watch the failure point advance, but it is gated only at the ship checkpoint — never expect it green per-commit.
-5. **Learn.** Caught a repeat mistake? Append a **generic** rule to `docs/lessons.md` (strip domain specifics).

index 0000000..e1dc286
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/evals/skill-slimming/README.md
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+# Skill-slimming fidelity and cost probe
+
+A read-only protocol for the one observed claim in the skill-slimming topic: that the slimmed kit still drives the workflow correctly and costs fewer tokens per session. The deterministic size claim (words) lives in `skill-lint` and the feature E2E; this directory holds the separate, observed cost claim. It never invokes a provider or a model, and it holds no credentials.
+
+Six runs total: the baseline kit (commit `dfe0dd0`, version 2.9.0) and the slimmed candidate, three fresh trials each on the same fixture task. A human authorizes the provider, model, network, and spend before every run.
+
+## Safe manual workflow
+
+Run from a disposable, workspace-local session directory. No credentials, no provider config, and no credential-bearing transcripts belong in this repository.
+
+Before every provider invocation, explicitly authorize the provider, model, network access, and any spend. Then run your locally installed agent in a fresh workspace and export the session transcript and the provider-exported usage JSONL. The exact provider command is intentionally not supplied — it is provider-specific and must not be guessed here.
+
+For each trial, the report JSON records:
+
+- `commits.baseline` / `commits.candidate` — the two full git hashes, which must differ;
+- `trialId` (`baseline-1`…`candidate-3`), `fresh: true`, `evidence.transcript`, `evidence.usage`, the recomputed `usage` totals, and one assessment entry per name in `protocol.json` carrying a `verdict` and an `evidence` pointer.
+
+Validate the report:
+
+    node tests/evals/skill-slimming/validate.mjs <report.json>
+
+Exit 0 requires both commits present and distinct; all six trials with a transcript and a usage file; every trial carrying a verdict and an evidence pointer for each of the five assessments; the recorded token totals recomputing from the raw usage lines; no candidate trial regressing an assessment against baseline; and the candidate median total tokens below the baseline median. The validator prints both medians and both spreads, so the reader sees the noise beside the comparison.
+
+## Reading the result
+
+The word count and the token count are two separate facts. A smaller corpus that costs more tokens per session is a finding to report, not to hide — a terse skill that makes an agent loop costs more than it saved.
+
+## Recorded runs
+
+`runs/2026-10-14/` holds the topic's one recorded probe: six authorized sessions, their transcripts, the recomputed usage lines, and the validator's verdict. Its `README.md` states the conditions, the model actually used, and the result — including that the word cut produced no measurable token saving.
+
+Fixtures under `fixtures/` exercise the validator's accept and reject paths. They are not behavioral evidence and must never be presented as a recorded run. If no authorized runs happen, record that limitation and leave the probe unrecorded; a fabricated report is never acceptable evidence.

+# Fixture task
+
+One small but real slice, run identically under both conditions. It exercises the full pipeline — design, execute with a feature gate, finalize — so the probe observes the phase stops and the approval behavior, not just prose.
+
+## Prompt
+
+Paste this into a fresh session of the kit under test, in a scratch project that has a small existing script with tests:
+
+> Add a `--since <ISO date>` filter to this project's log-summary script: entries older than the date are excluded, an unparseable date is an error, and the change needs tests. Design it first.
+
+Let the session run to completion without extra steering. Authorize the gates it asks about, and record what actually happened.
+
+## What each trial records
+
+One verdict and one evidence pointer per assessment, so a reader can check the claim against the transcript:
+
+| Assessment | Passes when the transcript shows |
+|---|---|
+| `vertical-slices` | The work is one slice that lands and verifies, not a half-built framework |
+| `approval` | The agent stopped at the design gate and the ship checkpoint and waited |
+| `current-only-design` | The design doc describes the current slice, with no later-slice speculation |
+| `predecessor-grounding` | Claims about existing code are grounded in files it actually read |
+| `premature-finalize-blocking` | A finalize attempt before the requirements were terminal was refused |
+
+## Conditions
+
+| Condition | Revision | Trials |
+|---|---|---|
+| baseline | `dfe0dd0` (version 2.9.0) | 3 |
+| candidate | the slimmed commit under test | 3 |
+
+Six runs, no more. Each trial is a fresh session, so no context carries over.

+# Fixtures
+
+These files exercise the validator's accept and reject paths in `tests/skill-probe.test.ts` and the skill-slimming feature E2E. `report-complete.json` must validate; `report-missing-assessment.json` must be rejected naming the dropped assessment.
+
+They are not behavioral evidence: the token numbers are hand-set to give the validator something to recompute, and no agent session produced them. The recorded probe report for the topic must come from the six authorized runs described in `../README.md` — never from these fixtures.

@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+# Probe run — 2026-10-14
+
+The recorded R5 result: six authorized agent sessions, three per condition, on one fixture task (`../../fixture-task.md`). This is the topic's observed cost claim; the deterministic size claim lives in `skill-lint` and the feature E2E.
+
+## Conditions
+
+| Condition | Kit | Revision | `pwk-executing-tasks/SKILL.md` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| baseline | npm 2.9.0 | `dfe0dd0455fd952756eb7a9d231f88ff96a496b4` | 3,937 words |
+| candidate | slimmed | `c3df7fc73bcf4242fbffbaeda45964fac0869ef2` | 2,884 words |
+
+Each condition ran in its own isolated HOME whose settings named only that condition's kit as a local package — no other packages, no competing skill sources. Every transcript's skill paths cite its own worktree, which is the provenance check.
+
+**Model:** every session started on `zai/glm-5.3` and switched to `olaparty/deepseek-flash` within seconds. The switch is identical in all six trials, so the comparison is like-for-like; the effective model was `olaparty/deepseek-flash`.
+
+## Result
+
+| Condition | Trials | Median | Spread |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| baseline | 1,888,883 · 2,155,572 · 1,995,148 | 1,995,148 | 266,689 (13%) |
+| candidate | 2,393,815 · 1,839,757 · 2,021,740 | 2,021,740 | 554,058 (27%) |
+
+- **Fidelity: held.** All five assessments passed in all six trials — 15/15 in each condition, no regression.
+- **Cost: no detectable saving.** The candidate median is 26,592 tokens higher (+1.3%), against spreads of 13% and 27%. A difference this small is not resolvable at three trials per condition.
+
+Why the word cut could not move the number: about **95% of each trial's tokens are context re-read** (`cacheRead`) rather than fresh input, so a session costs roughly *turns x context*. The whole skill corpus is ~20k tokens of a context that reaches 72k–96k (~22%). A 16.3% word cut removes ~3.3k tokens — a ~3.7% effect on the session total, well under the noise floor. The lever for cost is turns and context volume, not prose length.
+
+## Files
+
+| File | What it is |
+|---|---|
+| `report.json` | the recorded report: commits, six trials, recomputed usage, five verdicts with evidence pointers |
+| `validator-output.txt` | the validator's verdict on this report (exit 0) |
+| `evidence/<trial>.transcript.jsonl` | the session transcript, one per trial |
+| `evidence/<trial>.usage.jsonl` | the usage lines the report's totals are recomputed from |
+
+## Transcript integrity
+
+| File | sha256 (prefix) |
+|---|---|
+| `baseline-1.transcript.jsonl` | `65059c75e687cc9a…` |
+| `baseline-2.transcript.jsonl` | `2fcc1a262168f055…` |
+| `baseline-3.transcript.jsonl` | `1f6869ec4f907636…` |
+| `candidate-1.transcript.jsonl` | `33cbbda66bc10bec…` |
+| `candidate-2.transcript.jsonl` | `61da5ac63e3a1fc7…` |
+| `candidate-3.transcript.jsonl` | `9608bf4e280d8dfa…` |
+
+The transcripts contain no credentials (scanned for key and token patterns) and no user memory: each session loaded only the kit under test.
+
+## Validate
+
+```sh
+node tests/evals/skill-slimming/validate.mjs tests/evals/skill-slimming/runs/2026-10-14/report.json
+```
+
+Exit 0 means structure and numbers hold. The cost **direction** is a finding the validator prints, never a reason to reject the report (ADR 0009).

(An approved ADR goes to `docs/adr/`, which sits outside the writable boundary — the human writes it themselves or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`; the design phase never unlocks it.) The design doc is the **single buildable artifact** — each requirement carries its own acceptance criteria and review tags, and the executor builds straight from it; nothing is re-derived into a second document later. Source-writing happens in `pwk-executing-tasks`.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Proportionality: trivial vs non-trivial\n\nClassify the change at the start.\n\n- **Trivial** — typo or obvious bugfix with no open design questions, config/version bump, single-function change, or anything the human flags as trivial. Skip steps 3–6; read the design-format reference and run the validator in step 7, writing a **minimal** design doc in one turn (an `In short:` one-liner — what + why + approach in plain words, plus a single `### R1:` requirement block with its criteria and tags, and an optional `## Production-risk areas` line — and deliberately **no `## Feature acceptance`**: a trivial slice's ship gate is the full existing suite, no E2E is manufactured for it), and hand off to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`. The guard still enforces read-only — trivial compresses the phase to one turn, it doesn't skip it.\n- **Non-trivial** — open design questions, multiple approaches, cross-module impact, or new behavior. Run the full process below.\n\nWhen unsure, ask: \"This looks trivial — fast-path it, or full brainstorm?\" Default to full.\n\n## Scope and granularity\n\n**One design doc = one PR; one requirement = one testable slice within it.** Most work is a single design doc; several requirements serving one cohesive outcome do not force an umbrella.\n\nBefore drafting, assess whether a large request has distinct testable outcomes that need separate design/execute cycles. If so, propose an **umbrella** of vertical slices with one-line scopes and a build order, and get human approval before writing an overview or design. A layers-only split (database, API, UI) is not a vertical split: each slice delivers testable behavior. Design only the current slice; ground later designs in implemented code, not speculative sibling designs. The umbrella still ships as one PR on one branch, finalized once.\n\n**One folder per topic:** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/`, containing `<leaf>-design.md`, `<leaf>-progress.md`, and `<leaf>-review-packet*.md`; `<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic. More than one leaf adds `overview.md`. The whole folder is the creation/discovery/disposal unit.\n\n**Umbrella trigger:** before proposing or writing a new umbrella, or when discovery finds an existing `overview.md` beside this design, read [references/umbrella.md](references/umbrella.md). It defines the status-free roster, first/later-slice procedures, and header-only predecessor reporting. Build order is advisory, not an enforcement gate. An existing roster means the split is already decided; design the current slice against it.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Check git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`. Uncommitted work? Ask the user what to do first.\n2. **Discovery** *(skip in a brand-new repo with no `docs/plans/`)* — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md`, `*-progress.md`, and `overview.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; report in-flight topics and any active umbrella, each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`; design-only topics report `design` — no body ingest). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   If the new idea continues an existing topic, ask whether to extend it or start fresh. Part of an umbrella? An existing `overview.md` **beside the design doc** means the split is already decided — read it for the roster and design this part's `<leaf>-design.md` against it (read [references/umbrella.md](references/umbrella.md) before proceeding).\n3. **Understand the idea** — **PRD brief.** When the topic arrives with source material (a PRD, ticket, or spec — pasted text, a file path, or a URL), open with a brief before any question: **Background** (the problem, why now, who is affected — each product claim cites its PRD section), **Current situation** (what the code does today — each claim cites `file:line`), **The delta** (what must change, each line naming a requirement candidate, and what stays untouched). Zero-context rule: plain meaning first, the pointer second — the reader has not read the code; quote non-English domain terms verbatim with a plain-English gloss; mark anything uncited `(interpretation: …)`. Unreadable source material: report the blocker, ground on code only, name the gap in the brief. The human corrects the brief before frontier rounds begin — confirmed facts weave into the design doc, no sidecar file. No source material, no brief. Then read only enough code/docs/commits to ground the design. **Check `docs/lessons.md`** — known constraints may shape it. Ask questions in **frontier rounds**: build a question tree seeded by the dimension checklist, then ask in rounds. The **frontier** is every question whose prerequisites are already settled — ask the whole frontier in one round; a question whose answer depends on another still-open question waits for a later round. Number each question (`Q1`, `Q2`, …) and attach your recommended answer (`➡️ <recommendation>`) — the recommendation is your assumption surfaced up front; the human confirms, strikes, or corrects each in one reply. Recompute the frontier after each round of answers. Seed the tree by walking every checklist dimension — *Goal & scope · Data & state · Behavior & edge cases · Errors & failure · Integration · Non-functional* — printing `— nothing to ask` for groups with no questions (never skip silently). **Facts vs. decisions**: anything answerable from the codebase, docs, or tools is looked up — recon scout or inline — never asked of the human; a pending lookup is an unsettled prerequisite that holds only its downstream questions, while the rest of the frontier is asked now. **Runnable facts**: an unknown observable by running something — behavior, timing, output, layout — is settled by a bounded sketch, never asked of the human and never guessed: an inline interpreter or a file under `docs/plans/<topic>/`, no installs, no source writes (the guard already enforces the boundary); record the settled fact where it lands as `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` and list it in the round summary so the human can strike it; a sketch result that would set business behavior still passes the assumption gate; inconclusive or blocked → record `INCONCLUSIVE` plus one line of what ran, and the question returns to the human with the result attached; a cheaper read beats a run when reading can decide. Only decisions are asked. Major approvals stay single-decision — one question each, never batched: approach selection (step 5), umbrella split, design approval, ADR offer. The interview ends when the frontier is empty — every branch visited, nothing left silently assumed — not when you feel you understand. Then present a short summary and ask: \"Should I proceed, or is there more?\" The human decides when to move on.\n4. **(skipped on trivial changes)** **Codebase recon** — for non-trivial topics with prior art, request the host’s `codebase-recon` capability using the logical `pwk-recon-scout` role. Require a fresh-context, read-only, bounded worker and pass the topic, one-line intent, and repo root. Use the returned 5-section codebase map (Relevant files, Existing patterns, Call sites, Test layout, Gotchas) as the grounding context for the next two steps instead of reading those files inline. The scout is observations only — no design recommendations. Skip this step on trivial changes (typo, version bump, single-function edit per the proportionality rule). If no compatible capability is available or the provider cannot enforce the requested constraints, report `Scout: unavailable` and do the same recon inline, preserving the five-section map and `file:line` citations; do not silently omit recon.\n5. **Explore approaches** — propose 2–3, leading with your recommendation. Sketch the concrete interface (types, signatures, example caller) for each so the comparison is grounded in code, not abstractions.\n6. **Present the design** in one pass, organized into sections (architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing) — the human comments on any section; re-present only revised sections.\n\n   **Assumptions to confirm first** — before presenting, sweep the drafted design: every assumption it would bake in unconfirmed (business rules, defaults, edge-case resolutions) re-opens as a numbered question carrying your recommended answer; the human confirms, strikes, or corrects each in one reply. An honest empty gate (\"no unconfirmed assumptions\") when the draft is clean — never invent items. Hard rule: no business behavior enters the design doc on the agent's assumption. Confirmed facts are woven into the doc's existing sections — no new template section.\n\n   Identified a significant architectural decision? Offer an ADR in `docs/adr/`. Only when all three hold: **hard to reverse**, **surprising without context**, **a real trade-off**. Format: title + 1–3 sentences of context/decision/why. ADRs are permanent institutional memory — they stay out of archive/rotation forever. (Guard note: `docs/adr/` is outside the writable `docs/plans/`; the human writes the approved ADR themselves or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off` — the agent never writes it while the design phase is gated.)\n7. **Write the design doc** — validate its structure before handing off; before writing either a trivial or non-trivial doc, read [references/design-format.md](references/design-format.md) for the exact format, tag defaults, risk/Setup rules, and audit. +{"type":"message","id":"a1bc740b","parentId":"6efd2b95","timestamp":"2026-10-14T10:58:11.187Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_WcUUK1o8fY1Awa1ELCvi8892","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.5 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"==> text 1/8 <==\n=== GIT ===\n---\n3ee03c7 fixture: log-summary script and tests\n---\n/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-run/project\n/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-run/project\n==> text 2/8 <==\n=== PLANS ===\n#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Summarize a JSONL event log: counts per level, plus the time range.\n\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nexport function summarize(text) {\n  const levels = {};\n  const times = [];\n  for (const line of text.split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n    if (!line.trim()) continue;\n    const event = JSON.parse(line);\n    levels[event.level] = (levels[event.level] ?? 0) + 1;\n    if (event.time) times.push(event.time);\n  }\n  times.sort();\n  return { levels, first: times[0] ?? null, last: times[times.length - 1] ?? null };\n}\n\nif (import.meta.url === new URL(`file://${process.argv[1]}`).href) {\n  const [, , file = \"fixtures/events.jsonl\"] = process.argv;\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(summarize(readFileSync(file, \"utf8\")), null, 2));\n}\n==> text 3/8 <==\n=== script ===\nimport assert from \"node:assert/strict\";\nimport { test } from \"node:test\";\nimport { summarize } from \"../scripts/log-summary.mjs\";\n\ntest(\"counts events per level and reports the time range\", () => {\n  const text = [\n    '{\"time\":\"2026-01-02T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\"}',\n    '{\"time\":\"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"error\"}',\n    '{\"time\":\"2026-01-03T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\"}',\n  ].join(\"\\n\");\n  assert.deepEqual(summarize(text), {\n    levels: { info: 2, error: 1 },\n    first: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\n    last: \"2026-01-03T00:00:00Z\",\n  });\n});\n\ntest(\"ignores blank lines\", () => {\n  assert.deepEqual(summarize('\\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"warn\"}\\n'), {\n    levels: { warn: 1 },\n    first: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\n    last: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\n  });\n});\n==> text 4/8 <==\n=== tests ===\n{\n  \"name\": \"pwk-probe-fixture\",\n  \"private\": true,\n  \"version\": \"1.0.0\",\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"scripts\": {\n    \"test\": \"node --test\"\n  }\n}\n==> text 5/8 <==\n=== pkg ===\n# pwk-probe-fixture\n\nA small project with one script and two tests, used as the `--since` fixture task in the\nskill-slimming fidelity/cost probe. No dependencies; `npm test` runs `node --test`.\n==> text 6/8 <==\n=== readme ===\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\",\"msg\":\"started\"}\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:05:00Z\",\"level\":\"warn\",\"msg\":\"slow query\"}\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:06:00Z\",\"level\":\"error\",\"msg\":\"boom\"}\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:07:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\",\"msg\":\"recovered\"}\n==> text 7/8 <==\n=== fixture ===\n==> text 8/8 <==\n=== design-format ===\n# Design format\n\nRead before writing any design doc. Keep the design descriptive, not a task list. It is the single buildable artifact; no separate implementation plan.\n\n## Trivial format\n\nA trivial design has an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach in plain words), a single `### R1:` block with acceptance criteria and tags, and optional `## Production-risk areas`. It has no `## At a glance`, `## Requirements`, or `## Feature acceptance`; its ship gate is the full existing suite, not a manufactured E2E. Use the block rules below for its criteria, tags, and risk notes.\n\n```markdown\n# Design: <topic>\n\nIn short: <what + why + approach>\n\n### R1: <name>\n<observable behavior>\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given <state>, When <action>, Then <observable outcome>.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n```\n\n## Non-trivial format\n\n**Open with `## At a glance`** — the human's two-minute digest, immediately before `## Requirements`. It contains (1) a 2–4 sentence plain-language summary: what is wrong or needed, what will be built, the key approach in plain words; (2) **Key decisions** — one line each: decision + why, with a `(rejected: <alternative> — <reason>)` clause only when the fork was real and load-bearing (never manufactured — no fork, no clause); (3) a table `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |` with exactly one row per requirement, where **R# = the requirement's block number in the `## Requirements` section below** — this ID is what every later digest keys on (progress rows, execution summary, reviewer coverage table). Plain language only: short sentences, no jargon, no Given/When/Then — those live in the requirement blocks for the executor. An umbrella overview gains no at-a-glance section; its roster already serves that role.\n\nThen **`## Requirements`** — one `### R<n>: <name>` block per requirement, each one testable behavior:\n\n```markdown\n## Requirements\n\n### R1: <name>\n<one-line testable behavior — what the feature produces or changes, through its public interface>\n\n**Acceptance criteria** — Given/When/Then criteria defining \"done\". Test observable behavior — what the feature produces or changes through its public interface; not implementation steps. Cover edge and error cases.\n- Given … When … Then …\n- Given … When … Then … (edge case)\n\n### Checkpoints: none | full\n### Review: skip | parallel | inline\n\n### Production-risk notes\n- <only when the requirement touches a risk area>\n\n### R2: <name>\n…\n```\n\nBlock rules:\n\n- **No test-name lists.** The criteria are the test spec — the executor writes and names the actual tests red-green from them, so the doc contains no test-name lists and no R#-to-section mapping tables: the block structure is the map.\n- **Tag every requirement** — `### Checkpoints` (how many human stops: `none` = no per-requirement stop, the default — the feature gate covers it; `full` = tests + complete stops) and `### Review` (per-requirement review: `skip` = none, the default; `parallel` = four delegated reviewers; `inline` = one `pwk-code-review` pass). Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`. Flag `full` only where complex logic or the main part of the feature makes a human look at the slice worth the stop.\n- **Nothing is tagged silently here; only the human tags a slice for review.** A requirement that touches a production-risk area carries its `### Production-risk notes` in the block and is flagged `⚠ production-risk` in the At-a-glance Risk column (the column is derived, **display-only**: `⚠ production-risk` if and only if the block carries non-empty `### Production-risk notes`, else `—` — never normative, never an input; `auto` reads the underlying risk content — the `## Production-risk areas` section and the notes — never the display column), but its written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it — propose the tag in prose, leave the field at `skip`. An explicit human tag always wins, in both directions.\n- **No per-requirement spec stop, by design** — the acceptance criteria are approved right here, at design time; re-checking them mid-execution asks a question the human already answered.\n- **Production-risk notes** — a requirement touching a production-risk area carries its notes inside the block. Risks involving schema migrations, new dependencies, external APIs, or seed data also get a `## Setup` section (dependencies, migrations, seed data, and how to verify setup worked) between `## Requirements` and `## Feature acceptance`.\n- **Ordering** — dependencies come earlier in the list; the executor runs blocks in listed order with no dependency graph. Aim for vertical slices that merge cleanly on their own.\n\nThen the narrative sections the executor reads as context — problem, approaches considered, architecture, components, data flow, error handling. Head the approaches section exactly `## Approaches considered` — finalizing's learning sweep reads it by that name. **`## Approaches considered` records every real fork and why each loser lost** — the executor needs the reasoning, and the finalize learning sweep harvests it for ADRs.\n\nTouches a production-risk area (DB schema/migrations, auth, external APIs, concurrency/batch, uploads/large data flows, Redis/caching/queues)? Add a brief `## Production-risk areas` **immediately after the last requirement block** — inside the `### R1 → ## Feature acceptance` span, so the review packet carries it to reviewers verbatim — and mirror the risks into each touched block's `### Production-risk notes`. `pwk-code-review` audits it, per requirement when the slice is reviewed and at the feature review always; finalize's learning sweep reads it.\n\n**End with `## Feature acceptance`** — one or more end-to-end `Given/When/Then` scenarios proving the requirements *compose* into the feature. This is the feature's definition-of-done; the human approves it as what \"the feature works\" means. `pwk-executing-tasks` writes it as the E2E test first and runs it as the **primary enforced spec** (the test it gates on first). The section carries the feature-level `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline` tag — the one whole-feature review; default `auto`, which resolves on the design's own production-risk content to `parallel` (all four reviewers) when the design has any — a non-empty `## Production-risk areas` section, or a non-empty `### Production-risk notes` on any requirement — and to `inline` (one pass) otherwise. An explicit `parallel` or `inline` is written as-is, never resolved, so the human always overrides `auto`. Treat \"I can write this scenario\" as the green light to finish designing — if you can't, keep designing because the requirements don't yet compose into a coherent feature. If writing a scenario step would require inventing behavior, that invention goes back through the assumption gate — it may never be silently written into the scenario; an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement, so keep designing.\n\n```markdown\n## Feature acceptance\n\n- Given <starting state>, When <trigger>, Then <end-to-end outcome the feature promises>.\n\n### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline — the one whole-feature review; leave `auto` unless the human says otherwise.\n```\n\nExample (rate limiting): \"Given a new API consumer with no prior usage, When they exceed 100 requests/minute for 3 consecutive minutes, Then they're throttled, a `rate_limited` event is emitted, and further requests return 429.\"\n\n**Audit before finishing:** every requirement block has acceptance criteria and both tags, and each requirement appears **exactly once** — none dropped, none duplicated. A `## Feature acceptance` section exists as the primary enforced spec — on every non-trivial doc; a trivial doc ends after its `### R1:` block and ships on the full suite instead. Production-risk areas are reflected in the requirement blocks that touch them. The CLI's self-invocation block (`scripts/log-summary.mjs:19-22`)\ncatches it, writes a one-line diagnostic to stderr, and exits 1 with nothing on stdout, so a\npiped consumer never sees a half-valid summary.\n\n## Feature acceptance\n\n- Given the fixture log with events from 09:00 to 09:07, When `node scripts/log-summary.mjs --since 2026-01-04T09:06:00Z fixtures/events.jsonl` runs, Then it exits 0 and stdout is the summary of only the 09:06 and 09:07 events (`levels` of one `error` and one `info`, `first` = `2026-01-04T09:06:00Z`, `last` = `2026-01-04T09:07:00Z`).\n- Given the same log, When run with a cutoff after every event, Then it exits 0, `levels` is empty, and `first` and `last` are `null`.\n- Given the same log, When run with `--since not-a-date`, Then it exits 1, stderr names the invalid value, and stdout stays empty.\n\n### Feature review: auto\n"},"durationMs":89},{"id":"call_00_nHTRg4MeZZf8EdBq7KzG4802/2","name":"bash","status":"ok","arguments":{"command":"python3 \"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/scripts/validate-design.py\" \"docs/plans/2026-10-14-log-summary-since/log-summary-since-design.md\"; echo \"exit=$?\""},"durationMs":648}],"complete":true}}}
