Keep the design descriptive, not a task list. It is the single buildable artifact; no separate implementation plan.\n\n## Trivial format\n\nA trivial design has an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach in plain words), a single `### R1:` block with acceptance criteria and tags, and optional `## Production-risk areas`. It has no `## At a glance`, `## Requirements`, or `## Feature acceptance`; its ship gate is the full existing suite, not a manufactured E2E. Use the block rules below for its criteria, tags, and risk notes.\n\n```markdown\n# Design: <topic>\n\nIn short: <what + why + approach>\n\n### R1: <name>\n<observable behavior>\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given <state>, When <action>, Then <observable outcome>.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n```\n\n## Non-trivial format\n\n**Open with `## At a glance`** — the human's two-minute digest, immediately before `## Requirements`. It contains (1) a 2–4 sentence plain-language summary: what is wrong or needed, what will be built, the key approach in plain words; (2) **Key decisions** — one line each: decision + why, with a `(rejected: <alternative> — <reason>)` clause only when the fork was real and load-bearing (never manufactured — no fork, no clause); (3) a table `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |` with exactly one row per requirement, where **R# = the requirement's block number in the `## Requirements` section below** — this ID is what every later digest keys on (progress rows, execution summary, reviewer coverage table). Plain language only: short sentences, no jargon, no Given/When/Then — those live in the requirement blocks for the executor. An umbrella overview gains no at-a-glance section; its roster already serves that role.\n\nThen **`## Requirements`** — one `### R<n>: <name>` block per requirement, each one testable behavior:\n\n```markdown\n## Requirements\n\n### R1: <name>\n<one-line testable behavior — what the feature produces or changes, through its public interface>\n\n**Acceptance criteria** — Given/When/Then criteria defining \"done\". Test observable behavior — what the feature produces or changes through its public interface; not implementation steps. Cover edge and error cases.\n- Given … When … Then …\n- Given … When … Then … (edge case)\n\n### Checkpoints: none | full\n### Review: skip | parallel | inline\n\n### Production-risk notes\n- <only when the requirement touches a risk area>\n\n### R2: <name>\n…\n```\n\nBlock rules:\n\n- **No test-name lists.** The criteria are the test spec — the executor writes and names the actual tests red-green from them, so the doc contains no test-name lists and no R#-to-section mapping tables: the block structure is the map.\n- **Tag every requirement** — `### Checkpoints` (how many human stops: `none` = no per-requirement stop, the default — the feature gate covers it; `full` = tests + complete stops) and `### Review` (per-requirement review: `skip` = none, the default; `parallel` = four delegated reviewers; `inline` = one `pwk-code-review` pass). Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`. Flag `full` only where complex logic or the main part of the feature makes a human look at the slice worth the stop.\n- **Nothing is tagged silently here; only the human tags a slice for review.** A requirement that touches a production-risk area carries its `### Production-risk notes` in the block and is flagged `⚠ production-risk` in the At-a-glance Risk column (the column is derived, **display-only**: `⚠ production-risk` if and only if the block carries non-empty `### Production-risk notes`, else `—` — never normative, never an input; `auto` reads the underlying risk content — the `## Production-risk areas` section and the notes — never the display column), but its written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it — propose the tag in prose, leave the field at `skip`. An explicit human tag always wins, in both directions.\n- **No per-requirement spec stop, by design** — the acceptance criteria are approved right here, at design time; re-checking them mid-execution asks a question the human already answered.\n- **Production-risk notes** — a requirement touching a production-risk area carries its notes inside the block. Risks involving schema migrations, new dependencies, external APIs, or seed data also get a `## Setup` section (dependencies, migrations, seed data, and how to verify setup worked) between `## Requirements` and `## Feature acceptance`.\n- **Ordering** — dependencies come earlier in the list; the executor runs blocks in listed order with no dependency graph. Aim for vertical slices that merge cleanly on their own.\n\nThen the narrative sections the executor reads as context — problem, approaches considered, architecture, components, data flow, error handling. Head the approaches section exactly `## Approaches considered` — finalizing's learning sweep reads it by that name. **`## Approaches considered` records every real fork and why each loser lost** — the executor needs the reasoning, and the finalize learning sweep harvests it for ADRs.\n\nTouches a production-risk area (DB schema/migrations, auth, external APIs, concurrency/batch, uploads/large data flows, Redis/caching/queues)? Add a brief `## Production-risk areas` **immediately after the last requirement block** — inside the `### R1 → ## Feature acceptance` span, so the review packet carries it to reviewers verbatim — and mirror the risks into each touched block's `### Production-risk notes`. `pwk-code-review` audits it, per requirement when the slice is reviewed and at the feature review always; finalize's learning sweep reads it.\n\n**End with `## Feature acceptance`** — one or more end-to-end `Given/When/Then` scenarios proving the requirements *compose* into the feature. This is the feature's definition-of-done; the human approves it as what \"the feature works\" means. `pwk-executing-tasks` writes it as the E2E test first and runs it as the **primary enforced spec** (the test it gates on first). The section carries the feature-level `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline` tag — the one whole-feature review; default `auto`, which resolves on the design's own production-risk content to `parallel` (all four reviewers) when the design has any — a non-empty `## Production-risk areas` section, or a non-empty `### Production-risk notes` on any requirement — and to `inline` (one pass) otherwise. An explicit `parallel` or `inline` is written as-is, never resolved, so the human always overrides `auto`. Treat \"I can write this scenario\" as the green light to finish designing — if you can't, keep designing because the requirements don't yet compose into a coherent feature. If writing a scenario step would require inventing behavior, that invention goes back through the assumption gate — it may never be silently written into the scenario; an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement, so keep designing.\n\n```markdown\n## Feature acceptance\n\n- Given <starting state>, When <trigger>, Then <end-to-end outcome the feature promises>.\n\n### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline — the one whole-feature review; leave `auto` unless the human says otherwise.\n```\n\nExample (rate limiting): \"Given a new API consumer with no prior usage, When they exceed 100 requests/minute for 3 consecutive minutes, Then they're throttled, a `rate_limited` event is emitted, and further requests return 429.\"\n\n**Audit before finishing:** every requirement block has acceptance criteria and both tags, and each requirement appears **exactly once** — none dropped, none duplicated. A `## Feature acceptance` section exists as the primary enforced spec — on every non-trivial doc; a trivial doc ends after its `### R1:` block and ships on the full suite instead. Production-risk areas are reflected in the requirement blocks that touch them. The probe test: a criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; a criterion with no nameable probe sends the requirement back for splitting or rephrasing; criteria never name tests — the probe materializes at execution. A fact settled by a sketch carries its proof where it lands — `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` — woven into the section it confirms, never a new template section.\n\n## Structural validator contract\n\nRun `scripts/validate-design.py` as directed in the main skill. It reads UTF-8 Markdown without modifying it. Headings, tags, and labels inside backtick or tilde fenced examples do not count; close every fence. Real requirements use unique sequential `### R1: <name>`, `### R2: <name>`, … headings with nonempty names. Each block needs a standalone `**Acceptance criteria**` label in its main body, before any tag or risk-note heading (an explanatory suffix after an em dash, dash, or colon is allowed) and nonempty criteria before the next heading or bold section label. A bare bullet or content borrowed from risk notes is not a criterion section.\n\nWrite each selected tag as one value, not the template's pipe-separated alternatives. Missing optional tags retain `Checkpoints: none`, `Review: skip`, and `Feature review: auto`. Non-trivial designs require nonempty `## Feature acceptance` scenarios before their feature-review tag. Only the minimal trivial shape above receives the no-Feature-acceptance exception.\n\nThe helper checks structure, not meaning: it does not prove Given/When/Then quality, testability, complete edge/error coverage, good slicing, risk classification, confirmed assumptions, or human approval. Those remain the agent's audit and the human's judgment. Structural success does not complete the design gate by itself.\n\n\n=== validate-design.py ===\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Read-only validation of the workflow's Markdown design structure (Python 3.9+).\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom typing import List, Optional, Tuple\n\n\nTAG_VALUES = {\n    \"Checkpoints\": (\"none\", \"full\"),\n    \"Review\": (\"skip\", \"parallel\", \"inline\"),\n    \"Feature review\": (\"auto\", \"parallel\", \"inline\"),\n}\nHEADING = re.compile(r\"^ {0,3}(#{1,6})[ \\t]+(.+?)\\s*#*\\s*$\")\nREQUIREMENT = re.compile(r\"^R([1-9][0-9]*):\\s*(.*)$\")\nREQUIREMENT_LIKE = re.compile(r\"^R(?:[0-9]|\\s*:)\")\nCRITERIA = re.compile(r\"^\\*\\*Acceptance criteria\\*\\*(?:\\s*(?:—|–|-|:).*)?$\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Heading:\n    level: int\n    title: str\n    index: int\n\n\ndef visible_lines(text: str) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Blank fenced examples, retaining indexes for diagnostics. Not a Markdown renderer.\"\"\"\n    lines = []\n    errors = []\n    fence = \"\"\n    fence_line = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):\n        if fence:\n            if re.fullmatch(r\" {0,3}\" + re.escape(fence[0]) + \"{\" + str(len(fence)) + r\",}[ \\t]*\", line):\n                fence = \"\"\n            lines.append(\"\")\n            continue\n        opening = re.match(r\"^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$\", line)\n        if opening and not (opening[1][0] == \"`\" and \"`\" in opening[2]):\n            fence = opening[1]\n            fence_line = number\n            lines.append(\"\")\n        else:\n            lines.append(line)\n    if fence:\n        errors.append(f\"line {fence_line}: unclosed code fence; close it before validating\")\n    return lines, errors\n\n\ndef has_content(lines: List[str]) -> bool:\n    # Check presence, not whether the assertion is true, testable, or sufficiently specific.\n    for line in lines:\n        text = re.sub(r\"^\\s*(?:[-+*]|[0-9]+[.)])\\s*\", \"\", line).strip()\n        if text and re.search(r\"\\w\", text):\n            return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef criteria_body(lines: List[str], start: int, end: int) -> List[str]:\n    \"\"\"A heading or another bold section label terminates criteria, not just the next R ID.\"\"\"\n    result = []\n    for line in lines[start:end]:\n        if HEADING.match(line) or re.match(r\"^\\s*\\*\\*[^*]+\\*\\*\", line):\n            break\n        result.append(line)\n    return result\n\n\ndef validate(text: str) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str]]:\n    lines, errors = visible_lines(text)\n    headings = []\n    for index, line in enumerate(lines):\n        match = HEADING.match(line)\n        if match:\n            headings.append(Heading(len(match[1]), match[2], index))\n    for heading in headings:\n        if REQUIREMENT_LIKE.match(heading.title) and heading.level != 3:\n            errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: {heading.title} must use a ### requirement heading\")\n    requirements = [h for h in headings if h.level == 3 and REQUIREMENT_LIKE.match(h.title)]\n    features = [h for h in headings if h.level == 2 and h.title == \"Feature acceptance\"]\n    summaries = []\n\n    if not requirements:\n        errors.append(\"required requirement block missing; add ### R1: <name> with Acceptance criteria\")\n    seen = set()\n    for expected, heading in enumerate(requirements, 1):\n        match = REQUIREMENT.fullmatch(heading.title)\n        if not match:\n            errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: malformed requirement '{heading.title}'; use ### R{expected}: <name>\")\n            continue\n        number = int(match[1])\n        if number in seen:\n            errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: duplicate requirement R{number}\")\n        elif number != expected:\n            errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: expected R{expected}, found R{number}; IDs must be sequential in document order\")\n        seen.add(number)\n        if not match[2].strip():\n            errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: R{number} requires a nonempty name\")\n\n    intro_end = requirements[0].index if requirements else len(lines)\n    short = any(re.match(r\"^In short:\\s*\\S.*$\", line) for line in lines[:intro_end])\n    full_format = any(h.level == 2 and h.title in (\"At a glance\", \"Requirements\") for h in headings)\n    trivial = short and not full_format and len(requirements) == 1 and requirements[0].title.startswith(\"R1:\") and not features\n    if not trivial and not features:\n        errors.append(\"## Feature acceptance is required for non-trivial designs; the trivial exception needs an In short: one-liner and a single R1 block without full-format sections\")\n    if len(features) > 1:\n        errors.append(\"duplicate ## Feature acceptance section; keep exactly one\")\n\n    # Record ownership so a valid-looking tag cannot silently land outside its section.\n    owned_tags = set()\n\n    def tags(start: int, end: int, names: Tuple[str, ...], owner: str) -> dict:\n        values = {name: TAG_VALUES[name][0] for name in names}\n        found = set()\n        for heading in headings:\n            if not start <= heading.index < end:\n                continue\n            for name in names:\n                if heading.level != 3 or not re.match(re.escape(name) + r\"\\b\", heading.title):\n                    continue\n                owned_tags.add(heading.index)\n                if name in found:\n                    errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: duplicate {name} tag in {owner}\")\n                found.add(name)\n                value = heading.title[len(name):].strip()\n                value = value[1:].strip() if value.startswith(\":\") else \"\"\n                if value not in TAG_VALUES[name]:\n                    allowed = \" | \".join(TAG_VALUES[name])\n                    errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: invalid {name} tag in {owner}; expected {allowed}\")\n                else:\n                    values[name] = value\n        return values\n\n    for heading in requirements:\n        end = next((h.index for h in headings if h.index > heading.index and (h.level <= 2 or h in requirements)), len(lines))\n        criteria_end = next((h.index for h in headings if heading.index < h.index < end), end)\n        labels = [i for i in range(heading.index + 1, criteria_end) if CRITERIA.fullmatch(lines[i].strip())]\n        owner = heading.title.split(\":\", 1)[0]\n        if not labels:\n            errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: {owner} needs a standalone **Acceptance criteria** section\")\n        elif len(labels) > 1:\n            errors.append(f\"line {labels[1] + 1}: {owner} has duplicate Acceptance criteria sections\")\n        elif not has_content(criteria_body(lines, labels[0] + 1, end)):\n            errors.append(f\"line {labels[0] + 1}: {owner} Acceptance criteria is empty; add an end-to-end criterion before its review tag\")\n        values = tags(heading.index + 1, end, (\"Feature review\",), \"Feature acceptance\")\n        summaries.append(f\"Feature review={values['Feature review']}\")\n\n    for heading in headings:\n        for name in TAG_VALUES:\n            if re.match(re.escape(name) + r\"\\b\", heading.title) and heading.index not in owned_tags:\n                owner = \"## Feature acceptance\" if name == \"Feature review\" else \"a ### R<n>: requirement block\"\n                errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: {name} must be a ### tag inside {owner}\")\n    return errors, summaries\n\n\ndef main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=\"Read-only structural design validation. +{"type":"message","id":"27f0cb21","parentId":"e440095f","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:13:28.481Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<skill name=\"pwk-executing-tasks\" location=\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks/SKILL.md\">\nReferences are relative to /Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks.\n\n# Executing Tasks\n\nImplement the design doc found under `docs/plans/` via the **feature-gate flow**. The design doc is the single buildable artifact — its `### R<n>` blocks carry each requirement's acceptance criteria and tags. The criteria define *what*, you decide *how*: structure, signatures, internals are yours.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\nThe feature-acceptance E2E test is the primary enforced gate and the primary enforced spec for the feature. The flow is always on: write the E2E first (red), implement the requirements back-to-back, then run the feature review and pause at the **ship checkpoint** — one fully-informed stop where you present the execution summary and the reviewer coverage table, with the full diff on request. Per-requirement checkpoints and reviews are **opt-in** — they fire only for requirements the design doc tags (default off); the feature gate covers everything else. A trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`, per brainstorming's proportionality rule) skips the E2E steps and ships on the full suite; the one whole-feature review still runs at its ship checkpoint, its missing `### Feature review` tag defaulting to `auto`.\n\n## Before you start\n\nResolve local references and scripts from this installed skill directory. If a required resource is missing, report the blocker and stop before the affected action; do not silently skip its instructions.\n\n1. **Git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`; note uncommitted changes.\n2. **Find the doc** — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; take each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   If no doc at all, ask the user to run `/skill:pwk-brainstorming` first; if several, ask which. Report one line, e.g. `Found: design \"auth\" — feature-gate execute (E2E written, implementing 2/5)`. A matching `*-progress.md` means this is a **resume** (see [Resume and progress](#resume-and-progress)). An umbrella part whose prior leaves are not all at `done`: surface their `Feature phase:` lines (matched header-only from each `<leaf>-progress.md`) as advisory context in the pre-flight report — no refusal, no reorder; build order stays advisory.\n3. **Workspace — choose this topic’s branch/worktree.** Before creating, switching, or adopting one, read [Workspace and resume details](references/resume.md#workspace). Reuse this topic’s branch (one umbrella = one branch); a different topic’s branch never hosts these commits. Uncommitted planning docs do not cross a worktree boundary: commit this topic folder on its branch before a new worktree handoff; when adopting an existing checkout with uncommitted docs here, copy the topic folder there, verify it, then remove the source copy. Read the reference's command order before acting. Offer/adopt only after checking existing worktrees; wait for the user's choice.\n\n## First run\n\n1. **Parse the design doc** — read every `### R<n>:` heading and its `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags (defaults `none` / `skip`), plus the feature-level `### Feature review` tag in the `## Feature acceptance` section. Requirements run in **listed order** (build order); do not reorder. Read the `## Feature acceptance` section — it is the E2E you gate on first. A trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`) skips steps 5–6 below and goes straight into the implement phase.\n2. **Create the progress file** beside the design at `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md`. Before creating it, read [Progress format](references/progress-format.md) for the exact template, header slots, and row vocabulary. Start at `Feature phase: e2e-written` (trivial doc: `implementing (0/N)`); `Setup: pending` when the design has `## Setup`, otherwise `Setup: n/a`.\n\n3. **Setup pre-flight** *(only if the design doc has a `## Setup` section)* — install dependencies, apply migrations, seed data, then run the existing test suite. **⏸ CHECKPOINT: setup** — present results and wait for approval, then set `Setup: done` in the progress-file header so a resume can confirm it rather than assume it.\n\n4. **Commit the design docs** — `git add docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ && git commit -m \"docs: add design doc\"`. The add is scoped to the topic folder so another in-flight topic's uncommitted drafts never ride this commit (docs/lessons.md hygiene: one commit per topic).\n5. **Write the feature-acceptance E2E test (red).** Read the design doc's `## Feature acceptance` section and encode it as a real test file; run it; confirm it **fails** (it must — little or none of the feature exists yet). If it passes immediately, probe why before proceeding: the behavior may already exist, or the test may be asserting too little. If it still passes and the expected behavior looks wrong, **stop and present** rather than implementing against a wrong spec. Iterate it to green as you implement — fixing the implementation is the default, and you **stop and present only when you are genuinely blocked** (nothing you can do makes it pass, or the E2E itself is wrong). That stop is the reserved failure case; it is not the flow's default pause.\n6. **Notice, not a stop — report the E2E and continue.** Post 1–2 plain-language lines stating **what the E2E proves** (\"this test proves that …\"), plus the E2E test and its failing output, then go straight into the implement phase **without waiting for approval** — the `## Feature acceptance` text was approved during brainstorm, so there is nothing new here for the human to sign off. The notice is the window to object *before* implementation starts: a human who sees the E2E asserting the wrong thing says so, and you revise, re-run, and re-notice. Keep `Feature phase: e2e-written`.\n\n## Resume and progress\n\n`Feature phase` is one of: `e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`.\n\n**Done cell:** `⬜` not started · `🔄` in progress · `✅` done · `❌` failed · `⏭` skipped. A row is **terminal** when its Done cell is `✅`, `❌`, or `⏭` — resolved, not necessarily passed. Only executing changes Done cells; a requirement under review stays `🔄` until a clean pass permits `✅`.\n\nWhen a matching progress file exists, read [Resume](references/resume.md#resume) before routing. Read the header, Requirements table, and Execution summary only; `ship-paused` also needs Code digest. A pending setup checkpoint must be re-verified and approved before proceeding. Resume the first nonterminal row (`⬜`, `🔄`, blank); `✅`/`❌`/`⏭` are terminal, resolved rather than necessarily passed. Match `grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>` for the phase header; `reviewing` resumes review; `ship-paused` re-presents and waits, never approves itself. Missing reviewer reports require review again before showing coverage.\n\nBefore any progress-row update or code-digest write, read [Progress format](references/progress-format.md). Update the matching row directly, `Last updated`, and `Feature phase`; write execution-summary content at the same time as ✅, and deviations at deviation time. A failed/skipped row carries its reason in the Requirement cell and reconciles its test coverage so the suite stays green.\n\n## Implement phase\n\nBugs found mid-execution are mandatory execution-summary content: record the fix in the requirement's `How it was built` cell and fill its Deviated? column at fix time — the summary must show what the feature actually cost to land.\n\nSet `Feature phase: implementing (0/N)` and work the requirements in listed order. For each:\n\n1. **Mark the requirement 🔄** (Done column), read its `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags, and check `docs/lessons.md` for a rule that applies to this slice.\n2. **Write a meaningful test (red), then implement (green)** — TDD discipline. Encode the requirement's acceptance criteria as a real test through the public interface; run it; confirm it fails; implement to green. Skip the per-slice test only when the slice has no independent observable behavior (the feature E2E covers it). Follow the meaningful-test rules: (1) **Test observable behavior** — assert on what the feature produces or changes (a return value, persisted/updated data, an emitted event, an HTTP response) through its public interface; these assertions keep passing as the implementation changes. (2) **Write a per-slice test when the slice has its own observable behavior** — when a slice is pure config or a trivial extraction, the feature E2E covers it and a per-slice test is unnecessary. (Mirrored in `pwk-brainstorming` and `docs/lessons.md`.)\n3. **⏸ per-requirement checkpoint** *(fires only when the tag says so — opt-in)* — if `### Checkpoints: full`, stop and present after the tests and again after the slice is complete — both before its commit (the checkpoint rule below forbids committing before approval). With the default `none`, show the red→green inline and proceed.\n4. **Regression check after each commit** — run the **full existing suite**. This is what catches cross-requirement regressions (a later requirement breaking an earlier one's test). The **feature E2E stays red until the last requirement lands**; you may run it to watch the failure point advance, but it is gated only at the ship checkpoint — never expect it green per-commit.\n5. **Learn.** Caught a repeat mistake? Append a **generic** rule to `docs/lessons.md` (strip domain specifics).\n6. **Commit** the requirement with a clear message; record the requirement's commit hash in the Commit column.\n7. **Per-requirement review** *(fires only when the requirement's `### Review` tag is `parallel` or `inline` — default `skip`)* — review the slice now (see [Per-requirement review](#per-requirement-review-opt-in)); the row stays 🔄 through the review.\n8. **Mark the requirement ✅** and write its execution-summary row in the same step — Evidence cell non-empty, plain words plus pointer; advance `Feature phase: implementing (k/N)`. For a reviewed requirement this fires only after the review returns clean.\n\n### Per-requirement review (opt-in)\n\nIf the requirement's `### Review` tag is `parallel` or `inline` (default `skip`), review that slice at step 7 — read [Review mechanics](references/review.md) first and use its helper with `--scope requirement --requirement N`, limited to the commits and criteria of that requirement, written to `<design doc's directory>/<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md` (requirement-suffixed, so per-requirement packets never overwrite the feature packet or each other). The row stays 🔄 through the review: the four delegated roles — or the one `pwk-code-review` pass on `inline` — report findings, you apply the smell fixes yourself and commit them (the roles are read-only reporters), and a clean pass returns to step 8, which marks the row ✅. With `skip`, no per-requirement review — step 8 fires directly, and the feature-level review covers it.\n\nWith the default `none`, no per-requirement stop fires — the per-requirement test still runs red→green, and the feature review covers implementation quality.\n\n### Checkpoint gates are mandatory (when the tag says so)\n\nWhen a per-requirement checkpoint fires it is a **hard stop**:\n- Stop immediately; never proceed without explicit human approval.\n- **Never** `git add` or `git commit` before approval at a checkpoint.\n- Set the progress phase/status **before** pausing.\n\n## Ship checkpoint (all requirements terminal + review, merged)\n\nWhen every requirement's Done cell is terminal — `✅` (done), `❌` (failed, reason in row), or `⏭` (skipped, reason in row):\n\n1. **Run the FULL test suite** — a failure means one requirement regressed another; fix it now, in execute context.\n2. **Run the feature-acceptance E2E** — the test you wrote at the start. It must be **green** now that all requirements have landed. (A `❌`/`⏭` requirement's assertions were reconciled when its row went terminal, so a still-red E2E still means a requirement is missing or wrong.) If it is still red, a requirement is missing or wrong — fix it before proceeding. (A trivial design doc has no `## Feature acceptance` — the full suite staying green is its gate instead.)\n3. **Run the feature review** (below) per the design's `### Feature review` tag — set `Feature phase: reviewing` first, so a mid-review resume routes into this step instead of the implement loop. (A trivial design doc carries no `### Feature review` tag — the missing tag defaults to `auto`, which resolves on its risk content; a trivial diff is typically `inline`, one pass, and there is no E2E to re-green — the full suite is the gate.) The review runs **before** your final approval, so the pause is fully informed. Apply smell fixes yourself and re-green (full suite + E2E) before pausing.\n4. **Write the code digest** into the progress file — the review has succeeded, findings are fixed, and the code is final: read the packet's `## Commits`, `## Changed files`, and `## Diff` sections and fill the progress file's `## Code digest` using [Progress format](references/progress-format.md) and its fill rules. If the packet is stale or missing, read [Review mechanics](references/review.md) and re-run the helper before writing. A resumed `Feature phase: reviewing` that completes lands on this same write point before the checkpoint is assembled. Never a gate: it explains the change, it does not block shipping.\n\n   **Reconcile the Flow against reviewed reality before writing it.** The Flow is written from what was reviewed, not from recollection: in `parallel` mode every hop must correspond to a path the tracing reviewer's report names — no hop invented, no reported path dropped. In `inline` mode there is no separate tracing report — the inline pass itself performs code tracing — so check the Flow against that pass's tracing findings and spec-coverage result instead. A discrepancy you cannot resolve is **surfaced** to the human in the ship checkpoint's findings status, never smoothed over by writing a Flow that omits the path.\n5. **Set `Feature phase: ship-paused`** and **⏸ CHECKPOINT: ship** — present, in this order:\n   - a green-gates line: full suite green, feature E2E green (trivial doc: the suite line alone — there is no E2E);\n   - the **execution summary** — what each requirement became, deviations included, Evidence cells quoted so the human reads evidence rather than claims;\n   - the **verdict rows** — list every `❌`/`⏭` row with its reason, so the approval is given knowing what failed;\n   - the **code digest** — the plain-language change explanation from the progress file (summary, flow, gotchas, key files);\n   - the **coverage table** (one verdict row per R#) — from the spec-reviewer report in `parallel` mode, from the inline pass's spec alignment in `inline` mode;\n   - findings status: fixed / open for the human;\n   - \"full diff on request\" — the raw diff is one command away; show a hunk only where a verdict or finding makes the human ask.\n\n   Wait for approval. **request changes** → fix, re-run the gates (and the review if the change is substantive), re-present.\n\nA spec-reviewer report without a per-requirement coverage table is invalid — retry the role or complete it inline before pausing; the ship checkpoint is never presented without coverage. (Only the spec role owes the table; the tracing/smell/hazard reports keep their own report shapes.)\n\nThe old \"integration gate\" is gone — the feature E2E at the ship checkpoint *is* the gate; there is no separate end pass.\n\n## Feature review\n\nThis is step 3 of the [ship checkpoint](#ship-checkpoint-all-requirements-terminal--review-merged): it runs **before** the final human approval, so the pause is fully informed. Run **one** review over the **whole feature diff**, driven by the design doc's `### Feature review` tag — exactly one per part, never once per requirement. This is the single thorough review — per-requirement reviews, if any, only saw slices in isolation.\n\n**Assemble the review packet first** — read [Review mechanics](references/review.md), then invoke the installed skill’s `scripts/build-review-packet.py` with explicit `--project`, `--design`, `--progress`, and `--scope feature`. Check `python3 --version` for Python 3.9+ and helper availability before this step; if Python is missing or unavailable, report the blocker, request a suitable runtime, and stop. Do not auto-install a runtime, use a fallback implementation, or claim packet generation succeeded. No packet byte passes through model output. A failed helper is not usable evidence or approval; correct the inputs, never guess ranges. The helper writes `<leaf>-review-packet.md` beside the design; opt-in packets use `<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`.\n\n- **Resolve the tag first.** `auto` (the default, and what a missing tag means) resolves on the design's own production-risk content: if the design carries a non-empty `## Production-risk areas` section, or any requirement carries a non-empty `### Production-risk notes`, resolve to `parallel`; otherwise resolve to `inline`. An explicit `parallel` or `inline` is used as written and always wins over `auto` — explicit tag wins in both directions, so a human who wants one pass on a risky design gets one pass.\n\n- **`parallel`** — use the host’s `parallel-review` capability for four independent, fresh-context, read-only roles: `pwk-spec-reviewer`, `pwk-tracing-reviewer`, `pwk-smell-reviewer`, `pwk-hazard-reviewer`. Follow [Review mechanics](references/review.md#delegate-or-review-inline): a one-liner packet-file pointer with role framing last; the packet never appears in spawn arguments. Collect one outcome per role. Reviewers only report; you apply smell fixes, commit, and re-green full suite + E2E. Surface trace/spec/hazard findings to the human.\n- **`inline`** — perform `/skill:pwk-code-review` over the whole diff as a single pass.\n- **Fallback** — if compatible capability is absent, required read-only/fresh-context/bounded constraints cannot be proved, or delegation fails, do the missing work inline. Retain successful reports; required missing roles mean review is incomplete.\n- **Refresh** — if commits land during review, use [Review mechanics](references/review.md) to refresh the packet before any replacement role or digest write. Append requirement-fix IDs before a requirement refresh; keep the initial ID. Packet creation never substitutes for review or approval.\n\nOn success, continue assembling the ship checkpoint; once the human approves it — knowing what failed — set `Feature phase: done`. (An umbrella part's gate is its own progress file; `pwk-finalizing` reads every part's file, and a `❌` in any part blocks the umbrella until the human sends the work back or explicitly types `--force-failed`.)\n\n## Tags reference\n\nThe design doc tags each requirement and the feature level:\n\n| Tag | Values | Default | Fires |\n|-----|--------|---------|-------|\n| `### Checkpoints` | `none \\| full` | `none` | per-requirement human stops — `full` = tests + complete stops |\n| `### Review` | `skip \\| parallel \\| inline` | `skip` | per-requirement review — `parallel` = four delegated reviewers; `inline` = one `pwk-code-review` pass |\n| `### Feature review` | `auto \\| parallel \\| inline` | `auto` | the one whole-feature review — always run, never per requirement (a trivial doc carries no tag; the missing tag resolves to `auto`) |\n\nNothing is tagged silently: **only the human tags** a slice, and the feature review covers everything else. How each tag resolves lives where its decision executes — the [per-requirement review](#per-requirement-review-opt-in) and the [feature review](#feature-review).\n\n## User override commands\n\n| User says | Agent does |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| `skip` | Set its Done cell `⏭` (with the reason), reconcile its test coverage, move to next |\n| `status` | Show the progress file (feature phase + requirement table) |\n| `stop` | Restore current requirement to its pre-in-progress state, suggest `/new` |\n| `retry` | Re-read the requirement, start over |\n\n## Receiving feedback (outside a checkpoint)\n\nVerify the criticism against the code, evaluate the suggestion, then implement (with tests) or push back with evidence. Don't blindly apply.\n\n## After the feature review\n\nThe feature is implemented, reviewed, and approved at the ship checkpoint. Determine the next step from the artifacts (the human drives every transition — this is a suggestion, not a gate; the overview check below is **folder-local** — read the `overview.md` beside this leaf, inside the same `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` directory, never a repo-wide `docs/plans/**/overview.md`, and always excluding docs/plans/completed/, so an archived or sibling umbrella never routes):\n\n- **Standalone topic** (no `overview.md` in the topic folder) → suggest `/skill:pwk-finalizing`.\n- **Umbrella part** (an `overview.md` sits beside this leaf) → read the overview's `## Parts (build order)` roster. The umbrella is complete when every roster leaf has a `done` progress file → suggest `/skill:pwk-finalizing` (one PR for the whole umbrella). Otherwise look at the **next leaf** — the **first roster part with no `done` progress file**, not the next entry in build order: build order is advisory, so a part built out of order must not be skipped by the suggestion. That leaf with no progress file and no `<leaf>-design.md` is unstarted → suggest `/skill:pwk-brainstorming` for it; with a `<leaf>-design.md` but no progress file it is designed but never executed → suggest `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` (its pre-flight picks the design doc up — the same state pwk-status renders as `design`); with a progress file that is not `done` it is mid-flight → suggest `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` to resume that leaf instead.\n\nPresent:\n\n```\n✅ Feature complete — feature gates green, feature review done!\n\nFeature phase: done\n| # | Done | Requirement |\n|---|------|-------------|\n| 1 | ✅ | <name> |\n| … | … | … |\n\n   - Next part: /skill:pwk-brainstorming (unstarted leaf) or /skill:pwk-executing-tasks (designed or mid-flight) — per the routing above   ← umbrella, more parts remain\n   - Ship: /skill:pwk-finalizing                          ← standalone, or last umbrella part\n```\n\n## If you're stuck\n\n1. Re-read the requirement's acceptance criteria — you may have drifted.\n2. Check `git log` for context. Ask the user — clarify beats guessing.\n3. Still stuck → discard uncommitted changes (`git restore .`); if already committed, also `git revert` the requirement's commit(s). **Never leave a failed requirement's partial work on the shipped branch.**\n4. Set its Done cell `❌` (with the reason as a suffix in the Requirement cell), reconcile its test coverage, and move on. Check `docs/lessons.md` — a prior lesson may apply.\n\n## Contract index\n\nDetailed progress, resume, and review contracts live in `references/`. The following\nentrypoint markers remain canonical: `Feature phase` is one of\n`e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`; Done cells use\n`⬜`, `🔄`, `✅`, `❌`, `⏭`, where `✅`/`❌`/`⏭` are resolved. Only executing changes\nDone cells; a reviewed row flips only `🔄`→`✅`. `Setup: pending | done | n/a` is the\nheader slot, and the ceremony cell echoes the design doc's tag. Execution summary rows\nare written in the same step as marking a requirement ✅, with deviations recorded when\nthe departure happens. Resume uses `re-run the setup verification`; packet bounds use\nthe `Commit column`, the `parent of the first recorded commit`, and the `previous\nrequirement's last commit`. Successful delegated reports are retained. The Flow has\n`Spine`, `Branches`, `Side effects`, `was:`, and no line numbers; it is checked against\nthe tracing report and unresolved differences are surfaced. The digest is\n`never back-filled per requirement`, with gotchas `none beyond review findings` and\nkey files capped `at 5`.\n\n```markdown\n# Progress: <topic>\n\nDesign: docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md\n\nFeature phase: e2e-written\n\n## Requirements\n| # | Done | Requirement | Per-req ceremony | Commit |\n## Execution summary\n| R# | Requirement | How it was built | Deviated? | Evidence |\n## Code digest\n### Summary\n### Flow\n### Gotchas\n### Key files\n```\n</skill>"}],"timestamp":1791976408480}}

If on `main` — or on a different topic's feature branch, which stays that topic's own and never hosts this topic's commits — create or switch to this topic's branch: `git checkout <topic>` when it exists, else `git checkout -b <topic>` — the topic's folder slug (the `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` directory name, shared by every leaf of an umbrella), never a leaf slug. **`<topic>` is the folder slug** everywhere it appears in this skill, including the `../<repo>-<topic>` worktree convention below, so a standalone topic and an umbrella part name the same branch and the same worktree. For larger work, first check `git worktree list`: if a worktree already checks out this branch (the same `../<repo>-<topic>` convention), adopt it — resume the session there instead of offering a new `git worktree add`. One worktree per branch, created once: git refuses two checkouts of one branch, so a later umbrella part reuses part 1's worktree and a standalone resume reuses its own. Otherwise offer a worktree (`git worktree add ../<repo>-<topic> <topic>`) and hand off to a new session there so `pwd` is the worktree. **Uncommitted planning docs do not cross a worktree boundary**, and the design doc is still uncommitted (brainstorm never commits): when the user takes the worktree, commit the topic folder on this branch first — the same scoped add as the main skill's First-run commit — then switch this tree back to the branch it came from (e.g. `git checkout main` when it started there; git refuses `worktree add` of a branch that is still checked out here) and only then `git worktree add ../<repo>-<topic> <topic>` and hand off (the new session's First-run commit then has only its progress file to record). The adopt path above is safe only when the docs are already committed on the branch; if this tree holds uncommitted topic docs while another worktree holds the branch checkout, git refuses to commit to the branch from here — copy the topic folder into that worktree's `docs/plans/`, verify with `ls`, and remove the source copy before handing off. Wait for the user's choice.\n\n## Resume\n\nRead the progress file's `Feature phase` (match the line — e.g. `grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`), the Requirements table (the first row whose Done cell is not terminal routes the next requirement — `⬜`, `🔄`, and blank all mean not-done; `✅`/`❌`/`⏭` are resolved and are skipped past), and the Execution summary rows (how prior parts were built); read from the top through the end of `## Execution summary` and stop — the sections after it (deviation records, code digest) carry nothing the resume needs, with one exception: the `ship-paused` route re-presents the ship checkpoint, so it also reads the `## Code digest` written in the progress file. Before routing: if the header reads `Setup: pending` and the design doc has a `## Setup` section, the setup checkpoint was never approved — re-run the setup verification and wait at it:\n- `e2e-written` → write the E2E if not yet present, post the notice, and continue into the implement phase (no stop). A trivial design doc has no `## Feature acceptance` — skip both and go straight into the implement phase.\n- `implementing (k/N)` → continue the next not-yet-terminal requirement.\n- `reviewing` → continue/finish the feature review, then assemble the **ship** checkpoint.\n- `ship-paused` → re-present the ship checkpoint and wait — the execution summary, verdict rows, and code digest re-read from the progress file; if the prior session's reviewer reports are gone, re-run the feature review per the tag first (the checkpoint is never presented without coverage).\n\n=== progress-format.md ===\n# Progress format and code digest\n\nRead before creating or changing progress rows, or writing/re-presenting the code digest. This reference owns the unchanged progress artifact schema.\n\n2. **Create the progress file** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md`, beside the design doc it belongs to (`<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic; an umbrella part uses its roster slug), so `pwk-finalizing` finds it inside the topic folder. Keep the blank lines between the header fields: the blank lines are load-bearing, because CommonMark merges consecutive plain lines into one paragraph, so without them every preview renders the whole header as a single run-on line.\n\n   ```markdown\n   # Progress: <topic>\n\n   Design: docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md\n\n   Branch: <branch>\n\n   Setup: n/a\n\n   Started: <ISO timestamp>\n\n   Last updated: <ISO timestamp>\n\n   Feature phase: e2e-written\n\n   <!-- a trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`) starts at `implementing (0/N)` instead — there is no E2E to write -->\n\n   ## Requirements\n   | # | Done | Requirement | Per-req ceremony | Commit |\n   |---|------|-------------|-----------------|--------|\n   | 1 | ⬜ | <requirement name> | — | — |\n\n   ## Execution summary\n   | R# | Requirement | How it was built | Deviated? | Evidence |\n   |----|-------------|------------------|-----------|----------|\n   | 1 | <requirement name> | | | |\n\n   ## Deviation records\n\n   <!-- One short paragraph per design-decision reversal (what changed, why, what was rejected), written at deviation time; leave this section empty when every Deviated? entry is mechanical. -->\n\n   ## Code digest\n\n   <!-- Written once, after the feature review passes; never back-filled per requirement. -->\n\n   ### Summary\n   ### Flow\n   - **Spine** — `<entry point> -> [R1] <step> -> [R2] <step> -> <outcome>`\n   - **Branches**\n     - `<condition> -> <outcome>` [R2]\n     - `<changed behavior> — was: <previous behavior>`\n   - **Side effects** — reads: `<what>` · writes: `<what>`\n   ### Gotchas\n   - <one real risk per bullet>\n   ### Key files\n   - `<file>` — <what shifted inside it>\n   ```\n\n   The `## Code digest` is filled once, at the write point in the ship checkpoint — never per requirement. Fill rules: plain language, R# anchors where natural, no test names (the execution-summary rule). `### Summary` is 2–3 sentences: what the code now does differently, and why. `### Flow` uses `A -> B -> C` arrow chains, one spine or branch per bullet line, so every renderer shows each hop chain on its own line — bare label lines would merge into one run-on paragraph. `### Gotchas` lifts real risks from the review findings, one bullet each — `[ALERT]` only for reviewer-confirmed issues, never invented; with no findings, write `none beyond review findings` and mean it. `### Key files` is capped at 5 pivotal files, one bullet each: what shifted inside them.\n\n   **Flow shape** — this is the ship stop's navigable map, so it is the one digest section that carries structure, not just prose:\n\n   - **Spine** — the happy path as `A -> B -> C` hops, each hop named by symbol or module, with no line numbers anywhere and no file paths: symbol names survive edits and stay greppable, so a stale anchor can never mislead. Tag each hop `[R<n>]` with the requirement it comes from — that is what lets the coverage table's verdict rows be traced into the code without opening the diff.\n   - **Branches** — every alternative and error path as `condition -> outcome` (a linear spine with no branches reads as \"there are no edge cases\", which is rarely true). Put ⚠️ on the genuinely surprising ones. Add a `was: <previous behavior>` clause for each requirement whose behavior changed; skip it for purely additive requirements — honest-empty, never invented.\n   - **Inline worked values** — where a mapping is non-obvious, show it concretely (`` `implementing (2/5)` -> `execute 2/5` ``), so a reader can falsify it without running anything.\n   - **Side effects** — a bullet naming what is read and written, only when the feature performs I/O, network, or migrations; omit it entirely otherwise rather than filling a placeholder.\n   - **Cap: roughly 15 lines.** If the change genuinely needs more, the ship checkpoint **offers `/skill:pwk-walkthrough`** as the deep read (it regenerates a `file:line`-anchored walkthrough on demand) instead of growing the digest — the digest is what the human reads at the one remaining stop, and an unbounded Flow recreates the digging it exists to prevent.\n\n   `Feature phase` is one of: `e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`.\n\n   The `Setup:` header slot takes one of `Setup: pending | done | n/a` — the header starts `Setup: pending` when the design doc has a `## Setup` section, else `Setup: n/a`; the main skill's setup checkpoint flips it to `done` on approval. The phase line stays `e2e-written` through the setup stop — the Setup slot, not the phase, is what flags the not-yet-approved window, and the E2E is written after setup.\n\n\n## Progress file\n\nUpdate the matching requirement row directly (not via pattern matching that could corrupt the table). Update `Last updated` and `Feature phase` on every change.\n\n**Row vocabulary (canonical — this file owns it):**\n\n- **Done cell:** `⬜` not started · `🔄` in progress · `✅` done · `❌` failed · `⏭` skipped. A row is **terminal** when its Done cell is `✅`, `❌`, or `⏭` — resolved, not necessarily passed. A `❌`/`⏭` row carries its reason as a suffix in the Requirement cell (finalizing's verdict greps read it), and its test coverage is reconciled in the same step — assertions removed or skipped with the reason; the suite must stay green. This skill sets all five values. A requirement under review stays `🔄`: `pwk-code-review` reports findings and never edits the Done cell — the loop only ever flips `🔄`→`✅` when the review returns clean, and findings leave the row `🔄` for another pass.\n- **Per-req ceremony cell** echoes the design doc's tag, not progress: `—` (default `none`/`skip`) · `⏸ full` (fires two stops — after the slice's tests and after it is complete) · `🔎 inline` · `🔎 parallel`.\n\n**Execution summary rows are written in the same step as marking a requirement ✅** — never retrofitted at the end. \"How it was built\" = one or two plain sentences: what it does now + the approach actually taken; file names sparingly; **no test-name lists, no code** (the human reads this at the ship checkpoint — big picture only; the `Evidence` cell may name **one probe test**, never a list). The `Evidence` cell pairs **what it proves in plain words** with a pointer — a commit, a `file:line`, a command with its observed output line, or the single probe test — single-line so the table never breaks. No requirement is marked ✅ with an empty `Evidence` cell: either the pointer exists or the requirement is not done. If the implementation departs from the design, fill the Deviated? column **at deviation time** (when the departure happens), with a one-line why — it is a log, not a stop. A departure that **reverses or alters a design decision** gets a **deviation decision-record**: a short paragraph (what changed, why, what was rejected) written into the progress file while the knowledge is fresh — mechanical deviations keep the one-liner. `pwk-finalizing`'s learning sweep harvests these records for ADRs before the docs are disposed.\n\n\n## Commit entries for packet assembly\n\nRecord immutable hexadecimal commit IDs (7–64 characters). A cell can hold one ID or an ordered, whitespace-separated list: initial implementation first, review-fix commits last. Preserve the first recorded commit when appending a fix; replacing it loses the feature base. Record a commit hash after committing, never amend a commit to include its own hash.\n\nThe helper reads only the Requirements table Commit column. A done or in-review row needs a recorded commit. Terminal `❌`/`⏭` rows may have `—` when no commit remains; this does not supply a bound for a requirement packet. +{"type":"message","id":"4ba6fdd2","parentId":"240c3e98","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:15:04.992Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_O2jMR5EELeX56nUM7dMP2115","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"<console_output>\n=== review.md ===\n# Review mechanics and packet helper\n\nRead before any feature or opt-in requirement review, before refreshing a packet, and before writing the code digest from review evidence.\n\n## Assemble evidence\n\n**Assemble the review packet first** — once, by script, so that no packet byte passes through model output (spawn arguments are model output; file reads are not). The Commit column is the packet's source of truth for both spans: the feature packet base is `git rev-parse <first Commit-column entry>^` (the parent of the first recorded commit); a per-requirement packet spans from the previous requirement's last commit (exclusive) to this requirement's last commit (inclusive), with R1's exclusive bound being its own parent. No `merge-base` guessing, no default-branch knowledge. If commits land while the review is in flight, re-run the recipe before spawning any replacement role so the packet matches HEAD:\n\nUse the installed skill directory, not a repository checkout of the kit. First verify `python3 --version` reports Python 3.9 or newer and that the helper exists. Missing runtime/resource → report the dependency and stop this step. No runtime auto-install or alternate-language fallback.\n\n```sh\npython3 \"<executing-skill-dir>/scripts/build-review-packet.py\" \\\n  --project \"<repo-root>\" \\\n  --design \"docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md\" \\\n  --progress \"docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md\" \\\n  --scope feature\n```\n\nFor an opt-in requirement review, use the same invocation with `--scope requirement --requirement 2` (substitute the selected number). The feature destination is `<design doc's directory>/<leaf>-review-packet.md`; the requirement destination is `<design doc's directory>/<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`. Requirement-suffixed packets never overwrite each other or the feature packet.\n\n`--project` resolves from the caller's cwd and must name the Git worktree root. Design/progress arguments are absolute or relative to that project, regardless of the current directory or installed skill location. Both must be matched leaf files inside one active `docs/plans/<topic>/` folder. The helper derives the destination; symlink destinations are refused. Use argument lists in programmatic invocations, never shell interpolation.\n\nThe packet retains these sections, in order:\n- `## Commits`\n- `## Changed files`\n- `## Acceptance criteria (verbatim from the design doc)`\n- `## Feature acceptance (verbatim)` (empty for a trivial design)\n- `## Production-risk notes (verbatim, if any)`\n- `## Diff`\n\nCriteria and production-risk content remain verbatim, including all lines in multiple risk blocks; fenced template headings do not route extraction. Feature criteria span from the first real requirement to Feature acceptance (or document end); requirement criteria include only the selected requirement block. Design-level production-risk areas are retained as review context. The packet header records fixed `Base:` and `Head:` IDs: feature uses the first recorded commit's parent through current HEAD; requirement uses the previous requirement's last recorded commit exclusively through the selected last recorded commit inclusively. The helper excludes generated `*-review-packet*.md` files from diff/stat, including committed packets.\n\nA Commit cell is one immutable hexadecimal ID or an ordered whitespace-separated list. Preserve the first ID; append review-fix IDs in order. Feature assembly permits missing commits only for terminal failed/skipped rows. Requirement assembly needs an explicit selected and previous bound; it refuses to guess across a failed/skipped row without a commit. Missing relevant rows, malformed/ambiguous entries, invalid revisions, or non-ancestral order → correct the record from evidence and rerun. The helper never edits progress, commits, switches branches, or marks anything approved. It finishes all parse/Git work before atomically replacing a complete packet. A nonzero exit is failure, not review evidence: report stderr and stop delegation; an older packet remains intact but may be stale.\n\nAfter late review fixes, commit them and append their IDs to the selected row before refreshing a requirement packet; feature packets refresh HEAD automatically. Re-run the helper before any replacement reviewer and before digest writing if stale or missing. Packet generation is evidence assembly, not review approval. Re-green the full suite + E2E after fixes, then complete review and the human checkpoint.\n\n## Delegate or review inline\n\n- **`parallel`** (the `auto` resolution when risk content is present) — request the host’s `parallel-review` capability for four fresh-context, read-only logical roles: `pwk-spec-reviewer`, `pwk-tracing-reviewer`, `pwk-smell-reviewer`, and `pwk-hazard-reviewer`. Spawn each role with a **one-liner** — a pointer to the packet file with the role framing appended last: the checklist name of the role (`spec alignment`, `code tracing`, `code smells`, or `production hazards`). For example: `Read docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-review-packet.md. Your role: spec alignment.` The packet never appears in spawn arguments. Require independent execution and one collected outcome per role. The reviewer role contracts live in `agents/pwk-*-reviewer.md`; do not duplicate their checklists in the workflow instructions. Reviewers are read-only reporters; you apply smell fixes yourself (full suite + E2E must stay green, commit) and flag trace/spec/hazard findings as follow-ups for the human.\n\n- **`inline`** — perform `/skill:pwk-code-review` over the whole diff as a single pass.\n- **Fallback** — if the host has no compatible parallel-review capability, cannot prove the requested read-only/fresh-context/bounded constraints, or delegation fails, perform the missing review work inline. Retain successful delegated reports and do not mark the feature fully reviewed while a required role is missing.\n\n=== pwk-code-review/SKILL.md ===\n---\nname: pwk-code-review\ndescription: \"Review a completed requirement's code — trace the logic, check spec alignment against the acceptance criteria, fix code smells, and run a production hazard check. Runs as the feature-level review in pwk-executing-tasks (whole feature diff), or per-requirement when tagged. Unlocked: may edit code to apply smell fixes.\"\n---\n\n# Code Review\n\nReview the code just implemented — one tagged requirement, or the whole feature at the feature-level review. **Unlocked** — you may edit code to apply smell fixes; flag everything else as a follow-up.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Identify the scope** — in the feature-gate flow (the default), you review the **whole feature diff** at the feature-level review (`git diff $FEATURE_BASE...HEAD` — the parent of the first Commit-column entry; see the executing skill's packet recipe); all acceptance criteria in the design doc and the `## Feature acceptance` E2E are in scope. When invoked per-requirement (`Review: inline` on a tagged requirement — or inline-completing a missing delegated role when the tag is `parallel`), scope is just that requirement — read its acceptance criteria from the design doc, run `git log --oneline -5` and `git diff` to see what changed for it. Invoked standalone — no invoking skill, no design doc, no packet — review the span the user names (the working-tree diff, or the branch's commits against its parent branch): tracing, smell fixes, and the hazard check run as usual, while spec alignment has no acceptance criteria to key on — say so and judge the diff against its stated intent instead of manufacturing a coverage table. When the invoking skill already assembled a review packet (the feature packet, or the requirement-scoped `<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`), work from the packet — it is the scope of record; re-derive nothing the packet already states.\n\n2. **🔍 Code tracing** — trace the new or changed code paths end-to-end against the acceptance criteria and the feature E2E (a trivial design doc has no feature E2E — its acceptance criteria alone are the spec). For each path, determine whether data flows correctly from entry to the asserted outcome. Note any branch the tests do not exercise, any dead branch, or any path where the trace breaks.\n\n3. **📐 Spec alignment** — for each acceptance criterion, point to the code and the test that satisfy it. A criterion with no covering code or no test is a **gap**. Code that does more than the criteria specify is **scope creep** — flag it.\n\n   **Open the report with a coverage table** — one row per requirement in scope, keyed by the design doc's `### R<n>:` headings (R# = n; the whole design doc at the feature-level review, just the tagged requirement when invoked per-requirement):\n\n   | R# | Verdict | Evidence |\n   |----|---------|----------|\n   | 1 | <verdict> | file:line (code), file:line (test) |\n\n   Verdict per requirement: `covered | gap | scope-creep` — `covered` = every criterion has covering code and a test; `gap` = a criterion lacks code or a test; `scope-creep` = the code does more than the criteria specify. Findings elaborate on every non-`covered` row; an all-`covered` table needs no elaboration.\n\n4. **🧹 Code smells — fix these directly:** review the changed code and affected files against the requirement and feature scope, then fix what you find.\n   - Shallow modules (interface nearly as complex as implementation)\n   - Duplication\n   - Missing seams or premature abstraction\n   - Poor naming, magic values, dead code\n   Apply the fix, re-run the full suite (must stay green), and commit. Only a smell that requires a refactor large enough to risk the requirement is **flagged** instead of applied.\n\n5. **⚠️ Production hazard check** — audit the changed code against the high-risk hazards. For each, write `[SAFE]` (1-line justification) or `[TRIGGERED]` (concrete mitigation):\n   1. **Unbounded operations** — multi-key deletions/scans (`KEYS`, raw `SCAN` loops), full-table loads filtered in memory\n   2. **Missing indexes** — hot queries on unindexed columns (table scans under load)\n   3. **Unbounded concurrency** — unthrottled fan-out (`Promise.all` without batch limits)\n   4. **Long-running transactions** — holding DB connections/locks across slow external calls\n   5. **Query/command interpolation** — raw variables merged into SQL or shell (injection)\n   6. **Unrestricted uploads / temp flooding** — uploads to local temp without limits or `finally` cleanup\n   7. **Silent swallowing loops** — background workers catching/suppressing exceptions without logging/back-off\n   Also check the design's `## Production-risk areas`, if any.\n\n6. **Report** — summarize: tracing findings, spec gaps, smells fixed (with commits), hazards `[TRIGGERED]`. Non-trivial findings become follow-up items — the user decides whether to address now or defer.\n7. **Mark done** — the review never edits the progress file. A clean pass hands back so the executing loop can set the requirement's Done cell `✅` (the row was left `🔄` while under review) and write its execution-summary row; findings leave the row `🔄` for another pass. (At the feature-level review every row is already terminal — verify none regressed and move on.) Already-terminal rows of other requirements never regress. Done means reviewed, not just committed.\n\n## Principles\n\n- **Tracing and spec alignment are the core** — they catch what tests miss: untested branches, missing criteria, scope creep.\n- **Fix smells in place; flag everything else.** Keep the review scoped — the goal is polish on the requirement that just landed, not a redesign pass.\n- **Be proportional** — a one-function change doesn't need the depth of a batch pipeline. When this skill runs as the inline path because the design doc tagged the requirement `Review: inline`, that was a deliberate call at design approval — keep the review focused and don't second-guess the tag.\n\n## After the review\n\nReturn to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` — the next requirement, or the ship checkpoint when every requirement is done. Finalizing is proposed from the ship checkpoint, never from here. (The human tagged this requirement at design approval when its `### Review` tag was set — keep the review focused on the tag's scope.)\n=== progress now ===\n# Progress: since-filter\n\nDesign: The returned `first`/`last` remain the raw input time strings.\nOmitting `since` (or passing `undefined`/`null`) reproduces today's output exactly.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n- Given entries at `2026-01-04T09:00:00Z`, `09:05:00Z`, and `09:07:00Z`, When `summarize` runs with `since: \"2026-01-04T09:05:00Z\"`, Then the returned `levels` count only the 09:05 and 09:07 entries and `first`/`last` are `09:05:00Z`/`09:07:00Z`.\n- Given an entry whose time exactly equals `since`, When `summarize` runs with that `since`, Then the entry is kept (the bound is inclusive).\n- Given entries with missing or unparseable `time` alongside a `since` filter, When `summarize` runs, Then those entries contribute to neither `levels` nor the reported range.\n- Given `since` omitted, When `summarize` runs on any text, Then the result is identical to the pre-change output for that text.\n- Given a date-only value such as `2026-01-04`, When `summarize` runs, Then the cutoff is `2026-01-04T00:00:00Z` (settled by sketch: `node -e 'Date.parse(\"2026-01-04\")'` → `2026-01-04T00:00:00.000Z`).\n- Given an entry bearing a non-`Z` offset that is later in epoch terms but earlier lexicographically, When `summarize` runs with a `since` between them, Then the entry is kept (comparison is by parsed instant, not string order).\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n\n### R2: Accept `--since` on the command line\n\nThe CLI recognizes `--since <value>`, takes the value after the flag, and passes it to\n`summarize`. The single remaining positional argument is the input file, still defaulting to\n`fixtures/events.jsonl`; the flag and the file may appear in either order, and a repeated\n`--since` uses the last value.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n- Given the fixture log, When the CLI runs with `--since 2026-01-04T09:05:00Z fixtures/events.jsonl`, Then stdout is the filtered JSON summary.\n- Given the same inputs, When the CLI runs with the file path before `--since`, Then stdout is byte-identical to the flag-first run.\n- Given `--since <value>` with no file positional, When the CLI runs, Then it reads `fixtures/events.jsonl`.\n- Given `--since A --since B`, When the CLI runs, Then the `B` cutoff governs the output.\n- Given no `--since`, When the CLI runs on a file, Then stdout is unchanged from the pre-change CLI output.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n\n### R3: Reject an unparseable or valueless `--since`\n\nCalling `summarize` with a `since` that does not parse throws a `TypeError` naming the offending\nvalue, before any summary is produced. At the CLI, that error — and a `--since` that is the last\nargument with no value — is reported as `log-summary: <message>` on stderr with nothing on stdout\nand exit code 2. Errors unrelated to `--since` (such as an unreadable input file) keep their\nprevious behavior.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n- Given `--since not-a-date`, When the CLI runs, Then stderr carries a message naming `not-a-date`, stdout is empty, and the exit code is 2.\n- Given `--since` as the final argument with no following value, When the CLI runs, Then stderr carries a message and the exit code is 2.\n- Given a directly-imported `summarize`, When it is called with `since: \"2026-13-45\"`, Then it throws a `TypeError` rather than returning a summary.\n- Given a valid `--since` and a nonexistent input file, When the CLI runs, Then the failure is not converted to exit code 2 (the file error keeps its prior uncaught exit-1 behavior).\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n\n## Approaches considered\n\n- **A — Option parameter with epoch comparison, gating inside the existing loop (chosen).** Add `summarize(text, { since } = {})`, normalize `since` once, and skip disqualified entries before tallying. Smallest change to the exported surface; the no-filter branch of the loop is untouched, so existing behavior is preserved by construction.\n- **B — Two-phase parse/filter/reduce.** Parse every line into an object, filter with an exported `filterEvents`, then reduce. A second test seam, but it restructures the streaming loop that the \"unchanged when unfiltered\" guarantee rests on, and it materializes the whole log in memory — more surface than the feature needs.\n- **C — Filter in the CLI before calling `summarize`.** Drop lines by string comparison before the function sees them. Rejected: the filter becomes untestable at the unit seam, entries with no timestamp cannot be classified without parsing anyway, and it forces the lexicographic comparison rejected above.\n\n## Architecture\n\nOne module, no new files and no dependencies (stdlib only, consistent with the project). The change\nsplits into a parameterized pure function — the testable core — and a thin CLI adapter that parses\narguments, delegates, and owns process-level error reporting.\n\n## Components\n\n- **`summarize(text, { since } = {})`** — normalizes `since` to epoch milliseconds (`number` as-is, otherwise `Date.parse`; a `NaN` result throws `TypeError`). When a filter is active it skips entries whose `time` is absent/unparseable or earlier than the cutoff; otherwise its tallying and range logic are exactly as before.\n- **`parseArgs(argv)`** (module-internal) — scans for `--since`, consumes the next argument as its value (none present → `TypeError`), and collects positionals; the last positional is the file, defaulting to `fixtures/events.jsonl`. A repeated `--since` overwrites, so the last wins.\n- **CLI body** — reads the resolved file, calls `summarize`, and prints the JSON summary. A narrow `try`/`catch` around argument parsing and summarization maps their errors to `log-summary: <message>` on stderr plus exit code 2.\n\n## Data flow\n\n`argv` → `parseArgs` → `{ file, since }` → `readFileSync` → `summarize(text, { since })` →\n`JSON.stringify` → stdout. Filtered results keep the raw input `time` strings in `first`/`last`;\nno reformatting or normalization of the reported values is introduced.\n\n## Error handling\n\n| Situation | Behavior |\n| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `--since <unparseable>` | `TypeError` from `summarize`; CLI: stderr message, empty stdout, exit 2 |\n| `--since` with no value | `TypeError` from `parseArgs`; CLI: stderr message, empty stdout, exit 2 |\n| Timestamp missing/unparseable on an entry | Excluded silently while filtering; never an error |\n| Input file unreadable | Unchanged — propagates as today, exit 1 |\n\n## Testing\n\nObservable behavior only: library semantics are checked by asserting the returned summary object\nacross the boundary, untimed-entry, mixed-format, and no-filter cases; the CLI is checked by running\n`node scripts/log-summary.mjs …` and inspecting stdout, stderr, and the exit code.
