+{"type":"message","id":"2a66a67c","parentId":"caa52bae","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:16:26.876Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<skill name=\"pwk-finalizing\" location=\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-finalizing/SKILL.md\">\nReferences are relative to /Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-finalizing.\n\n# Finalizing\n\nShip the completed work.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Pre-finalization checks\n\n1. **Verify the repo root** — run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts).\n2. **Run the FULL test suite** — every test must pass, and only a green suite ships. Resume spans sessions; re-run the suite yourself rather than trust the previous session's ending state. Anything failing → send the user back to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`.\n3. Read **every** relevant progress file — for a multi-leaf topic that's each leaf's progress file — discovered by listing `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-progress.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`. With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every topic’s `Feature phase:` extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   More than one topic in flight? Ask which one this finalize ships — finalizing touches only its own topic, and another topic still being designed or executed never blocks this run. Then match, in the chosen topic's file(s), the `Feature phase:` line (e.g. `grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`) and read only the matching ❌/⏭ verdict rows in the Requirements table (e.g. `sed -n '/^## Requirements/,/^## Execution summary/p' <file> | grep '^| [0-9].*❌'` / `sed -n '/^## Requirements/,/^## Execution summary/p' <file> | grep '^| [0-9].*⏭'` — scoped to Requirements-table rows because the Execution summary rows share the same row shape, with reasons); the sections after the tables carry nothing the gate needs. Apply the gates below to the chosen topic's file(s) and no others:\n   - **Any `❌ failed`** (in any leaf of the topic) → **block**. Present counts and reasons; continue only when the user sends the task back to executing-tasks, or explicitly types `--force-failed` to acknowledge shipping with incomplete requirements.\n   - **Only `⏭ skipped`** → warn and confirm (\"Requirement N was skipped. Continue, or go back?\").\n   - **`Feature phase` must be `done`** in every progress file of the topic — any other value (`e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`) means that topic is still in flight: its ship checkpoint has not been approved. Send the user back to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` instead of finalizing.\n4. **Cross-check the roster — fail closed on unstarted work.** Find the topic folder locally: the progress file's `Design:` ref names the design doc, and that directory is the topic folder. An `overview.md` **beside the design doc** (same folder — never a repo-wide `docs/plans/**/overview.md`, or a sibling topic's overview would route this finalize) means a multi-leaf topic. Read that overview's `## Parts (build order)` roster and require one `<leaf>-progress.md` per leaf. A roster leaf with no progress file is **unstarted** — **block**, naming the leaf, and send the user back to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` to build it; never dispose an unstarted design unread. (A leaf with a progress file that is not `done` is already stopped by the gate above.)\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Derive the topic set** —\n   - **Multi-leaf topic** (an `overview.md` sits beside the design doc, inside the same `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folder — never a repo-wide `docs/plans/**/overview.md`, and always excluding docs/plans/completed/, so an archived or sibling topic never routes): read its roster; the set is the topic folder itself, disposed as one unit.\n   - **Single-leaf topic**: progress file → `Design:` ref → that design doc's own folder → `<topic>`, which **is the folder slug** — the topic directory's name, and the same value `pwk-executing-tasks` uses for the branch and worktree (never a leaf filename). One folder.\n\n   Ambiguous with several designs in flight? Ask.\n2. **Run the learning sweep — before any disposal command.** The planning docs are about to be destroyed; extract the durable knowledge first, while its container still exists. Read each design doc's At-a-glance key-decision bullets **and its `Approaches considered` section** (the full forks with their reasoning — every leaf's, for an umbrella), each progress file's `Deviated?` entries (including any deviation decision-records), and each Code digest's `[ALERT]` entries. (A trivial doc has no `## At a glance` and no `Approaches considered` — a trivial slice's sweep is expected to come up honest-empty.) Then:\n   - **Offer an ADR** (in `docs/adr/`) for each item that passes the three gates — **hard to reverse**, **surprising without context**, **a real trade-off** — informed by how the decision actually played out during execution, not just how it looked at design time.\n   - **Append generic rules** to `docs/lessons.md` (strip domain specifics).\n   - Both outputs are **honest-empty**: most features qualify for nothing — say so and move on; never manufacture. When an item passes the gates but the recorded material is too thin to draft a credible ADR, **ask the human rather than fabricating** context — the human was there.\n   - The sweep is file-based by necessity: executing and finalizing usually run in fresh sessions with no memory of the brainstorm conversation — everything the sweep needs must already be on disk.\n3. **Dispose of consumed plan docs — ask archive or delete** — for **every topic** in the set, dispose its topic folder `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` **as one unit**: every leaf's `-design.md`, `-progress.md`, and `-review-packet*.md`, plus `overview.md` for an umbrella. The digest sections (`## At a glance`, `## Execution summary`) live inside their host docs and ride the folder — no separate disposal; the Evidence cells ride with the summary rows, so the shipped record keeps its proof. The folder path is taken verbatim from discovery, and the `????-??-??-` dated shape is the topic's identity — a bare `*<topic>*` pattern would over-match unrelated topics. Present both options and let the human choose:\n\n   - **Delete (default)** — code + tests are the source of truth; removing the scaffold prevents stale plan docs from misleading future sessions:\n\n     The invariant: the topic folder `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is the disposal unit — delete it entirely, nothing more and nothing less; any single operation achieving exactly this is correct, and the bash below is one canonical example.\n\n     ```bash\n     # the topic folder goes as one unit (every leaf, plus overview.md if it has one).\n     # The folder path is taken verbatim from discovery — never typed or\n     # reconstructed (rm -rf has no glob guard):\n     rm -rf docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/\n     git add -A docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ && git commit -m \"chore: delete planning docs for <topic>\"\n     # the add is scoped to the topic pathspec, so another in-flight topic's\n     # uncommitted drafts never ride the disposal commit.\n     ```\n\n   - **Archive** — keep the planning history for future readers (e.g. a complex design worth preserving) by moving the artifacts into `docs/plans/completed/`:\n\n     The invariant: the topic folder `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` moves whole into `docs/plans/completed/` and the destination is verified before committing; any single operation achieving exactly this is correct, and the bash below is one canonical example.\n\n     ```bash\n     mkdir -p docs/plans/completed\n     # the topic folder goes as one unit (every leaf, plus overview.md if it has one).\n     # No error suppression on the folder move: verify the archive landed before\n     # committing, or a silently failed move would commit the deletion and destroy\n     # the history the human chose to keep:\n     mv docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ docs/plans/completed/\n     ls docs/plans/completed/<date>-<topic>/ >/dev/null\n     # both sides of the move, and nothing else — another in-flight topic's\n     # uncommitted drafts never ride the archive commit:\n     git add -A docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ docs/plans/completed/ && git commit -m \"chore: archive planning docs for <topic>\"\n     ```\n\n   Verify with `ls docs/plans/` before and after. Both paths commit the disposal so the shipped branch is clean. Neither path touches `docs/adr/`, `docs/lessons.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, or `README.md` — those are permanent.\n4. **Curate lessons (Agile Scrum Master hat)** — if `docs/lessons.md` exists: add missed lessons, generalize domain-specific rules into generic patterns, de-duplicate, categorize, retire stale rules. None exists but lessons were learned? Create it. (The learning sweep above feeds this; curation then shapes the whole file.)\n5. **Update documentation** — if the API or surface changed: `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, any inline docs. Bump the package version (major for breaking changes).\n6. **Choose a merge strategy** — ask the human:\n\n   1. **Create PR** — `git push origin <branch>` then `gh pr create`.\n   2. **Rebase & merge** *(recommended)* — rebase onto parent, `--ff-only` merge, push parent, delete branch.\n   3. **Squash & merge** — squash onto parent, push, delete branch.\n   4. **Merge commit** — `--no-ff` merge, push parent, delete branch.\n\n   For 2–4, confirm the detected parent branch before proceeding. When a worktree was used, the parent-side commands (merge onto parent, push parent, branch deletion) run from the main working tree — the topic worktree holds the feature-branch checkout, so the parent cannot be checked out there (`git -C ../<repo> …` drives the main side without moving the session; the root check's never-cd rule still holds) — and step 7's worktree removal comes **first**: a branch checked out in a worktree cannot be deleted.\n7. **Clean up** — if a worktree was used, verify presence first (`git worktree list`): when the topic's worktree exists, remove it (`git worktree remove ../<repo>-<topic>`, where `<topic>` is the folder slug — the same one `pwk-executing-tasks` created the branch under, never a leaf slug). The `../` path is written from the main working tree, and the removal runs from there — `git -C ../<repo> worktree remove ../<repo>-<topic>` when the session stands inside the worktree, which git refuses to remove under itself. When absent, cleanup is a silent no-op — never a failure.\n\n## Principles\n\n- The learning sweep runs before disposal and touches only `docs/adr/` and `docs/lessons.md` — the two permanent stores.\n\n- Dispose of the active work's artifacts only (archive or delete, the human's choice) — the unit is the topic folder `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/`, one folder whether the topic has a single leaf or an umbrella's many. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.\n- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.\n- Optional first line: `// @options: {\"max_output_tokens\": 10000, \"timeout_ms\": 60000}`\n\nGlobals:\n- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.\n- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.\n- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.\n- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /Users/yinlootan/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.\n\nNested tools:\n\n### `read`\nRead the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.\n\n- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { read(args: {\n  // Maximum number of lines to read\n  limit?: number;\n  // Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)\n  offset?: number;\n  // Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)\n  path: string;\n}): Promise<string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: \"image\"; }>; };\n```\n\n### `bash`\nExecute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.\n\n- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { bash(args: {\n  // Shell command to execute\n  command: string;\n  // Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)\n  timeout?: number;\n}): Promise<{\n  exit_code: number;\n  // Full output, when truncated\n  full_output_path?: string;\n  // Combined stdout and stderr, possibly truncated\n  output: string;\n  truncated: boolean;\n  wall_time_seconds: number;\n}>; };\n```\n\n### `edit`\nEdit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.\n\n- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)\n- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls\n- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.\n- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { edit(args: {\n  // One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.\n  edits: Array<{\n    // Replacement text for this targeted edit.\n    newText: string;\n    // Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.\n    oldText: string;\n  }>;\n  // Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)\n  path: string;\n}): Promise<string>; };\n```\n\n### `write`\nWrite content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.\n\n- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { write(args: {\n  // Content to write to the file\n  content: string;\n  // Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)\n  path: string;\n}): Promise<string>; };\n```","parameters":{"type":"object","required":["code"],"properties":{"code":{"type":"string","description":"Raw JavaScript source."}}},"constrainedSampling":{"type":"grammar","variants":{"openai_lark":"\nstart: options_source | plain_source\noptions_source: OPTIONS_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE\nplain_source: SOURCE\n\nOPTIONS_LINE: /[ \\t]*\\/\\/ @options:[^\\r\\n]*/\nNEWLINE: /\\r?\\n/\nSOURCE: /[\\s\\S]+/\n"}}}]}}

+{"type":"message","id":"be92108f","parentId":"9c871974","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:19:05.297Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll start by loading the brainstorming skill, since you asked to design first."},{"type":"toolCall","id":"call_00_ET_GfPkJWRZTmzuUIhWepmG7359","name":"codemode","arguments":{"code":"const skill = await tools.read({ path: \"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/SKILL.md\" });\ntext(skill);"}}],"api":"openai-completions","provider":"olaparty","model":"deepseek-flash","usage":{"input":160,"output":97,"cacheRead":2944,"cacheWrite":0,"reasoning":0,"totalTokens":3201,"cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0}},"stopReason":"toolUse","timestamp":1791976743202,"responseId":"40abd845-091c-40b8-80f9-f767f2d339a4","rawStopReason":"tool_calls","durationMs":2095,"thinkingLevel":"high"}}
+{"type":"message","id":"a7ec30da","parentId":"be92108f","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:19:05.348Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_ET_GfPkJWRZTmzuUIhWepmG7359","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"---\nname: pwk-brainstorming\ndescription: \"Use this before any creative work — creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores intent and design, then writes the single buildable design doc (requirements with acceptance criteria + review tags) that pwk-executing-tasks builds from. Use this skill whenever the user describes something they want to build, change, or improve, even if they don't say 'brainstorm' — phrases like 'I want to add X', 'let's build Y', 'we need a way to Z', or 'help me design' all apply.\"\n---\n\n# Brainstorming\n\nRead-only exploration of source code; every file you create or edit goes under `docs/plans/`. (An approved ADR goes to `docs/adr/`, which sits outside the writable boundary — the human writes it themselves or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`; the design phase never unlocks it.) The design doc is the **single buildable artifact** — each requirement carries its own acceptance criteria and review tags, and the executor builds straight from it; nothing is re-derived into a second document later. Source-writing happens in `pwk-executing-tasks`.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Proportionality: trivial vs non-trivial\n\nClassify the change at the start.\n\n- **Trivial** — typo or obvious bugfix with no open design questions, config/version bump, single-function change, or anything the human flags as trivial. Skip steps 3–6; read the design-format reference and run the validator in step 7, writing a **minimal** design doc in one turn (an `In short:` one-liner — what + why + approach in plain words, plus a single `### R1:` requirement block with its criteria and tags, and an optional `## Production-risk areas` line — and deliberately **no `## Feature acceptance`**: a trivial slice's ship gate is the full existing suite, no E2E is manufactured for it), and hand off to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`. The guard still enforces read-only — trivial compresses the phase to one turn, it doesn't skip it.\n- **Non-trivial** — open design questions, multiple approaches, cross-module impact, or new behavior. Run the full process below.\n\nWhen unsure, ask: \"This looks trivial — fast-path it, or full brainstorm?\" Default to full.\n\n## Scope and granularity\n\n**One design doc = one PR; one requirement = one testable slice within it.** Most work is a single design doc; several requirements serving one cohesive outcome do not force an umbrella.\n\nBefore drafting, assess whether a large request has distinct testable outcomes that need separate design/execute cycles. If so, propose an **umbrella** of vertical slices with one-line scopes and a build order, and get human approval before writing an overview or design. A layers-only split (database, API, UI) is not a vertical split: each slice delivers testable behavior. Design only the current slice; ground later designs in implemented code, not speculative sibling designs. The umbrella still ships as one PR on one branch, finalized once.\n\n**One folder per topic:** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/`, containing `<leaf>-design.md`, `<leaf>-progress.md`, and `<leaf>-review-packet*.md`; `<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic. More than one leaf adds `overview.md`. The whole folder is the creation/discovery/disposal unit.\n\n**Umbrella trigger:** before proposing or writing a new umbrella, or when discovery finds an existing `overview.md` beside this design, read [references/umbrella.md](references/umbrella.md). It defines the status-free roster, first/later-slice procedures, and header-only predecessor reporting. Build order is advisory, not an enforcement gate. An existing roster means the split is already decided; design the current slice against it.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Check git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`. Uncommitted work? Ask the user what to do first.\n2. **Discovery** *(skip in a brand-new repo with no `docs/plans/`)* — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md`, `*-progress.md`, and `overview.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; report in-flight topics and any active umbrella, each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`; design-only topics report `design` — no body ingest). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   If the new idea continues an existing topic, ask whether to extend it or start fresh. Part of an umbrella? An existing `overview.md` **beside the design doc** means the split is already decided — read it for the roster and design this part's `<leaf>-design.md` against it (read [references/umbrella.md](references/umbrella.md) before proceeding).\n3. **Understand the idea** — **PRD brief.** When the topic arrives with source material (a PRD, ticket, or spec — pasted text, a file path, or a URL), open with a brief before any question: **Background** (the problem, why now, who is affected — each product claim cites its PRD section), **Current situation** (what the code does today — each claim cites `file:line`), **The delta** (what must change, each line naming a requirement candidate, and what stays untouched). Zero-context rule: plain meaning first, the pointer second — the reader has not read the code; quote non-English domain terms verbatim with a plain-English gloss; mark anything uncited `(interpretation: …)`. Unreadable source material: report the blocker, ground on code only, name the gap in the brief. The human corrects the brief before frontier rounds begin — confirmed facts weave into the design doc, no sidecar file. No source material, no brief. Then read only enough code/docs/commits to ground the design. **Check `docs/lessons.md`** — known constraints may shape it. Ask questions in **frontier rounds**: build a question tree seeded by the dimension checklist, then ask in rounds. The **frontier** is every question whose prerequisites are already settled — ask the whole frontier in one round; a question whose answer depends on another still-open question waits for a later round. Number each question (`Q1`, `Q2`, …) and attach your recommended answer (`➡️ <recommendation>`) — the recommendation is your assumption surfaced up front; the human confirms, strikes, or corrects each in one reply. Recompute the frontier after each round of answers. Seed the tree by walking every checklist dimension — *Goal & scope · Data & state · Behavior & edge cases · Errors & failure · Integration · Non-functional* — printing `— nothing to ask` for groups with no questions (never skip silently). **Facts vs. decisions**: anything answerable from the codebase, docs, or tools is looked up — recon scout or inline — never asked of the human; a pending lookup is an unsettled prerequisite that holds only its downstream questions, while the rest of the frontier is asked now. **Runnable facts**: an unknown observable by running something — behavior, timing, output, layout — is settled by a bounded sketch, never asked of the human and never guessed: an inline interpreter or a file under `docs/plans/<topic>/`, no installs, no source writes (the guard already enforces the boundary); record the settled fact where it lands as `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` and list it in the round summary so the human can strike it; a sketch result that would set business behavior still passes the assumption gate; inconclusive or blocked → record `INCONCLUSIVE` plus one line of what ran, and the question returns to the human with the result attached; a cheaper read beats a run when reading can decide. Only decisions are asked. Major approvals stay single-decision — one question each, never batched: approach selection (step 5), umbrella split, design approval, ADR offer. The interview ends when the frontier is empty — every branch visited, nothing left silently assumed — not when you feel you understand. Then present a short summary and ask: \"Should I proceed, or is there more?\" The human decides when to move on.\n4. **(skipped on trivial changes)** **Codebase recon** — for non-trivial topics with prior art, request the host’s `codebase-recon` capability using the logical `pwk-recon-scout` role. Require a fresh-context, read-only, bounded worker and pass the topic, one-line intent, and repo root. Use the returned 5-section codebase map (Relevant files, Existing patterns, Call sites, Test layout, Gotchas) as the grounding context for the next two steps instead of reading those files inline. The scout is observations only — no design recommendations. Skip this step on trivial changes (typo, version bump, single-function edit per the proportionality rule). If no compatible capability is available or the provider cannot enforce the requested constraints, report `Scout: unavailable` and do the same recon inline, preserving the five-section map and `file:line` citations; do not silently omit recon.\n5. **Explore approaches** — propose 2–3, leading with your recommendation. Sketch the concrete interface (types, signatures, example caller) for each so the comparison is grounded in code, not abstractions.\n6. **Present the design** in one pass, organized into sections (architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing) — the human comments on any section; re-present only revised sections.\n\n   **Assumptions to confirm first** — before presenting, sweep the drafted design: every assumption it would bake in unconfirmed (business rules, defaults, edge-case resolutions) re-opens as a numbered question carrying your recommended answer; the human confirms, strikes, or corrects each in one reply. An honest empty gate (\"no unconfirmed assumptions\") when the draft is clean — never invent items. Hard rule: no business behavior enters the design doc on the agent's assumption. Confirmed facts are woven into the doc's existing sections — no new template section.\n\n   Identified a significant architectural decision? Offer an ADR in `docs/adr/`. Only when all three hold: **hard to reverse**, **surprising without context**, **a real trade-off**. Format: title + 1–3 sentences of context/decision/why. ADRs are permanent institutional memory — they stay out of archive/rotation forever. (Guard note: `docs/adr/` is outside the writable `docs/plans/`; the human writes the approved ADR themselves or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off` — the agent never writes it while the design phase is gated.)\n7. **Write the design doc** — validate its structure before handing off; before writing either a trivial or non-trivial doc, read [references/design-format.md](references/design-format.md) for the exact format, tag defaults, risk/Setup rules, and audit. Requirement blocks carry acceptance criteria plus `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags. Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`. Write `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md`, creating the topic folder when absent. It is descriptive, not a task list; the executor builds directly from it.\n\n   **Completion gate:** Test observable behavior through the public interface. Audit every requirement's criteria, tags, and risk notes; confirm each appears exactly once. A criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; a criterion with no nameable probe sends the requirement back for splitting or rephrasing, and design-doc criteria never name tests — the probe materializes at execution. For non-trivial work, finish with end-to-end `## Feature acceptance` as the primary enforced spec. If writing a scenario step would require inventing behavior, that invention goes back through the assumption gate — an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement, not permission to guess. Risk notes never set the tag — the written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it, and only the human tags a slice for review.  ].join(\"\\n\");\n  assert.deepEqual(summarize(text), {\n    levels: { info: 2, error: 1 },\n    first: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\n    last: \"2026-01-03T00:00:00Z\",\n  });\n});\n\ntest(\"ignores Keep the design descriptive, not a task list. It is the single buildable artifact; no separate implementation plan.\n\n## Trivial format\n\nA trivial design has an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach in plain words), a single `### R1:` block with acceptance criteria and tags, and optional `## Production-risk areas`. It has no `## At a glance`, `## Requirements`, or `## Feature acceptance`; its ship gate is the full existing suite, not a manufactured E2E. Use the block rules below for its criteria, tags, and risk notes.\n\n```markdown\n# Design: <topic>\n\nIn short: <what + why + approach>\n\n### R1: <name>\n<observable behavior>\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given <state>, When <action>, Then <observable outcome>.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n```\n\n## Non-trivial format\n\n**Open with `## At a glance`** — the human's two-minute digest, immediately before `## Requirements`. It contains (1) a 2–4 sentence plain-language summary: what is wrong or needed, what will be built, the key approach in plain words; (2) **Key decisions** — one line each: decision + why, with a `(rejected: <alternative> — <reason>)` clause only when the fork was real and load-bearing (never manufactured — no fork, no clause); (3) a table `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |` with exactly one row per requirement, where **R# = the requirement's block number in the `## Requirements` section below** — this ID is what every later digest keys on (progress rows, execution summary, reviewer coverage table). Plain language only: short sentences, no jargon, no Given/When/Then — those live in the requirement blocks for the executor. An umbrella overview gains no at-a-glance section; its roster already serves that role.\n\nThen **`## Requirements`** — one `### R<n>: <name>` block per requirement, each one testable behavior:\n\n```markdown\n## Requirements\n\n### R1: <name>\n<one-line testable behavior — what the feature produces or changes, through its public interface>\n\n**Acceptance criteria** — Given/When/Then criteria defining \"done\". Test observable behavior — what the feature produces or changes through its public interface; not implementation steps. Cover edge and error cases.\n- Given … When … Then …\n- Given … When … Then … (edge case)\n\n### Checkpoints: none | full\n### Review: skip | parallel | inline\n\n### Production-risk notes\n- <only when the requirement touches a risk area>\n\n### R2: <name>\n…\n```\n\nBlock rules:\n\n- **No test-name lists.** The criteria are the test spec — the executor writes and names the actual tests red-green from them, so the doc contains no test-name lists and no R#-to-section mapping tables: the block structure is the map.\n- **Tag every requirement** — `### Checkpoints` (how many human stops: `none` = no per-requirement stop, the default — the feature gate covers it; `full` = tests + complete stops) and `### Review` (per-requirement review: `skip` = none, the default; `parallel` = four delegated reviewers; `inline` = one `pwk-code-review` pass). Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`. Flag `full` only where complex logic or the main part of the feature makes a human look at the slice worth the stop.\n- **Nothing is tagged silently here; only the human tags a slice for review.** A requirement that touches a production-risk area carries its `### Production-risk notes` in the block and is flagged `⚠ production-risk` in the At-a-glance Risk column (the column is derived, **display-only**: `⚠ production-risk` if and only if the block carries non-empty `### Production-risk notes`, else `—` — never normative, never an input; `auto` reads the underlying risk content — the `## Production-risk areas` section and the notes — never the display column), but its written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it — propose the tag in prose, leave the field at `skip`. An explicit human tag always wins, in both directions.\n- **No per-requirement spec stop, by design** — the acceptance criteria are approved right here, at design time; re-checking them mid-execution asks a question the human already answered.\n- **Production-risk notes** — a requirement touching a production-risk area carries its notes inside the block. Risks involving schema migrations, new dependencies, external APIs, or seed data also get a `## Setup` section (dependencies, migrations, seed data, and how to verify setup worked) between `## Requirements` and `## Feature acceptance`.\n- **Ordering** — dependencies come earlier in the list; the executor runs blocks in listed order with no dependency graph. Aim for vertical slices that merge cleanly on their own.\n\nThen the narrative sections the executor reads as context — problem, approaches considered, architecture, components, data flow, error handling. Head the approaches section exactly `## Approaches considered` — finalizing's learning sweep reads it by that name. **`## Approaches considered` records every real fork and why each loser lost** — the executor needs the reasoning, and the finalize learning sweep harvests it for ADRs.\n\nTouches a production-risk area (DB schema/migrations, auth, external APIs, concurrency/batch, uploads/large data flows, Redis/caching/queues)? Add a brief `## Production-risk areas` **immediately after the last requirement block** — inside the `### R1 → ## Feature acceptance` span, so the review packet carries it to reviewers verbatim — and mirror the risks into each touched block's `### Production-risk notes`. `pwk-code-review` audits it, per requirement when the slice is reviewed and at the feature review always; finalize's learning sweep reads it.\n\n**End with `## Feature acceptance`** — one or more end-to-end `Given/When/Then` scenarios proving the requirements *compose* into the feature. This is the feature's definition-of-done; the human approves it as what \"the feature works\" means. `pwk-executing-tasks` writes it as the E2E test first and runs it as the **primary enforced spec** (the test it gates on first). The section carries the feature-level `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline` tag — the one whole-feature review; default `auto`, which resolves on the design's own production-risk content to `parallel` (all four reviewers) when the design has any — a non-empty `## Production-risk areas` section, or a non-empty `### Production-risk notes` on any requirement — and to `inline` (one pass) otherwise. An explicit `parallel` or `inline` is written as-is, never resolved, so the human always overrides `auto`. Treat \"I can write this scenario\" as the green light to finish designing — if you can't, keep designing because the requirements don't yet compose into a coherent feature. If writing a scenario step would require inventing behavior, that invention goes back through the assumption gate — it may never be silently written into the scenario; an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement, so keep designing.\n\n```markdown\n## Feature acceptance\n\n- Given <starting state>, When <trigger>, Then <end-to-end outcome the feature promises>.\n\n### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline — the one whole-feature review; leave `auto` unless the human says otherwise.\n```\n\nExample (rate limiting): \"Given a new API consumer with no prior usage, When they exceed 100 requests/minute for 3 consecutive minutes, Then they're throttled, a `rate_limited` event is emitted, and further requests return 429.\"\n\n**Audit before finishing:** every requirement block has acceptance criteria and both tags, and each requirement appears **exactly once** — none dropped, none duplicated. A `## Feature acceptance` section exists as the primary enforced spec — on every non-trivial doc; a trivial doc ends after its `### R1:` block and ships on the full suite instead. Production-risk areas are reflected in the requirement blocks that touch them. The probe test: a criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; a criterion with no nameable probe sends the requirement back for splitting or rephrasing; criteria never name tests — the probe materializes at execution. A fact settled by a sketch carries its proof where it lands — `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` — woven into the section it confirms, never a new template section.\n\n## Structural validator contract\n\nRun `scripts/validate-design.py` as directed in the main skill. It reads UTF-8 Markdown without modifying it. Headings, tags, and labels inside backtick or tilde fenced examples do not count; close every fence. Real requirements use unique sequential `### R1: <name>`, `### R2: <name>`, … headings with nonempty names. Each block needs a standalone `**Acceptance criteria**` label in its main body, before any tag or risk-note heading (an explanatory suffix after an em dash, dash, or colon is allowed) and nonempty criteria before the next heading or bold section label. A bare bullet or content borrowed from risk notes is not a criterion section.\n\nWrite each selected tag as one value, not the template's pipe-separated alternatives. Missing optional tags retain `Checkpoints: none`, `Review: skip`, and `Feature review: auto`. Non-trivial designs require nonempty `## Feature acceptance` scenarios before their feature-review tag. Only the minimal trivial shape above receives the no-Feature-acceptance exception.\n\nThe helper checks structure, not meaning: it does not prove Given/When/Then quality, testability, complete edge/error coverage, good slicing, risk classification, confirmed assumptions, or human approval. Those remain the agent's audit and the human's judgment. Structural success does not complete the design gate by itself.\n==> text 2/2 <==\n/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/references:\ntotal 32\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 4 yinlootan  staff   128 Oct 14 18:43 .\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 5 yinlootan  staff   160 Oct 14 18:43 ..\n-rw-r--r--@ 1 yinlootan  staff  9790 Oct 14 18:43 design-format.md\n-rw-r--r--@ 1 yinlootan  staff  2764 Oct 14 18:43 umbrella.md\n\n/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/scripts:\ntotal 24\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 3 yinlootan  staff    96 Oct 14 18:43 .\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 5 yinlootan  staff   160 Oct 14 18:43 ..\n-rw-r--r--@ 1 yinlootan  staff  9070 Oct 14 18:43 validate-design.py\nPython 3.14.3\n"}],"details":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_2ZdfIs5VB5etBSzqvOAy8983/1","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/references/design-format.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":0.8175419999897713},{"id":"call_00_2ZdfIs5VB5etBSzqvOAy8983/2","name":"bash","args":"{\"command\":\"ls -la \\\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/scripts\\\" \\\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/references\\\"; python3 --ve...","status":"ok","durationMs":16.532500000001164}]},"isError":false,"durationMs":44,"timestamp":1791976822578,"nestedCalls":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_2ZdfIs5VB5etBSzqvOAy8983/1","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/references/design-format.md"},"durationMs":1},{"id":"call_00_2ZdfIs5VB5etBSzqvOAy8983/2","name":"bash","status":"ok","arguments":{"command":"ls -la \"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/scripts\" \"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-brainstorming/references\"; python3 --version","timeout":20},"durationMs":17}],"complete":true}}}

the CLI extracts the flag from argv and delegates. Tests drive\n  the function directly and the CLI path is exercised once end-to-end.\n- **CLI-only filtering (rejected).** The cutoff would be applied inside the argv branch and every\n  boundary case would be tested by spawning a child process — slower and noisier for no extra\n  coverage, and it would leave the filtering behavior outside the module's public surface.\n- **A separate \\`filterSince(text, since)\\` export composed by the caller (rejected).** Two public\n  functions where one optional option serves the single behavior under test; it also splits the\n  cut-off decision away from the counting that consumes it.\n- **Loose \\`Date.parse\\` validation (rejected).** Settled by sketch:\n  \\`node -e\\` on Node v24.21.0 → \\`Date.parse(\"2026\")\\` and \\`Date.parse(\"2026-1-4\")\\` both return\n  timestamps, while \\`\"\"\\`, \\`\"fox\"\\`, and \\`\"2026-13-45\"\\` return NaN — so a NaN-only check would\n  accept non-ISO values and make the documented contract meaningless.\n- **String comparison instead of parsed instants (rejected).** Settled by sketch:\n  \\`[\"2026-01-04T09:05:00+02:00\",\"2026-01-04T08:00:00Z\"].sort()\\` puts the offset form last even\n  though it is the earlier instant, so lexicographic comparison gets the boundary wrong.\n\n## Architecture and data flow\n\n\\`\\`\\`js\nsummarize(text, { since } = {}) // since: optional ISO-8601 string; throws RangeError if invalid\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n1. **Validation (once, up front).** If \\`since\\` is provided, it must match a strict ISO-8601 shape\n   (date-only or a timestamp, optional fractional seconds, optional \\`Z\\`/offset) and\n   \\`Date.parse\\` it must not be NaN; otherwise \\`summarize\\` throws \\`RangeError\\`. Missing-value\n   detection for a bare \\`--since\\` is the CLI's job, since the function only sees a value.\n2. **Per-line pass.** Blank lines are skipped as today. Each remaining line is parsed as JSON;\n   when a cutoff is set, an entry whose \\`time\\` is absent or does not parse to an instant at or\n   after the cutoff is skipped entirely (no level count, no range contribution). Entries that\n   survive are counted into \\`levels\\` and push their raw \\`time\\` string into \\`times\\`.\n3. **Range.** \\`times.sort()\\` and the \\`[0]\\` / \\`[last]\\` selection are untouched, so first/last\n   remain raw strings and the reported range is over the included set only.\n\n**CLI.** A small scan over \\`argv\\` pulls out \\`--since\\` plus its following argument and leaves the\nfirst remaining positional argument as the file path (default \\`fixtures/events.jsonl\\`, extra\npositionals ignored as today). Before calling \\`summarize\\`, a \\`--since\\` with no following value is\nreported as a usage error. The \\`summarize\\` call is wrapped so a thrown \\`RangeError\\` becomes\n\\`log-summary: invalid --since date: \"<value>\"\\` on stderr followed by \\`process.exit(2)\\`; any other\nerror propagates exactly as it does today (unhandled → exit 1).\n\n**Known limitation (unchanged by this work).** The existing range selection sorts raw strings, so\nwith mixed timezone offsets \\`first\\`/\\`last\\` can disagree with the epoch-based filtering. All\nfixture and test data uses \\`Z\\` timestamps, where the two agree; fixing the range ordering is out\nof scope here and deliberately left alone so this diff stays behavior-preserving without a cutoff.\n\n## Error handling\n\n- Invalid or missing \\`--since\\` value → stderr message naming the problem, exit 2, no stdout. Run after pwk-brainstorming. Per-requirement checkpoints/reviews are opt-in (default off).\"\n---\n\n# Executing Tasks\n\nImplement the design doc found under `docs/plans/` via the **feature-gate flow**. The design doc is the single buildable artifact — its `### R<n>` blocks carry each requirement's acceptance criteria and tags. The criteria define *what*, you decide *how*: structure, signatures, internals are yours.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\nThe feature-acceptance E2E test is the primary enforced gate and the primary enforced spec for the feature. The flow is always on: write the E2E first (red), implement the requirements back-to-back, then run the feature review and pause at the **ship checkpoint** — one fully-informed stop where you present the execution summary and the reviewer coverage table, with the full diff on request. Per-requirement checkpoints and reviews are **opt-in** — they fire only for requirements the design doc tags (default off); the feature gate covers everything else. A trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`, per brainstorming's proportionality rule) skips the E2E steps and ships on the full suite; the one whole-feature review still runs at its ship checkpoint, its missing `### Feature review` tag defaulting to `auto`.\n\n## Before you start\n\nResolve local references and scripts from this installed skill directory. If a required resource is missing, report the blocker and stop before the affected action; do not silently skip its instructions.\n\n1. **Git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`; note uncommitted changes.\n2. **Find the doc** — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; take each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   If no doc at all, ask the user to run `/skill:pwk-brainstorming` first; if several, ask which. Report one line, e.g. `Found: design \"auth\" — feature-gate execute (E2E written, implementing 2/5)`. A matching `*-progress.md` means this is a **resume** (see [Resume and progress](#resume-and-progress)). An umbrella part whose prior leaves are not all at `done`: surface their `Feature phase:` lines (matched header-only from each `<leaf>-progress.md`) as advisory context in the pre-flight report — no refusal, no reorder; build order stays advisory.\n3. **Workspace — choose this topic’s branch/worktree.** Before creating, switching, or adopting one, read [Workspace and resume details](references/resume.md#workspace). Reuse this topic’s branch (one umbrella = one branch); a different topic’s branch never hosts these commits. Uncommitted planning docs do not cross a worktree boundary: commit this topic folder on its branch before a new worktree handoff; when adopting an existing checkout with uncommitted docs here, copy the topic folder there, verify it, then remove the source copy. Read the reference's command order before acting. Offer/adopt only after checking existing worktrees; wait for the user's choice.\n\n## First run\n\n1. **Parse the design doc** — read every `### R<n>:` heading and its `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags (defaults `none` / `skip`), plus the feature-level `### Feature review` tag in the `## Feature acceptance` section. Requirements run in **listed order** (build order); do not reorder. Read the `## Feature acceptance` section — it is the E2E you gate on first. A trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`) skips steps 5–6 below and goes straight into the implement phase.\n2. **Create the progress file** beside the design at `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md`. Before creating it, read [Progress format](references/progress-format.md) for the exact template, header slots, and row vocabulary. Start at `Feature phase: e2e-written` (trivial doc: `implementing (0/N)`); `Setup: pending` when the design has `## Setup`, otherwise `Setup: n/a`.\n\n3. **Setup pre-flight** *(only if the design doc has a `## Setup` section)* — install dependencies, apply migrations, seed data, then run the existing test suite. **⏸ CHECKPOINT: setup** — present results and wait for approval, then set `Setup: done` in the progress-file header so a resume can confirm it rather than assume it.\n\n4. **Commit the design docs** — `git add docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ && git commit -m \"docs: add design doc\"`. The add is scoped to the topic folder so another in-flight topic's uncommitted drafts never ride this commit (docs/lessons.md hygiene: one commit per topic).\n5. **Write the feature-acceptance E2E test (red).** Read the design doc's `## Feature acceptance` section and encode it as a real test file; run it; confirm it **fails** (it must — little or none of the feature exists yet). If it passes immediately, probe why before proceeding: the behavior may already exist, or the test may be asserting too little. If it still passes and the expected behavior looks wrong, **stop and present** rather than implementing against a wrong spec. Iterate it to green as you implement — fixing the implementation is the default, and you **stop and present only when you are genuinely blocked** (nothing you can do makes it pass, or the E2E itself is wrong). That stop is the reserved failure case; it is not the flow's default pause.\n6. **Notice, not a stop — report the E2E and continue.** Post 1–2 plain-language lines stating **what the E2E proves** (\"this test proves that …\"), plus the E2E test and its failing output, then go straight into the implement phase **without waiting for approval** — the `## Feature acceptance` text was approved during brainstorm, so there is nothing new here for the human to sign off. The notice is the window to object *before* implementation starts: a human who sees the E2E asserting the wrong thing says so, and you revise, re-run, and re-notice. Keep `Feature phase: e2e-written`.\n\n## Resume and progress\n\n`Feature phase` is one of: `e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`.\n\n**Done cell:** `⬜` not started · `🔄` in progress · `✅` done · `❌` failed · `⏭` skipped. A row is **terminal** when its Done cell is `✅`, `❌`, or `⏭` — resolved, not necessarily passed. Only executing changes Done cells; a requirement under review stays `🔄` until a clean pass permits `✅`.\n\nWhen a matching progress file exists, read [Resume](references/resume.md#resume) before routing. Read the header, Requirements table, and Execution summary only; `ship-paused` also needs Code digest. A pending setup checkpoint must be re-verified and approved before proceeding. Resume the first nonterminal row (`⬜`, `🔄`, blank); `✅`/`❌`/`⏭` are terminal, resolved rather than necessarily passed. Match `grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>` for the phase header; `reviewing` resumes review; `ship-paused` re-presents and waits, never approves itself. Missing reviewer reports require review again before showing coverage.\n\nBefore any progress-row update or code-digest write, read [Progress format](references/progress-format.md). Update the matching row directly, `Last updated`, and `Feature phase`; write execution-summary content at the same time as ✅, and deviations at deviation time. A failed/skipped row carries its reason in the Requirement cell and reconciles its test coverage so the suite stays green.\n\n## Implement phase\n\nBugs found mid-execution are mandatory execution-summary content: record the fix in the requirement's `How it was built` cell and fill its Deviated? column at fix time — the summary must show what the feature actually cost to land.\n\nSet `Feature phase: implementing (0/N)` and work the requirements in listed order. For each:\n\n1. **Mark the requirement 🔄** (Done column), read its `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags, and check `docs/lessons.md` for a rule that applies to this slice.\n2. **Write a meaningful test (red), then implement (green)** — TDD discipline. Encode the requirement's acceptance criteria as a real test through the public interface; run it; confirm it fails; implement to green. Skip the per-slice test only when the slice has no independent observable behavior (the feature E2E covers it). Follow the meaningful-test rules: (1) **Test observable behavior** — assert on what the feature produces or changes (a return value, persisted/updated data, an emitted event, an HTTP response) through its public interface; these assertions keep passing as the implementation changes. (2) **Write a per-slice test when the slice has its own observable behavior** — when a slice is pure config or a trivial extraction, the feature E2E covers it and a per-slice test is unnecessary. (Mirrored in `pwk-brainstorming` and `docs/lessons.md`.)\n3. **⏸ per-requirement checkpoint** *(fires only when the tag says so — opt-in)* — if `### Checkpoints: full`, stop and present after the tests and again after the slice is complete — both before its commit (the checkpoint rule below forbids committing before approval). With the default `none`, show the red→green inline and proceed.\n4. **Regression check after each commit** — run the **full existing suite**. This is what catches cross-requirement regressions (a later requirement breaking an earlier one's test). The **feature E2E stays red until the last requirement lands**; you may run it to watch the failure point advance, but it is gated only at the ship checkpoint — never expect it green per-commit.\n5. **Learn.** Caught a repeat mistake? Append a **generic** rule to `docs/lessons.md` (strip domain specifics).\n6. **Commit** the requirement with a clear message; record the requirement's commit hash in the Commit column.\n7. **Per-requirement review** *(fires only when the requirement's `### Review` tag is `parallel` or `inline` — default `skip`)* — review the slice now (see [Per-requirement review](#per-requirement-review-opt-in)); the row stays 🔄 through the review.\n8. **Mark the requirement ✅** and write its execution-summary row in the same step — Evidence cell non-empty, plain words plus pointer; advance `Feature phase: implementing (k/N)`. With `skip`, no per-requirement review — step 8 fires directly, and the feature-level review covers it.\n\nWith the default `none`, no per-requirement stop fires — the per-requirement test still runs red→green, and the feature review covers implementation quality.\n\n### Checkpoint gates are mandatory (when the tag says so)\n\nWhen a per-requirement checkpoint fires it is a **hard stop**:\n- Stop immediately; never proceed without explicit human approval.\n- **Never** `git add` or `git commit` before approval at a checkpoint.\n- Set the progress phase/status **before** pausing.\n\n## Ship checkpoint (all requirements terminal + review, merged)\n\nWhen every requirement's Done cell is terminal — `✅` (done), `❌` (failed, reason in row), or `⏭` (skipped, reason in row):\n\n1. **Run the FULL test suite** — a failure means one requirement regressed another; fix it now, in execute context.\n2. **Run the feature-acceptance E2E** — the test you wrote at the start. (A `❌`/`⏭` requirement's assertions were reconciled when its row went terminal, so a still-red E2E still means a requirement is missing or wrong.) If it is still red, a requirement is missing or wrong — fix it before proceeding. (A trivial design doc has no `## Feature acceptance` — the full suite staying green is its gate instead.)\n3. **Run the feature review** (below) per the design's `### Feature review` tag — set `Feature phase: reviewing` first, so a mid-review resume routes into this step instead of the implement loop. Apply smell fixes yourself and re-green (full suite + E2E) before pausing.\n4. **Write the code digest** into the progress file — the review has succeeded, findings are fixed, and the code is final: read the packet's `## Commits`, `## Changed files`, and `## Diff` sections and fill the progress file's `## Code digest` using [Progress format](references/progress-format.md) and its fill rules. This reference owns the unchanged progress artifact schema.\n\n2. **Create the progress file** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md`, beside the design doc it belongs to (`<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic; an umbrella part uses its roster slug), so `pwk-finalizing` finds it inside the topic folder. Fill rules: plain language, R# anchors where natural, no test names (the execution-summary rule). `### Summary` is 2–3 sentences: what the code now does differently, and why. `### Flow` uses `A -> B -> C` arrow chains, one spine or branch per bullet line, so every renderer shows each hop chain on its own line — bare label lines would merge into one run-on paragraph. `### Gotchas` lifts real risks from the review findings, one bullet each — `[ALERT]` only for reviewer-confirmed issues, never invented; with no findings, write `none beyond review findings` and mean it. `### Key files` is capped at 5 pivotal files, one bullet each: what shifted inside them.\n\n   **Flow shape** — this is the ship stop's navigable map, so it is the one digest section that carries structure, not just prose:\n\n   - **Spine** — the happy path as `A -> B -> C` hops, each hop named by symbol or module, with no line numbers anywhere and no file paths: symbol names survive edits and stay greppable, so a stale anchor can never mislead. Tag each hop `[R<n>]` with the requirement it comes from — that is what lets the coverage table's verdict rows be traced into the code without opening the diff.\n   - **Branches** — every alternative and error path as `condition -> outcome` (a linear spine with no branches reads as \"there are no edge cases\", which is rarely true). Put ⚠️ on the genuinely surprising ones. Add a `was: <previous behavior>` clause for each requirement whose behavior changed; skip it for purely additive requirements — honest-empty, never invented.\n   - **Inline worked values** — where a mapping is non-obvious, show it concretely (`` `implementing (2/5)` -> `execute 2/5` ``), so a reader can falsify it without running anything.\n   - **Side effects** — a bullet naming what is read and written, only when the feature performs I/O, network, or migrations; omit it entirely otherwise rather than filling a placeholder.\n   - **Cap: roughly 15 lines.** If the change genuinely needs more, the ship checkpoint **offers `/skill:pwk-walkthrough`** as the deep read (it regenerates a `file:line`-anchored walkthrough on demand) instead of growing the digest — the digest is what the human reads at the one remaining stop, and an unbounded Flow recreates the digging it exists to prevent.\n\n   `Feature phase` is one of: `e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`.\n\n   The `Setup:` header slot takes one of `Setup: pending | done | n/a` — the header starts `Setup: pending` when the design doc has a `## Setup` section, else `Setup: n/a`; the main skill's setup checkpoint flips it to `done` on approval. The phase line stays `e2e-written` through the setup stop — the Setup slot, not the phase, is what flags the not-yet-approved window, and the E2E is written after setup.\n\n\n## Progress file\n\nUpdate the matching requirement row directly (not via pattern matching that could corrupt the table). Update `Last updated` and `Feature phase` on every change.\n\n**Row vocabulary (canonical — this file owns it):**\n\n- **Done cell:** `⬜` not started · `🔄` in progress · `✅` done · `❌` failed · `⏭` skipped. A row is **terminal** when its Done cell is `✅`, `❌`, or `⏭` — resolved, not necessarily passed. A `❌`/`⏭` row carries its reason as a suffix in the Requirement cell (finalizing's verdict greps read it), and its test coverage is reconciled in the same step — assertions removed or skipped with the reason; the suite must stay green. This skill sets all five values. A requirement under review stays `🔄`: `pwk-code-review` reports findings and never edits the Done cell — the loop only ever flips `🔄`→`✅` when the review returns clean, and findings leave the row `🔄` for another pass.\n- **Per-req ceremony cell** echoes the design doc's tag, not progress: `—` (default `none`/`skip`) · `⏸ full` (fires two stops — after the slice's tests and after it is complete) · `🔎 inline` · `🔎 parallel`.\n\n**Execution summary rows are written in the same step as marking a requirement ✅** — never retrofitted at the end. \"How it was built\" = one or two plain sentences: what it does now + the approach actually taken; file names sparingly; **no test-name lists, no code** (the human reads this at the ship checkpoint — big picture only; the `Evidence` cell may name **one probe test**, never a list). The `Evidence` cell pairs **what it proves in plain words** with a pointer — a commit, a `file:line`, a command with its observed output line, or the single probe test — single-line so the table never breaks. No requirement is marked ✅ with an empty `Evidence` cell: either the pointer exists or the requirement is not done. If the implementation departs from the design, fill the Deviated? column **at deviation time** (when the departure happens), with a one-line why — it is a log, not a stop. A departure that **reverses or alters a design decision** gets a **deviation decision-record**: a short paragraph (what changed, why, what was rejected) written into the progress file while the knowledge is fresh — mechanical deviations keep the one-liner. `pwk-finalizing`'s learning sweep harvests these records for ADRs before the docs are disposed.\n\n\n## Commit entries for packet assembly\n\nRecord immutable hexadecimal commit IDs (7–64 characters). A cell can hold one ID or an ordered, whitespace-separated list: initial implementation first, review-fix commits last. Preserve the first recorded commit when appending a fix; replacing it loses the feature base. Record a commit hash after committing, never amend a commit to include its own hash.\n\nThe helper reads only the Requirements table Commit column. A done or in-review row needs a recorded commit. Terminal `❌`/`⏭` rows may have `—` when no commit remains; this does not supply a bound for a requirement packet. If the selected or immediately previous requirement lacks a bound, stop and correct the record from Git evidence; never invent one.\n==> text 2/3 <==\n===== resume.md =====\n# Workspace and resume details\n\nRead before choosing or adopting a topic branch/worktree, and whenever a matching progress file exists.\n\n## Workspace\n\n3. **Workspace — create the feature branch** — if you're already on **this topic's** feature branch, **reuse** it: a later umbrella part continues on the same umbrella branch as part 1. If on `main` — or on a different topic's feature branch, which stays that topic's own and never hosts this topic's commits — create or switch to this topic's branch: `git checkout <topic>` when it exists, else `git checkout -b <topic>` — the topic's folder slug (the `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` directory name, shared by every leaf of an umbrella), never a leaf slug. **`<topic>` is the folder slug** everywhere it appears in this skill, including the `../<repo>-<topic>` worktree convention below, so a standalone topic and an umbrella part name the same branch and the same worktree. For larger work, first check `git worktree list`: if a worktree already checks out this branch (the same `../<repo>-<topic>` convention), adopt it — resume the session there instead of offering a new `git worktree add`. One worktree per branch, created once: git refuses two checkouts of one branch, so a later umbrella part reuses part 1's worktree and a standalone resume reuses its own. Otherwise offer a worktree (`git worktree add ../<repo>-<topic> <topic>`) and hand off to a new session there so `pwd` is the worktree. **Uncommitted planning docs do not cross a worktree boundary**, and the design doc is still uncommitted (brainstorm never commits): when the user takes the worktree, commit the topic folder on this branch first — the same scoped add as the main skill's First-run commit — then switch this tree back to the branch it came from (e.g. `git checkout main` when it started there; git refuses `worktree add` of a branch that is still checked out here) and only then `git worktree add ../<repo>-<topic> <topic>` and hand off (the new session's First-run commit then has only its progress file to record). The adopt path above is safe only when the docs are already committed on the branch; if this tree holds uncommitted topic docs while another worktree holds the branch checkout, git refuses to commit to the branch from here — copy the topic folder into that worktree's `docs/plans/`, verify with `ls`, and remove the source copy before handing off. Wait for the user's choice.\n\n## Resume\n\nRead the progress file's `Feature phase` (match the line — e.g. `grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`), the Requirements table (the first row whose Done cell is not terminal routes the next requirement — `⬜`, `🔄`, and blank all mean not-done; `✅`/`❌`/`⏭` are resolved and are skipped past), and the Execution summary rows (how prior parts were built); read from the top through the end of `## Execution summary` and stop — the sections after it (deviation records, code digest) carry nothing the resume needs, with one exception: the `ship-paused` route re-presents the ship checkpoint, so it also reads the `## Code digest` written in the progress file. Before routing: if the header reads `Setup: pending` and the design doc has a `## Setup` section, the setup checkpoint was never approved — re-run the setup verification and wait at it:\n- `e2e-written` → write the E2E if not yet present, post the notice, and continue into the implement phase (no stop). A trivial design doc has no `## Feature acceptance` — skip both and go straight into the implement phase.\n- `implementing (k/N)` → continue the next not-yet-terminal requirement.\n- `reviewing` → continue/finish the feature review, then assemble the **ship** checkpoint.\n- `ship-paused` → re-present the ship checkpoint and wait — the execution summary, verdict rows, and code digest re-read from the progress file; if the prior session's reviewer reports are gone, re-run the feature review per the tag first (the checkpoint is never presented without coverage).\n==> text 3/3 <==\n===== review.md =====\n# Review mechanics and packet helper\n\nRead before any feature or opt-in requirement review, before refreshing a packet, and before writing the code digest from review evidence.\n\n## Assemble evidence\n\n**Assemble the review packet first** — once, by script, so that no packet byte passes through model output (spawn arguments are model output; file reads are not). The Commit column is the packet's source of truth for both spans: the feature packet base is `git rev-parse <first Commit-column entry>^` (the parent of the first recorded commit); a per-requirement packet spans from the previous requirement's last commit (exclusive) to this requirement's last commit (inclusive), with R1's exclusive bound being its own parent. No `merge-base` guessing, no default-branch knowledge. If commits land while the review is in flight, re-run the recipe before spawning any replacement role so the packet matches HEAD:\n\nUse the installed skill directory, not a repository checkout of the kit. First verify `python3 --version` reports Python 3.9 or newer and that the helper exists. Missing runtime/resource → report the dependency and stop this step. No runtime auto-install or alternate-language fallback.\n\n```sh\npython3 \"<executing-skill-dir>/scripts/build-review-packet.py\" \\\n  --project \"<repo-root>\" \\\n  --design \"docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md\" \\\n  --progress \"docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md\" \\\n  --scope feature\n```\n\nFor an opt-in requirement review, use the same invocation with `--scope requirement --requirement 2` (substitute the selected number). The feature destination is `<design doc's directory>/<leaf>-review-packet.md`; the requirement destination is `<design doc's directory>/<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`. Requirement-suffixed packets never overwrite each other or the feature packet.\n\n`--project` resolves from the caller's cwd and must name the Git worktree root. Design/progress arguments are absolute or relative to that project, regardless of the current directory or installed skill location. Both must be matched leaf files inside one active `docs/plans/<topic>/` folder. The helper derives the destination; symlink destinations are refused. Use argument lists in programmatic invocations, never shell interpolation.\n\nThe packet retains these sections, in order:\n- `## Commits`\n- `## Changed files`\n- `## Acceptance criteria (verbatim from the design doc)`\n- `## Feature acceptance (verbatim)` (empty for a trivial design)\n- `## Production-risk notes (verbatim, if any)`\n- `## Diff`\n\nCriteria and production-risk content remain verbatim, including all lines in multiple risk blocks; fenced template headings do not route extraction. Feature criteria span from the first real requirement to Feature acceptance (or document end); requirement criteria include only the selected requirement block. Design-level production-risk areas are retained as review context. The packet header records fixed `Base:` and `Head:` IDs: feature uses the first recorded commit's parent through current HEAD; requirement uses the previous requirement's last recorded commit exclusively through the selected last recorded commit inclusively. The helper excludes generated `*-review-packet*.md` files from diff/stat, including committed packets.\n\nA Commit cell is one immutable hexadecimal ID or an ordered whitespace-separated list. Preserve the first ID; append review-fix IDs in order. Feature assembly permits missing commits only for terminal failed/skipped rows. Requirement assembly needs an explicit selected and previous bound; it refuses to guess across a failed/skipped row without a commit. Missing relevant rows, malformed/ambiguous entries, invalid revisions, or non-ancestral order → correct the record from evidence and rerun. The helper never edits progress, commits, switches branches, or marks anything approved. It finishes all parse/Git work before atomically replacing a complete packet. A nonzero exit is failure, not review evidence: report stderr and stop delegation; an older packet remains intact but may be stale.\n\nAfter late review fixes, commit them and append their IDs to the selected row before refreshing a requirement packet; feature packets refresh HEAD automatically. Re-run the helper before any replacement reviewer and before digest writing if stale or missing. Packet generation is evidence assembly, not review approval. Re-green the full suite + E2E after fixes, then complete review and the human checkpoint.\n\n## Delegate or review inline\n\n- **`parallel`** (the `auto` resolution when risk content is present) — request the host’s `parallel-review` capability for four fresh-context, read-only logical roles: `pwk-spec-reviewer`, `pwk-tracing-reviewer`, `pwk-smell-reviewer`, and `pwk-hazard-reviewer`. Spawn each role with a **one-liner** — a pointer to the packet file with the role framing appended last: the checklist name of the role (`spec alignment`, `code tracing`, `code smells`, or `production hazards`). For example: `Read docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-review-packet.md. Your role: spec alignment.` The packet never appears in spawn arguments. Require independent execution and one collected outcome per role. The reviewer role contracts live in `agents/pwk-*-reviewer.md`; do not duplicate their checklists in the workflow instructions. Reviewers are read-only reporters; you apply smell fixes yourself (full suite + E2E must stay green, commit) and flag trace/spec/hazard findings as follow-ups for the human.\n\n- **`inline`** — perform `/skill:pwk-code-review` over the whole diff as a single pass.\n- **Fallback** — if the host has no compatible parallel-review capability, cannot prove the requested read-only/fresh-context/bounded constraints, or delegation fails, perform the missing review work inline. Retain successful delegated reports and do not mark the feature fully reviewed while a required role is missing.\n"}],"details":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_1kAfwDeHl6ID0J2OqPey1900/1","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks/references/progress-format.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":1.501458000013372},{"id":"call_00_1kAfwDeHl6ID0J2OqPey1900/2","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks/references/resume.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":1.263875000004191},{"id":"call_00_1kAfwDeHl6ID0J2OqPey1900/3","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks/references/review.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":1.0901669999875594}]},"isError":false,"durationMs":27,"timestamp":1791976894172,"nestedCalls":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_1kAfwDeHl6ID0J2OqPey1900/1","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks/references/progress-format.md"},"durationMs":1},{"id":"call_00_1kAfwDeHl6ID0J2OqPey1900/2","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks/references/resume.md"},"durationMs":1},{"id":"call_00_1kAfwDeHl6ID0J2OqPey1900/3","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-baseline/skills/pwk-executing-tasks/references/review.md"},"durationMs":1}],"complete":true}}}
