+{"type":"message","id":"a593b824","parentId":"083d4f25","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:23:27.195Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_mHZrQirRBzfyzsbvz9mH1050","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.1 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"==> text 1/2 <==\nR2 commit: c0ec581\nc0ec581 feat: reject an unparseable --since value (R2)\n1e7c778 feat: filter log summary by --since cutoff (R1)\n9f08df4 docs: add design doc\n3ee03c7 fixture: log-summary script and tests\n==> text 2/2 <==\n===== code-review skill =====\n---\nname: pwk-code-review\ndescription: \"Review a completed requirement's code — trace the logic, check spec alignment against the acceptance criteria, fix code smells, and run a production hazard check. Runs as the feature-level review in pwk-executing-tasks (whole feature diff), or per-requirement when tagged. Unlocked: may edit code to apply smell fixes.\"\n---\n\n# Code Review\n\nReview the code just implemented — one tagged requirement, or the whole feature at the feature-level review. **Unlocked** — you may edit code to apply smell fixes; flag everything else as a follow-up.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Identify the scope** — in the feature-gate flow (the default), you review the **whole feature diff** at the feature-level review (`git diff $FEATURE_BASE...HEAD` — the parent of the first Commit-column entry; see the executing skill's packet recipe); all acceptance criteria in the design doc and the `## Feature acceptance` E2E are in scope. When invoked per-requirement (`Review: inline` on a tagged requirement — or inline-completing a missing delegated role when the tag is `parallel`), scope is just that requirement — read its acceptance criteria from the design doc, run `git log --oneline -5` and `git diff` to see what changed for it. Invoked standalone — no invoking skill, no design doc, no packet — review the span the user names (the working-tree diff, or the branch's commits against its parent branch): tracing, smell fixes, and the hazard check run as usual, while spec alignment has no acceptance criteria to key on — say so and judge the diff against its stated intent instead of manufacturing a coverage table. When the invoking skill already assembled a review packet (the feature packet, or the requirement-scoped `<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`), work from the packet — it is the scope of record; re-derive nothing the packet already states.\n\n2. **🔍 Code tracing** — trace the new or changed code paths end-to-end against the acceptance criteria and the feature E2E (a trivial design doc has no feature E2E — its acceptance criteria alone are the spec). For each path, determine whether data flows correctly from entry to the asserted outcome. Note any branch the tests do not exercise, any dead branch, or any path where the trace breaks.\n\n3. **📐 Spec alignment** — for each acceptance criterion, point to the code and the test that satisfy it. A criterion with no covering code or no test is a **gap**. Code that does more than the criteria specify is **scope creep** — flag it.\n\n   **Open the report with a coverage table** — one row per requirement in scope, keyed by the design doc's `### R<n>:` headings (R# = n; the whole design doc at the feature-level review, just the tagged requirement when invoked per-requirement):\n\n   | R# | Verdict | Evidence |\n   |----|---------|----------|\n   | 1 | <verdict> | file:line (code), file:line (test) |\n\n   Verdict per requirement: `covered | gap | scope-creep` — `covered` = every criterion has covering code and a test; `gap` = a criterion lacks code or a test; `scope-creep` = the code does more than the criteria specify. Findings elaborate on every non-`covered` row; an all-`covered` table needs no elaboration.\n\n4. **🧹 Code smells — fix these directly:** review the changed code and affected files against the requirement and feature scope, then fix what you find.\n   - Shallow modules (interface nearly as complex as implementation)\n   - Duplication\n   - Missing seams or premature abstraction\n   - Poor naming, magic values, dead code\n   Apply the fix, re-run the full suite (must stay green), and commit. Only a smell that requires a refactor large enough to risk the requirement is **flagged** instead of applied.\n\n5. **⚠️ Production hazard check** — audit the changed code against the high-risk hazards. For each, write `[SAFE]` (1-line justification) or `[TRIGGERED]` (concrete mitigation):\n   1. **Unbounded operations** — multi-key deletions/scans (`KEYS`, raw `SCAN` loops), full-table loads filtered in memory\n   2. **Missing indexes** — hot queries on unindexed columns (table scans under load)\n   3. **Unbounded concurrency** — unthrottled fan-out (`Promise.all` without batch limits)\n   4. **Long-running transactions** — holding DB connections/locks across slow external calls\n   5. **Query/command interpolation** — raw variables merged into SQL or shell (injection)\n   6. **Unrestricted uploads / temp flooding** — uploads to local temp without limits or `finally` cleanup\n   7. **Silent swallowing loops** — background workers catching/suppressing exceptions without logging/back-off\n   Also check the design's `## Production-risk areas`, if any.\n\n6. **Report** — summarize: tracing findings, spec gaps, smells fixed (with commits), hazards `[TRIGGERED]`. Non-trivial findings become follow-up items — the user decides whether to address now or defer.\n7. **Mark done** — the review never edits the progress file. A clean pass hands back so the executing loop can set the requirement's Done cell `✅` (the row was left `🔄` while under review) and write its execution-summary row; findings leave the row `🔄` for another pass. (At the feature-level review every row is already terminal — verify none regressed and move on.) Already-terminal rows of other requirements never regress. Done means reviewed, not just committed.\n\n## Principles\n\n- **Tracing and spec alignment are the core** — they catch what tests miss: untested branches, missing criteria, scope creep.\n- **Fix smells in place; flag everything else.** Keep the review scoped — the goal is polish on the requirement that just landed, not a redesign pass.\n- **Be proportional** — a one-function change doesn't need the depth of a batch pipeline. When this skill runs as the inline path because the design doc tagged the requirement `Review: inline`, that was a deliberate call at design approval — keep the review focused and don't second-guess the tag.\n\n## After the review\n\nReturn to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` — the next requirement, or the ship checkpoint when every requirement is done. Finalizing is proposed from the ship checkpoint, never from here. +{"type":"message","id":"702a0cbe","parentId":"944aedc4","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:28:15.269Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"<console_output>\n===== scripts/log-summary.mjs =====\n#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Summarize a JSONL event log: counts per level, plus the time range.\n\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nexport function summarize(text) {\n  const levels = {};\n  const times = [];\n  for (const line of text.split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n    if (!line.trim()) continue;\n    const event = JSON.parse(line);\n    levels[event.level] = (levels[event.level] ?? 0) + 1;\n    if (event.time) times.push(event.time);\n  }\n  times.sort();\n  return { levels, first: times[0] ?? null, last: times[times.length - 1] ?? null };\n}\n\nif (import.meta.url === new URL(`file://${process.argv[1]}`).href) {\n  const [, , file = \"fixtures/events.jsonl\"] = process.argv;\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(summarize(readFileSync(file, \"utf8\")), null, 2));\n}\n\n===== tests/log-summary.test.mjs =====\nimport assert from \"node:assert/strict\";\nimport { test } from \"node:test\";\nimport { summarize } from \"../scripts/log-summary.mjs\";\n\ntest(\"counts events per level and reports the time range\", () => {\n  const text = [\n    '{\"time\":\"2026-01-02T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\"}',\n    '{\"time\":\"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"error\"}',\n    '{\"time\":\"2026-01-03T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\"}',\n  ].join(\"\\n\");\n  assert.deepEqual(summarize(text), {\n    levels: { info: 2, error: 1 },\n    first: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\n    last: \"2026-01-03T00:00:00Z\",\n  });\n});\n\ntest(\"ignores blank lines\", () => {\n  assert.deepEqual(summarize('\\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"warn\"}\\n'), {\n    levels: { warn: 1 },\n    first: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\n    last: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\",\n  });\n});\n\n===== fixtures/events.jsonl =====\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:00:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\",\"msg\":\"started\"}\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:05:00Z\",\"level\":\"warn\",\"msg\":\"slow query\"}\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:06:00Z\",\"level\":\"error\",\"msg\":\"boom\"}\n{\"time\":\"2026-01-04T09:07:00Z\",\"level\":\"info\",\"msg\":\"recovered\"}\n\n===== README.md =====\n# pwk-probe-fixture\n\nA small project with one script and two tests, used as the `--since` fixture task in the\nskill-slimming fidelity/cost probe. No dependencies; `npm test` runs `node --test`.\n\n</console_output>"}],"details":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/1","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"scripts/log-summary.mjs\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":1.8847080000014103},{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/2","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"tests/log-summary.test.mjs\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":1.6245420000013837},{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/3","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"fixtures/events.jsonl\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":0.8714159999981348},{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/4","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"README.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":1.3977909999994154}]},"isError":false,"durationMs":36,"timestamp":1791977295269,"nestedCalls":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/1","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"scripts/log-summary.mjs"},"durationMs":2},{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/2","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"tests/log-summary.test.mjs"},"durationMs":2},{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/3","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"fixtures/events.jsonl"},"durationMs":1},{"id":"call_00_TBzx9CS93Qoy0cq7dKEy8925/4","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"README.md"},"durationMs":1}],"complete":true}}}

+{"type":"message","id":"b1796b22","parentId":"99b229c6","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:28:17.415Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_56Yjq7t16AJgQ330PJa25407","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"<console_output>\n---\nname: pwk-brainstorming\ndescription: \"Use this before any creative work — creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores intent and design, then writes the single buildable design doc (requirements with acceptance criteria + review tags) that pwk-executing-tasks builds from. Use this skill whenever the user describes something they want to build, change, or improve, even if they don't say 'brainstorm' — phrases like 'I want to add X', 'let's build Y', 'we need a way to Z', or 'help me design' all apply.\"\n---\n\n# Brainstorming\n\nRead-only exploration of source code; every file you create or edit goes under `docs/plans/`. An approved ADR goes to `docs/adr/` — outside the writable boundary, so the human writes it or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`, and the design phase never unlocks it. The design doc is the **single buildable artifact**: each requirement carries its own acceptance criteria and review tags, and the executor builds straight from it. Source-writing happens in `pwk-executing-tasks`.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Proportionality: trivial vs non-trivial\n\nClassify the change at the start.\n\n- **Trivial** — a typo or obvious bugfix with no open design questions, a config or version bump, a single-function change, or anything the human flags as trivial. Skip steps 3–6: read the design-format reference, run the validator in step 7, and write a **minimal** design doc in one turn — an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach), one `### R1:` block with criteria and tags, an optional `## Production-risk areas` line, and deliberately **no `## Feature acceptance`** (a trivial slice ships on the full existing suite; no E2E is manufactured). Hand off to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`. The guard still enforces read-only — trivial compresses the phase to one turn, it does not skip it.\n- **Non-trivial** — open design questions, multiple approaches, cross-module impact, or new behavior. Run the full process below.\n\nWhen unsure, ask: \"This looks trivial — fast-path it, or full brainstorm?\" Default to full.\n\n## Scope and granularity\n\n**One design doc = one PR; one requirement = one testable slice within it.** Most work is a single design doc; several requirements serving one cohesive outcome do not force an umbrella.\n\nA large request with distinct testable outcomes that need separate design/execute cycles becomes an **umbrella** of vertical slices with one-line scopes and a build order, approved before you write an overview or design. A layers-only split (database, API, UI) is not vertical — each slice delivers testable behavior. Design only the current slice, grounded in implemented code, not speculative sibling designs; the umbrella still ships as one PR on one branch, finalized once.\n\n**One folder per topic:** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/`, holding `<leaf>-design.md`, `<leaf>-progress.md`, and `<leaf>-review-packet*.md`; `<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic, and more than one leaf adds `overview.md`. The folder is the creation, discovery, and disposal unit.\n\n**Umbrella trigger:** before proposing a new umbrella, or when discovery finds an `overview.md` beside this design, read [references/umbrella.md](references/umbrella.md) — it owns the status-free roster, the first/later-slice procedures, and header-only predecessor reporting. Build order is advisory, not a gate, and an existing roster means the split is already decided; design the current slice against it.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Check git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`. Uncommitted work? Ask the user what to do first.\n2. **Discovery** *(skip in a brand-new repo with no `docs/plans/`)* — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md`, `*-progress.md`, and `overview.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; report in-flight topics and any active umbrella, each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`; design-only topics report `design` — no body ingest). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   If the idea continues an existing topic, ask whether to extend it or start fresh. An `overview.md` **beside the design doc** means the split is already decided — read it for the roster and design this part’s `<leaf>-design.md` against it.\n3. **Understand the idea** — **PRD brief.** With source material (a PRD, ticket, or spec — pasted text, a path, a URL), open with a brief before any question: **Background** (the problem, why now, who is affected — each product claim cites its PRD section), **Current situation** (what the code does today — each claim cites `file:line`), **The delta** (what must change, each line naming a requirement candidate, and what stays untouched). Zero-context rule: plain meaning first, the pointer second — quote non-English domain terms with a plain-English gloss and mark anything uncited `(interpretation: …)`. Unreadable source material: report the blocker, ground on code only, name the gap. The human corrects the brief before frontier rounds; confirmed facts weave into the design doc, with no sidecar file. No source material, no brief. Then read only enough code, docs, and commits to ground the design, and **check `docs/lessons.md`**.\n\n   Ask questions in **frontier rounds** — the frontier is every question whose prerequisites are settled. Build the tree by walking every checklist dimension (*Goal & scope · Data & state · Behavior & edge cases · Errors & failure · Integration · Non-functional*), print `— nothing to ask` for empty groups, and ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question (`Q1`, `Q2`, …) with your recommended answer (`➡️ <recommendation>`) so the human confirms, strikes, or corrects each in one reply. A question that depends on another still-open one waits for a later round; recompute the frontier after each round.\n\n   **Facts vs. decisions:** anything answerable from the codebase, docs, or tools is looked up — recon scout or inline — never asked of the human; a pending lookup holds only its downstream questions while the rest of the frontier is asked now. **Runnable facts:** an unknown observable by running something — behavior, timing, output, layout — is settled by a bounded sketch, never asked of the human and never guessed: an inline interpreter or a file under `docs/plans/<topic>/`, no installs, no source writes. Record it where it lands as `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` and list it in the round summary so the human can strike it; a sketch result that would set business behavior still passes the assumption gate; inconclusive or blocked → record `INCONCLUSIVE` plus one line of what ran, and the question returns to the human with the result attached. A cheaper read beats a run when reading can decide, and only decisions are asked.\n\n   Major approvals stay single-decision — one question each, never batched: approach selection (step 5), umbrella split, design approval, ADR offer. The interview ends when the frontier is empty — every branch visited, nothing left silently assumed — not when you feel you understand. Then present a short summary and ask: \"Should I proceed, or is there more?\" The human decides when to move on.\n4. **(skipped on trivial changes)** **Codebase recon** — for a non-trivial topic with prior art, request the host’s `codebase-recon` capability using the logical `pwk-recon-scout` role: a fresh-context, read-only, bounded worker given the topic, one-line intent, and repo root. Use its 5-section map (Relevant files, Existing patterns, Call sites, Test layout, Gotchas) as grounding for steps 5–6 instead of reading those files inline; the scout reports observations only, never design recommendations. No compatible capability, or constraints it cannot enforce → report `Scout: unavailable` and do the same recon inline, preserving the five-section map and `file:line` citations; never omit recon silently.\n5. **Explore approaches** — propose 2–3, leading with your recommendation, and sketch the concrete interface (types, signatures, example caller) for each so the comparison is grounded in code rather than abstractions.\n6. **Present the design** in one pass, organized into sections (architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing) — the human comments on any section; re-present only revised sections.\n\n   **Assumptions to confirm first** — before presenting, sweep the drafted design: every unconfirmed assumption it would bake in (business rules, defaults, edge-case resolutions) re-opens as a numbered question with your recommended answer, for one reply. An honest empty gate (\"no unconfirmed assumptions\") when the draft is clean — never invent items. Hard rule: no business behavior enters the design doc on the agent's assumption; confirmed facts are woven into existing sections, with no new template section.\n\n   Identified a significant architectural decision? Offer an ADR in `docs/adr/`, only when all three hold: **hard to reverse**, **surprising without context**, **a real trade-off**. Format: title + 1–3 sentences of context/decision/why. ADRs are permanent institutional memory — never archived or rotated. (Guard note: the human writes the approved ADR or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`; you never write it while the design phase is gated.)\n7. **Write the design doc** — validate its structure before handing off. Read [references/design-format.md](references/design-format.md) first for the exact format, tag defaults, risk/Setup rules, and audit; requirement blocks carry acceptance criteria plus `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags. Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`. Write `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md`, creating the topic folder when absent. It is descriptive, not a task list — the executor builds directly from it.\n\n   **Completion gate:** Test observable behavior through the public interface. Audit every requirement’s criteria, tags, and risk notes — each appears exactly once. A criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; a criterion with no nameable probe sends the requirement back for splitting or rephrasing, and design-doc criteria never name tests — the probe materializes at execution. For non-trivial work, finish with an end-to-end `## Feature acceptance` as the primary enforced spec. If writing a scenario step would require inventing behavior, that invention goes back through the assumption gate: an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement, not permission to guess. Risk notes never set the tag — the written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it, and only the human tags a slice for review. Keep designing until the requirements compose into a coherent feature and the human approves the design, including feature acceptance; trivial work keeps the compressed one-turn path above.\n\n   **Python prerequisite:** structural validation requires Python 3.9+ where commands execute, using only its standard library. Confirm a compatible `python3` exists before invoking the helper; if it is missing or too old, report the blocker and request a suitable runtime, then stop at this gate. Never auto-install Python, use a fallback implementation, or claim validation succeeded.\n\n   Resolve the helper from this installed skill’s directory and pass explicit paths, quoting paths with spaces:\n\n   ```sh\n   python3 \"<brainstorming-skill-dir>/scripts/validate-design.py\" \"<design-path>\"\n   ```\n\n   Nonzero means validation did not succeed: report file-specific diagnostics, correct the structural errors, and rerun. A missing local reference or helper is a blocker before its dependent action; success verifies structure only — never semantic correctness, sound slicing, confirmed assumptions, or human approval.\n\nThe session stays read-only and uncommitted through brainstorm: branch creation and the design-doc commit happen at the start of `pwk-executing-tasks`.\n\n## Principles\n\n- Detail-gathering asks in frontier rounds; approvals ask one decision at a time\n- No silent assumptions — ask, gate, or look it up\n- YAGNI — remove unnecessary features\n- Design for testability\n- Explore alternatives before settling\n\n## After the design\n\nAsk: \"Ready to execute? Run `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`\"\n\n## Contract index\n\nThe detailed design contract is in `references/design-format.md`; this compact index keeps\nthe pipeline markers visible to tools that inspect only the entrypoint:\n`## At a glance` → **Key decisions** → `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |`;\n`### R<n>: <name>` blocks contain Given/When/Then criteria, no test-name lists, and both\ntags. The feature section ends with `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline`.\nProduction-risk display is `⚠ production-risk` if and only if notes exist; alternatives\nare never manufactured. The umbrella roster uses `## Parts (build order)` and\n`N. <leaf> — <one-line scope>`.\nThe design format carries `Given/When/Then criteria`, `no test-name lists`, and tags;\nthe full contract also states `written \\`### Review\\` value stays \\`skip\\`` and records\narchitectural deviations `at deviation time`.\n\n```markdown\n## Feature acceptance\n- Given <starting state>, When <trigger>, Then <outcome>.\n### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline\n```\n\n</console_output>"}],"details":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_56Yjq7t16AJgQ330PJa25407/1","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-brainstorming/SKILL.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":0.8063339999971504}]},"isError":false,"durationMs":29,"timestamp":1791977297415,"nestedCalls":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_56Yjq7t16AJgQ330PJa25407/1","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-brainstorming/SKILL.md"},"durationMs":1}],"complete":true}}}

+{"type":"message","id":"6f2d1de8","parentId":"f39ddd49","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:29:23.656Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_T06XDj7APmvhRPKOm62u0660","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"<console_output>\n===== design-format.md =====\n# Design format\n\nRead before writing any design doc. Keep the design descriptive, not a task list. It is the single buildable artifact; no separate implementation plan.\n\n## Trivial format\n\nA trivial design has an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach), a single `### R1:` block with acceptance criteria and tags, and optional `## Production-risk areas`. It has no `## At a glance`, `## Requirements`, or `## Feature acceptance`; its ship gate is the full existing suite, not a manufactured E2E. The block rules below cover it.\n\n```markdown\n# Design: <topic>\n\nIn short: <what + why + approach>\n\n### R1: <name>\n<observable behavior>\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given <state>, When <action>, Then <observable outcome>.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n```\n\n## Non-trivial format\n\n**Open with `## At a glance`** — the human's two-minute digest, immediately before `## Requirements`: (1) a 2–4 sentence plain-language summary of what is wrong or needed, what will be built, and the key approach; (2) **Key decisions** — one line each: decision + why, with a `(rejected: <alternative> — <reason>)` clause only when the fork was real (never manufactured); (3) a table `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |`, exactly one row per requirement, where **R# = the requirement's block number in the `## Requirements` section below** — the ID every later digest keys on. Plain language only: no jargon, no Given/When/Then — those live in the requirement blocks. An umbrella overview gains no at-a-glance section; its roster serves that role.\n\nThen **`## Requirements`** — one `### R<n>: <name>` block per requirement, each one testable behavior:\n\n```markdown\n## Requirements\n\n### R1: <name>\n<one-line testable behavior — what the feature produces or changes, through its public interface>\n\n**Acceptance criteria** — Given/When/Then criteria defining \"done\". Test observable behavior — what the feature produces or changes through its public interface; not implementation steps. Cover edge and error cases.\n- Given … When … Then …\n- Given … When … Then … (edge case)\n\n### Checkpoints: none | full\n### Review: skip | parallel | inline\n\n### Production-risk notes\n- <only when the requirement touches a risk area>\n\n### R2: <name>\n…\n```\n\nBlock rules:\n\n- **No test-name lists.** The criteria are the test spec: the executor writes and names the tests red-green from them, so the doc holds no test-name lists and no R#-to-section map — the block structure is the map.\n- **Tag every requirement** — `### Checkpoints` (`none` = no per-requirement stop, the default; `full` = tests + complete stops) and `### Review` (`skip` = the default; `parallel` = four delegated reviewers; `inline` = one `pwk-code-review` pass). Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`; flag `full` only where complex logic or the feature's main part makes a human look worth the stop.\n- **Nothing is tagged silently here; only the human tags a slice for review.** A requirement touching a production-risk area carries its `### Production-risk notes` and is flagged `⚠ production-risk` in the At-a-glance Risk column — display-only, derived: `⚠ production-risk` if and only if the block carries non-empty notes, never an input; `auto` reads the underlying risk content, never the display column. Its written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it — propose the tag in prose; an explicit human tag always wins, both ways.\n- **No per-requirement spec stop, by design** — the criteria were approved at design time; re-checking mid-execution asks a question already answered.\n- **Production-risk notes** — risks involving schema migrations, new dependencies, external APIs, or seed data also get a `## Setup` section (dependencies, migrations, seed data, and how to verify setup worked) between `## Requirements` and `## Feature acceptance`.\n- **Ordering** — dependencies come earlier; the executor runs blocks in listed order with no dependency graph. Aim for vertical slices that merge cleanly on their own.\n\nThen the narrative sections the executor reads as context — problem, approaches considered, architecture, components, data flow, error handling. Head the fork record exactly `## Approaches considered` — finalizing's learning sweep reads it by that name — and **record every real fork and why each loser lost**; the executor needs the reasoning and finalize harvests it for ADRs.\n\nTouches a production-risk area (DB schema/migrations, auth, external APIs, concurrency/batch, uploads/large data flows, Redis/caching/queues)? Add a brief `## Production-risk areas` **immediately after the last requirement block** — inside the `### R1 → ## Feature acceptance` span, so the review packet carries it verbatim — and mirror the risks into each touched block's `### Production-risk notes`. `pwk-code-review` audits it (per reviewed slice, and always at the feature review); finalize's learning sweep reads it.\n\n**End with `## Feature acceptance`** — one or more end-to-end `Given/When/Then` scenarios proving the requirements *compose* into the feature. It is the feature's definition-of-done and the **primary enforced spec**: `pwk-executing-tasks` writes it as the E2E test first and gates on it. The section carries the feature-level `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline` tag — the one whole-feature review; default `auto`, which resolves on the design's own production-risk content to `parallel` (all four reviewers) when the design has any — a non-empty `## Production-risk areas` section, or a non-empty `### Production-risk notes` on any requirement — and to `inline` (one pass) otherwise. An explicit `parallel` or `inline` is written as-is, never resolved. If a scenario step would require inventing behavior, the invention goes back through the assumption gate — never silently into the scenario; an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement.\n\n```markdown\n## Feature acceptance\n\n- Given <starting state>, When <trigger>, Then <end-to-end outcome the feature promises>.\n\n### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline — the one whole-feature review; leave `auto` unless the human says otherwise.\n```\n\nExample (rate limiting): \"Given a new API consumer with no prior usage, When they exceed 100 requests/minute for 3 consecutive minutes, Then they're throttled, a `rate_limited` event is emitted, and further requests return 429.\"\n\n**Audit before finishing:** every requirement block has acceptance criteria and both tags, and each requirement appears **exactly once** — none dropped, none duplicated. Non-trivial docs carry a `## Feature acceptance` section as the primary enforced spec; a trivial doc ends after its `### R1:` block and ships on the full suite. Production-risk areas appear in the blocks that touch them. The probe test: a criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; one with no nameable probe goes back for splitting or rephrasing, and criteria never name tests. A fact settled by a sketch carries its proof where it lands — `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` — woven into the section it confirms, never a new template section.\n\n## Structural validator contract\n\nRun `scripts/validate-design.py` as directed in the main skill. It reads UTF-8 Markdown without modifying it; headings, tags, and labels inside backtick or tilde fenced examples do not count, so close every fence. Real requirements use unique sequential `### R1: <name>`, `### R2: <name>`, … headings with nonempty names. Each block needs a standalone `**Acceptance criteria**` label in its main body, before any tag or risk-note heading (an explanatory suffix after an em dash, dash, or colon is allowed), with nonempty criteria before the next heading or bold label. A bare bullet or content borrowed from risk notes is not a criterion section.\n\nWrite each selected tag as one value, not the template's pipe-separated alternatives. Missing optional tags retain `Checkpoints: none`, `Review: skip`, and `Feature review: auto`. Non-trivial designs require nonempty `## Feature acceptance` scenarios before their feature-review tag. Only the minimal trivial shape above receives the no-Feature-acceptance exception.\n\nThe helper checks structure, not meaning: it does not prove Given/When/Then quality, testability, edge/error coverage, good slicing, risk classification, confirmed assumptions, or human approval. Those remain the agent's audit and the human's judgment. Per-requirement checkpoints and reviews are **opt-in** — they fire only when the design doc tags them, and the feature gate covers the rest. A trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`) skips the E2E and ships on the full suite.\n\n## Before you start\n\nResolve local references and scripts from this skill directory; a missing required resource is a blocker to report, never to skip.\n\n1. **Git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`; note uncommitted changes.\n2. **Find the doc** — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). The `## Feature acceptance` section is the E2E you gate on first; a trivial doc skips steps 5–6.\n2. **Create the progress file** beside the design at `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md`, reading [Progress format](references/progress-format.md) first. Start at `Feature phase: e2e-written` (trivial doc: `implementing (0/N)`); `Setup: pending` when the design has `## Setup`, otherwise `Setup: n/a`.\n3. **Setup pre-flight** *(only if the design doc has a `## Setup` section)* — install dependencies, apply migrations, seed data, then run the suite. **⏸ CHECKPOINT: setup** — present results and wait for approval, then set `Setup: done`.\n4. **Commit the design docs** — `git add docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ && git commit -m \"docs: add design doc\"`, scoped to the topic folder so another topic’s drafts never ride it.\n5. **Write the feature-acceptance E2E test (red)** — encode the `## Feature acceptance` section as a real test, run it, confirm it **fails**. Unlocked: may edit code to apply smell fixes.\"\n---\n\n# Code Review\n\nReview the code just implemented — one tagged requirement, or the whole feature at the feature-level review. **Unlocked** — you may edit code to apply smell fixes; flag everything else as a follow-up.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Identify the scope** — in the feature-gate flow (the default) you review the **whole feature diff** at the feature-level review (`git diff $FEATURE_BASE...HEAD`, `$FEATURE_BASE` being the parent of the first Commit-column entry; see the executing skill's packet recipe), with every design-doc acceptance criterion and the `## Feature acceptance` E2E in scope. Invoked per-requirement (`Review: inline` on a tagged requirement, or inline-completing a missing delegated role when the tag is `parallel`), the scope is that requirement alone — read its acceptance criteria from the design doc and use `git log --oneline -5` plus `git diff` to see what changed. Invoked standalone — no invoking skill, no design doc, no packet — review the span the user names (the working-tree diff, or the branch's commits against its parent): tracing, smell fixes, and the hazard check run as usual, while spec alignment has no criteria to key on — say so and judge the diff against its stated intent rather than manufacturing a coverage table. When the invoking skill already assembled a packet (the feature packet, or the requirement-scoped `<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`), work from the packet — it is the scope of record; re-derive nothing it states.\n\n2. **🔍 Code tracing** — trace the new or changed code paths end-to-end against the acceptance criteria and the feature E2E (a trivial design doc has no feature E2E — its acceptance criteria alone are the spec). For each path, determine whether data flows correctly from entry to the asserted outcome. Note any branch the tests do not exercise, any dead branch, or any path where the trace breaks.\n\n3. **📐 Spec alignment** — for each acceptance criterion, point to the code and the test that satisfy it. A criterion with no covering code or no test is a **gap**. Code that does more than the criteria specify is **scope creep** — flag it.\n\n   **Open the report with a coverage table** — one row per requirement in scope, keyed by the design doc's `### R<n>:` headings (R# = n; the whole design doc at the feature-level review, just the tagged requirement when invoked per-requirement):\n\n   | R# | Verdict | Evidence |\n   |----|---------|----------|\n   | 1 | <verdict> | file:line (code), file:line (test) |\n\n   Verdict per requirement: `covered | gap | scope-creep` — `covered` = every criterion has covering code and a test; `gap` = a criterion lacks code or a test; `scope-creep` = the code does more than the criteria specify; findings elaborate on every non-`covered` row, and an all-`covered` table needs no elaboration.\n\n4. **🧹 Code smells — fix these directly:** review the changed code and affected files against the requirement and feature scope, then fix what you find.\n   - Shallow modules (interface nearly as complex as implementation)\n   - Duplication\n   - Missing seams or premature abstraction\n   - Poor naming, magic values, dead code\n   Apply the fix, re-run the full suite (must stay green), and commit. Only a smell that requires a refactor large enough to risk the requirement is **flagged** instead of applied.\n\n5. **⚠️ Production hazard check** — audit the changed code against the high-risk hazards. For each, write `[SAFE]` (1-line justification) or `[TRIGGERED]` (concrete mitigation):\n   1. **Unbounded operations** — multi-key deletions/scans (`KEYS`, raw `SCAN` loops), full-table loads filtered in memory\n   2. **Missing indexes** — hot queries on unindexed columns (table scans under load)\n   3. **Unbounded concurrency** — unthrottled fan-out (`Promise.all` without batch limits)\n   4. **Long-running transactions** — holding DB connections/locks across slow external calls\n   5. **Query/command interpolation** — raw variables merged into SQL or shell (injection)\n   6. **Unrestricted uploads / temp flooding** — uploads to local temp without limits or `finally` cleanup\n   7. **Silent swallowing loops** — background workers catching/suppressing exceptions without logging/back-off\n   Also check the design's `## Production-risk areas`, if any.\n\n6. **Report** — summarize: tracing findings, spec gaps, smells fixed (with commits), hazards `[TRIGGERED]`. Non-trivial findings become follow-up items — the user decides whether to address now or defer.\n7. **Mark done** — the review never edits the progress file. A clean pass hands back so the executing loop can set the requirement's Done cell `✅` (the row was left `🔄` while under review) and write its execution-summary row; findings leave the row `🔄` for another pass. (At the feature-level review every row is already terminal — verify none regressed and move on.) Already-terminal rows of other requirements never regress. Done means reviewed, not just committed.\n\n## Principles\n\n- **Tracing and spec alignment are the core** — they catch what tests miss: untested branches, missing criteria, scope creep.\n- **Fix smells in place; flag everything else.** Keep the review scoped — the goal is polish on the requirement that just landed, not a redesign pass.\n- **Be proportional** — a one-function change doesn't need the depth of a batch pipeline; a `Review: inline` tag was a deliberate call at design approval — keep the review focused and don't second-guess it.\n\n## After the review\n\nReturn to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` — the next requirement, or the ship checkpoint when every requirement is done. `\"2026-01-01t00:00:00z\"`, When parsed, Then it is accepted, because ISO 8601 permits lowercase designators.\n- Given the zone-less `\"2026-01-01T00:00:00\"`, When parsed, Then it throws, because the Date.parse(value) : NaN;\n  if (Number.isNaN(epoch)) {\n    throw new RangeError(\n      `invalid --since value: ${JSON.stringify(value)} (expected an ISO 8601 instant like 2026-01-04T09:05:00Z, or a date like 2026-01-04)`,\n    );\n  }\n  return epoch;\n}\n\nexport function summarize(text, { since } = {}) {\n  if (since !== undefined && (typeof since !== \"number\" || Number.isNaN(since))) {\n    throw new TypeError(`since must be an epoch-millisecond number, received ${JSON.stringify(since)}`);\n  }\n  const levels = {};\n  const times = [];\n  for (const line of text.split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n    if (!line.trim()) continue;\n    const event = JSON.parse(line);\n    if (since !== undefined) {\n      // NaN-safe: untimed or unparseable timestamps never satisfy >=.\n      const at = event.time ? +{"type":"message","id":"74de83c4","parentId":"ef067c3d","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:37:27.770Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<skill name=\"pwk-finalizing\" location=\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-finalizing/SKILL.md\">\nReferences are relative to /Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-finalizing.\n\n# Finalizing\n\nShip the completed work.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Pre-finalization checks\n\n1. **Verify the repo root** — run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts).\n2. **Run the FULL test suite** — only a green suite ships; re-run it yourself rather than trusting the previous session's ending state. Anything failing → send the user back to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`.\n3. Read **every** relevant progress file — for a multi-leaf topic that's each leaf's progress file — discovered by listing `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-progress.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`. With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every topic’s `Feature phase:` extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   More than one topic in flight? Ask which one this finalize ships — finalizing touches only its own topic, and another topic being designed or executed never blocks this run. Then match the chosen topic's `Feature phase:` line (e.g. `grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`) and read only its ❌/⏭ verdict rows in the Requirements table (e.g. `sed -n '/^## Requirements/,/^## Execution summary/p' <file> | grep '^| [0-9].*❌'` / `sed -n '/^## Requirements/,/^## Execution summary/p' <file> | grep '^| [0-9].*⏭'` — scoped to Requirements-table rows because the Execution summary rows share the same row shape); the sections after the tables carry nothing the gate needs. Apply the gates below to the chosen topic's file(s) and no others:\n   - **Any `❌ failed`** (in any leaf of the topic) → **block**. Present counts and reasons; continue only when the user sends the task back to executing-tasks, or explicitly types `--force-failed`.\n   - **Only `⏭ skipped`** → warn and confirm (\"Requirement N was skipped. Continue, or go back?\").\n   - **`Feature phase` must be `done`** in every progress file of the topic — any other value (`e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`) means its ship checkpoint has not been approved: send the user back to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` instead of finalizing.\n4. **Cross-check the roster — fail closed on unstarted work.** The progress file's `Design:` ref names the design doc, and that directory is the topic folder. An `overview.md` **beside the design doc** (same folder — never a repo-wide `docs/plans/**/overview.md`) means a multi-leaf topic: read that overview's `## Parts (build order)` roster and require one `<leaf>-progress.md` per leaf. A roster leaf with no progress file is **unstarted** — **block**, naming the leaf, and send the user back to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` to build it; never dispose an unstarted design unread. (A leaf whose progress file is not `done` is already stopped by the gate above.)\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Derive the topic set** —\n   - **Multi-leaf topic** (an `overview.md` beside the design doc, inside the same `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folder — never a repo-wide `docs/plans/**/overview.md`, and always excluding docs/plans/completed/, so an archived or sibling topic never routes): the set is the topic folder itself, disposed as one unit.\n   - **Single-leaf topic**: progress file → `Design:` ref → that design doc's own folder → `<topic>`, which **is the folder slug** — the topic directory's name, and the same value `pwk-executing-tasks` uses for the branch and worktree (never a leaf filename). One folder.\n\n   Ambiguous with several designs in flight? Ask.\n2. **Run the learning sweep — before any disposal command.** The planning docs are about to be destroyed, so extract the durable knowledge first, while its container still exists: each design doc's At-a-glance key-decision bullets **and its `Approaches considered` section** (every leaf's, for an umbrella), each progress file's `Deviated?` entries, and each Code digest's `[ALERT]` entries. (A trivial doc has no `## At a glance` and no `Approaches considered` — expect an honest-empty sweep.) Then:\n   - **Offer an ADR** (in `docs/adr/`) for each item that passes the three gates — **hard to reverse**, **surprising without context**, **a real trade-off**.\n   - **Append generic rules** to `docs/lessons.md` (strip domain specifics).\n   - Both outputs are **honest-empty**: most features qualify for nothing — say so and move on; never manufacture. When an item passes the gates but the recorded material is too thin for a credible ADR, **ask the human rather than fabricating**.\n   - The sweep is file-based by necessity: executing and finalizing usually run in fresh sessions with no memory of the brainstorm, so everything the sweep needs must already be on disk.\n3. **Dispose of consumed plan docs — ask archive or delete** — for **every topic** in the set, dispose its topic folder `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` **as one unit**: every leaf's `-design.md`, `-progress.md`, and `-review-packet*.md`, plus `overview.md` for an umbrella. The digest sections and the Evidence cells live inside their host docs and ride the folder. The folder path is taken verbatim from discovery, and the `????-??-??-` dated shape is the topic's identity — a bare `*<topic>*` pattern would over-match unrelated topics. Present both options and let the human choose:\n\n   - **Delete (default)** — code + tests are the source of truth; removing the scaffold prevents stale plan docs from misleading future sessions. The invariant: the topic folder is the disposal unit — delete it entirely, nothing more and nothing less; any single operation achieving exactly this is correct, and the bash below is one canonical example.\n\n     ```bash\n     # the topic folder goes as one unit (every leaf, plus overview.md if it has one).\n     # The folder path is taken verbatim from discovery — never typed or\n     # reconstructed (rm -rf has no glob guard):\n     rm -rf docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/\n     git add -A docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ && git commit -m \"chore: delete planning docs for <topic>\"\n     # the add is scoped to the topic pathspec, so another in-flight topic's\n     # uncommitted drafts never ride the disposal commit.\n     ```\n\n   - **Archive** — keep the planning history for future readers by moving the artifacts into `docs/plans/completed/`. The invariant: the topic folder moves whole into `docs/plans/completed/` and the destination is verified before committing; any single operation achieving exactly this is correct, and the bash below is one canonical example.\n\n     ```bash\n     mkdir -p docs/plans/completed\n     # the topic folder goes as one unit (every leaf, plus overview.md if it has one).\n     # No error suppression on the folder move: verify the archive landed before\n     # committing, or a silently failed move would commit the deletion and destroy\n     # the history the human chose to keep:\n     mv docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ docs/plans/completed/\n     ls docs/plans/completed/<date>-<topic>/ >/dev/null\n     # both sides of the move, and nothing else — another in-flight topic's\n     # uncommitted drafts never ride the archive commit:\n     git add -A docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ docs/plans/completed/ && git commit -m \"chore: archive planning docs for <topic>\"\n     ```\n\n   Verify with `ls docs/plans/` before and after. Both paths commit the disposal so the shipped branch is clean. Neither touches `docs/adr/`, `docs/lessons.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, or `README.md` — those are permanent.\n4. **Curate lessons (Agile Scrum Master hat)** — if `docs/lessons.md` exists: add missed lessons, generalize domain-specific rules, de-duplicate, categorize, retire stale rules. None exists but lessons were learned? Create it. (The learning sweep feeds this; curation then shapes the whole file.)\n5. **Update documentation** — if the API or surface changed: `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, any inline docs. Bump the package version (major for breaking changes).\n6. **Choose a merge strategy** — ask the human: 1. **Create PR** (`git push origin <branch>` then `gh pr create`). 2. **Rebase & merge** *(recommended)* — rebase onto parent, `--ff-only` merge, push parent, delete branch. 3. **Squash & merge**. 4. **Merge commit** (`--no-ff`).\n\n   For 2–4, confirm the detected parent branch first. When a worktree was used, the parent-side commands (merge onto parent, push parent, branch deletion) run from the main working tree — the worktree holds the feature branch, so the parent cannot be checked out there (`git -C ../<repo> …`; the never-cd rule still holds) — and step 7's worktree removal comes **first**: a branch checked out in a worktree cannot be deleted.\n7. **Clean up** — if a worktree was used, check `git worktree list` first: when the topic's worktree exists, remove it (`git worktree remove ../<repo>-<topic>`, `<topic>` being the folder slug, never a leaf slug) from the main working tree — `git -C ../<repo> worktree remove ../<repo>-<topic>` when the session stands inside the worktree, which git refuses to remove under itself. Absent → a silent no-op, never a failure.\n\n## Principles\n\n- The learning sweep runs before disposal and touches only `docs/adr/` and `docs/lessons.md` — the two permanent stores.\n- Dispose of the active work's artifacts only, the human's choice — the unit is the topic folder `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/`, one folder whether a single leaf or an umbrella's many. Unrelated topics stay in `docs/plans/`.\n- ADRs are permanent institutional memory — never archived or rotated.\n- Bump the package version if this is a published change (major for breaking changes).\n</skill>"}],"timestamp":1791977847769}}

An approved ADR goes to `docs/adr/` — outside the writable boundary, so the human writes it or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`, and the design phase never unlocks it. The design doc is the **single buildable artifact**: each requirement carries its own acceptance criteria and review tags, and the executor builds straight from it. Source-writing happens in `pwk-executing-tasks`.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Proportionality: trivial vs non-trivial\n\nClassify the change at the start.\n\n- **Trivial** — a typo or obvious bugfix with no open design questions, a config or version bump, a single-function change, or anything the human flags as trivial. Skip steps 3–6: read the design-format reference, run the validator in step 7, and write a **minimal** design doc in one turn — an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach), one `### R1:` block with criteria and tags, an optional `## Production-risk areas` line, and deliberately **no `## Feature acceptance`** (a trivial slice ships on the full existing suite; no E2E is manufactured). Hand off to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`. The guard still enforces read-only — trivial compresses the phase to one turn, it does not skip it.\n- **Non-trivial** — open design questions, multiple approaches, cross-module impact, or new behavior. Run the full process below.\n\nWhen unsure, ask: \"This looks trivial — fast-path it, or full brainstorm?\" Default to full.\n\n## Scope and granularity\n\n**One design doc = one PR; one requirement = one testable slice within it.** Most work is a single design doc; several requirements serving one cohesive outcome do not force an umbrella.\n\nA large request with distinct testable outcomes that need separate design/execute cycles becomes an **umbrella** of vertical slices with one-line scopes and a build order, approved before you write an overview or design. A layers-only split (database, API, UI) is not vertical — each slice delivers testable behavior. Design only the current slice, grounded in implemented code, not speculative sibling designs; the umbrella still ships as one PR on one branch, finalized once.\n\n**One folder per topic:** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/`, holding `<leaf>-design.md`, `<leaf>-progress.md`, and `<leaf>-review-packet*.md`; `<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic, and more than one leaf adds `overview.md`. The folder is the creation, discovery, and disposal unit.\n\n**Umbrella trigger:** before proposing a new umbrella, or when discovery finds an `overview.md` beside this design, read [references/umbrella.md](references/umbrella.md) — it owns the status-free roster, the first/later-slice procedures, and header-only predecessor reporting. Build order is advisory, not a gate, and an existing roster means the split is already decided; design the current slice against it.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Check git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`. Uncommitted work? Ask the user what to do first.\n2. **Discovery** *(skip in a brand-new repo with no `docs/plans/`)* — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md`, `*-progress.md`, and `overview.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; report in-flight topics and any active umbrella, each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`; design-only topics report `design` — no body ingest). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   If the idea continues an existing topic, ask whether to extend it or start fresh. An `overview.md` **beside the design doc** means the split is already decided — read it for the roster and design this part’s `<leaf>-design.md` against it.\n3. **Understand the idea** — **PRD brief.** With source material (a PRD, ticket, or spec — pasted text, a path, a URL), open with a brief before any question: **Background** (the problem, why now, who is affected — each product claim cites its PRD section), **Current situation** (what the code does today — each claim cites `file:line`), **The delta** (what must change, each line naming a requirement candidate, and what stays untouched). Zero-context rule: plain meaning first, the pointer second — quote non-English domain terms with a plain-English gloss and mark anything uncited `(interpretation: …)`. Unreadable source material: report the blocker, ground on code only, name the gap. The human corrects the brief before frontier rounds; confirmed facts weave into the design doc, with no sidecar file. No source material, no brief. Then read only enough code, docs, and commits to ground the design, and **check `docs/lessons.md`**.\n\n   Ask questions in **frontier rounds** — the frontier is every question whose prerequisites are settled. Build the tree by walking every checklist dimension (*Goal & scope · Data & state · Behavior & edge cases · Errors & failure · Integration · Non-functional*), print `— nothing to ask` for empty groups, and ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question (`Q1`, `Q2`, …) with your recommended answer (`➡️ <recommendation>`) so the human confirms, strikes, or corrects each in one reply. A question that depends on another still-open one waits for a later round; recompute the frontier after each round.\n\n   **Facts vs. decisions:** anything answerable from the codebase, docs, or tools is looked up — recon scout or inline — never asked of the human; a pending lookup holds only its downstream questions while the rest of the frontier is asked now. **Runnable facts:** an unknown observable by running something — behavior, timing, output, layout — is settled by a bounded sketch, never asked of the human and never guessed: an inline interpreter or a file under `docs/plans/<topic>/`, no installs, no source writes. Record it where it lands as `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` and list it in the round summary so the human can strike it; a sketch result that would set business behavior still passes the assumption gate; inconclusive or blocked → record `INCONCLUSIVE` plus one line of what ran, and the question returns to the human with the result attached. A cheaper read beats a run when reading can decide, and only decisions are asked.\n\n   Major approvals stay single-decision — one question each, never batched: approach selection (step 5), umbrella split, design approval, ADR offer. The interview ends when the frontier is empty — every branch visited, nothing left silently assumed — not when you feel you understand. Then present a short summary and ask: \"Should I proceed, or is there more?\" The human decides when to move on.\n4. **(skipped on trivial changes)** **Codebase recon** — for a non-trivial topic with prior art, request the host’s `codebase-recon` capability using the logical `pwk-recon-scout` role: a fresh-context, read-only, bounded worker given the topic, one-line intent, and repo root. Use its 5-section map (Relevant files, Existing patterns, Call sites, Test layout, Gotchas) as grounding for steps 5–6 instead of reading those files inline; the scout reports observations only, never design recommendations. No compatible capability, or constraints it cannot enforce → report `Scout: unavailable` and do the same recon inline, preserving the five-section map and `file:line` citations; never omit recon silently.\n5. **Explore approaches** — propose 2–3, leading with your recommendation, and sketch the concrete interface (types, signatures, example caller) for each so the comparison is grounded in code rather than abstractions.\n6. **Present the design** in one pass, organized into sections (architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing) — the human comments on any section; re-present only revised sections.\n\n   **Assumptions to confirm first** — before presenting, sweep the drafted design: every unconfirmed assumption it would bake in (business rules, defaults, edge-case resolutions) re-opens as a numbered question with your recommended answer, for one reply. An honest empty gate (\"no unconfirmed assumptions\") when the draft is clean — never invent items. Hard rule: no business behavior enters the design doc on the agent's assumption; confirmed facts are woven into existing sections, with no new template section.\n\n   Identified a significant architectural decision? Offer an ADR in `docs/adr/`, only when all three hold: **hard to reverse**, **surprising without context**, **a real trade-off**. Format: title + 1–3 sentences of context/decision/why. ADRs are permanent institutional memory — never archived or rotated. (Guard note: the human writes the approved ADR or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`; you never write it while the design phase is gated.)\n7. **Write the design doc** — validate its structure before handing off. Read [references/design-format.md](references/design-format.md) first for the exact format, tag defaults, risk/Setup rules, and audit; requirement blocks carry acceptance criteria plus `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags. Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`. Write `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md`, creating the topic folder when absent. It is descriptive, not a task list — the executor builds directly from it.\n\n   **Completion gate:** Test observable behavior through the public interface. Audit every requirement’s criteria, tags, and risk notes — each appears exactly once. A criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; a criterion with no nameable probe sends the requirement back for splitting or rephrasing, and design-doc criteria never name tests — the probe materializes at execution. For non-trivial work, finish with an end-to-end `## Feature acceptance` as the primary enforced spec. If writing a scenario step would require inventing behavior, that invention goes back through the assumption gate: an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement, not permission to guess. Risk notes never set the tag — the written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it, and only the human tags a slice for review. Keep designing until the requirements compose into a coherent feature and the human approves the design, including feature acceptance; trivial work keeps the compressed one-turn path above.\n\n   **Python prerequisite:** structural validation requires Python 3.9+ where commands execute, using only its standard library. Confirm a compatible `python3` exists before invoking the helper; if it is missing or too old, report the blocker and request a suitable runtime, then stop at this gate. Never auto-install Python, use a fallback implementation, or claim validation succeeded.\n\n   Resolve the helper from this installed skill’s directory and pass explicit paths, quoting paths with spaces:\n\n   ```sh\n   python3 \"<brainstorming-skill-dir>/scripts/validate-design.py\" \"<design-path>\"\n   ```\n\n   Nonzero means validation did not succeed: report file-specific diagnostics, correct the structural errors, and rerun. A missing local reference or helper is a blocker before its dependent action; success verifies structure only — never semantic correctness, sound slicing, confirmed assumptions, or human approval.\n\nThe session stays read-only and uncommitted through brainstorm: branch creation and the design-doc commit happen at the start of `pwk-executing-tasks`.\n\n## Principles\n\n- Detail-gathering asks in frontier rounds; approvals ask one decision at a time\n- No silent assumptions — ask, gate, or look it up\n- YAGNI — remove unnecessary features\n- Design for testability\n- Explore alternatives before settling\n\n## After the design\n\nAsk: \"Ready to execute? Run `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`\"\n\n## Contract index\n\nThe detailed design contract is in `references/design-format.md`; this compact index keeps\nthe pipeline markers visible to tools that inspect only the entrypoint:\n`## At a glance` → **Key decisions** → `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |`;\n`### R<n>: <name>` blocks contain Given/When/Then criteria, no test-name lists, and both\ntags. The feature section ends with `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline`.\nProduction-risk display is `⚠ production-risk` if and only if notes exist; alternatives\nare never manufactured. The umbrella roster uses `## Parts (build order)` and\n`N. <leaf> — <one-line scope>`.\nThe design format carries `Given/When/Then criteria`, `no test-name lists`, and tags;\nthe full contract also states `written \\`### Review\\` value stays \\`skip\\`` and records\narchitectural deviations `at deviation time`.\n\n```markdown\n## Feature acceptance\n- Given <starting state>, When <trigger>, Then <outcome>.\n### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline\n```\n"}],"details":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_ZyUPcnfDABX66l9Uepy87330/1","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-brainstorming/SKILL.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":1.9175840000007156}]},"isError":false,"durationMs":60,"timestamp":1791978029478,"nestedCalls":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_ZyUPcnfDABX66l9Uepy87330/1","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-brainstorming/SKILL.md"},"durationMs":2}],"complete":true}}}

The block rules below cover it.\n\n```markdown\n# Design: <topic>\n\nIn short: <what + why + approach>\n\n### R1: <name>\n<observable behavior>\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given <state>, When <action>, Then <observable outcome>.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n```\n\n## Non-trivial format\n\n**Open with `## At a glance`** — the human's two-minute digest, immediately before `## Requirements`: (1) a 2–4 sentence plain-language summary of what is wrong or needed, what will be built, and the key approach; (2) **Key decisions** — one line each: decision + why, with a `(rejected: <alternative> — <reason>)` clause only when the fork was real (never manufactured); (3) a table `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |`, exactly one row per requirement, where **R# = the requirement's block number in the `## Requirements` section below** — the ID every later digest keys on. Test observable behavior — what the feature produces or changes through its public interface; not implementation steps. Cover edge and error cases.\n- Given … When … Then …\n- Given … When … Then … (edge case)\n\n### Checkpoints: none | full\n### Review: skip | parallel | inline\n\n### Production-risk notes\n- <only when the requirement touches a risk area>\n\n### R2: <name>\n…\n```\n\nBlock rules:\n\n- **No test-name lists.** The criteria are the test spec: the executor writes and names the tests red-green from them, so the doc holds no test-name lists and no R#-to-section map — the block structure is the map.\n- **Tag every requirement** — `### Checkpoints` (`none` = no per-requirement stop, the default; `full` = tests + complete stops) and `### Review` (`skip` = the default; `parallel` = four delegated reviewers; `inline` = one `pwk-code-review` pass). Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`; flag `full` only where complex logic or the feature's main part makes a human look worth the stop.\n- **Nothing is tagged silently here; only the human tags a slice for review.** A requirement touching a production-risk area carries its `### Production-risk notes` and is flagged `⚠ production-risk` in the At-a-glance Risk column — display-only, derived: `⚠ production-risk` if and only if the block carries non-empty notes, never an input; `auto` reads the underlying risk content, never the display column. Its written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it — propose the tag in prose; an explicit human tag always wins, both ways.\n- **No per-requirement spec stop, by design** — the criteria were approved at design time; re-checking mid-execution asks a question already answered.\n- **Production-risk notes** — risks involving schema migrations, new dependencies, external APIs, or seed data also get a `## Setup` section (dependencies, migrations, seed data, and how to verify setup worked) between `## Requirements` and `## Feature acceptance`.\n- **Ordering** — dependencies come earlier; the executor runs blocks in listed order with no dependency graph. Aim for vertical slices that merge cleanly on their own.\n\nThen the narrative sections the executor reads as context — problem, approaches considered, architecture, components, data flow, error handling. Head the fork record exactly `## Approaches considered` — finalizing's learning sweep reads it by that name — and **record every real fork and why each loser lost**; the executor needs the reasoning and finalize harvests it for ADRs.\n\nTouches a production-risk area (DB schema/migrations, auth, external APIs, concurrency/batch, uploads/large data flows, Redis/caching/queues)? The section carries the feature-level `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline` tag — the one whole-feature review; default `auto`, which resolves on the design's own production-risk content to `parallel` (all four reviewers) when the design has any — a non-empty `## Production-risk areas` section, or a non-empty `### Production-risk notes` on any requirement — and to `inline` (one pass) otherwise. expected {allowed}\")\n                else:\n                    values[name] = value\n        return values\n\n    for heading in requirements:\n        end = next((h.index for h in headings if h.index > heading.index and (h.level <= 2 or h in requirements)), len(lines))\n        criteria_end = next((h.index for h in headings if heading.index < h.index < end), end)\n        labels = [i for i in range(heading.index + 1, criteria_end) if CRITERIA.fullmatch(lines[i].strip())]\n        owner = heading.title.split(\":\", 1)[0]\n        if not labels:\n            errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: {owner} needs a standalone **Acceptance criteria** section\")\n        elif len(labels) > 1:\n            errors.append(f\"line {labels[1] + 1}: {owner} has duplicate Acceptance criteria sections\")\n        elif not has_content(criteria_body(lines, labels[0] + 1, end)):\n            errors.append(f\"line {labels[0] + 1}: {owner} Acceptance criteria is empty; add an end-to-end criterion before its review tag\")\n        values = tags(heading.index + 1, end, (\"Feature review\",), \"Feature acceptance\")\n        summaries.append(f\"Feature review={values['Feature review']}\")\n\n    for heading in headings:\n        for name in TAG_VALUES:\n            if re.match(re.escape(name) + r\"\\b\", heading.title) and heading.index not in owned_tags:\n                owner = \"## Feature acceptance\" if name == \"Feature review\" else \"a ### R<n>: requirement block\"\n                errors.append(f\"line {heading.index + 1}: {name} must be a ### tag inside {owner}\")\n    return errors, summaries\n\n\ndef main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=\"Read-only structural design validation.
