The criteria define *what*, you decide *how*.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\nThe feature-acceptance E2E test is the primary enforced gate and the primary enforced spec. The flow is always on: E2E first (red), the requirements back-to-back, then the feature review and the **ship checkpoint**. Per-requirement checkpoints and reviews are **opt-in** — they fire only when the design doc tags them, and the feature gate covers the rest. A trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`) skips the E2E and ships on the full suite.\n\n## Before you start\n\nResolve local references and scripts from this skill directory; a missing required resource is a blocker to report, never to skip.\n\n1. **Git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`; note uncommitted changes.\n2. **Find the doc** — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; take each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   No doc → ask for `/skill:pwk-brainstorming`; several → ask which. A matching `*-progress.md` means a **resume** ([Resume and progress](#resume-and-progress)); an umbrella part whose prior leaves are not all `done` shows their `Feature phase:` lines as advisory context.\n3. **Workspace** — choose this topic’s branch or worktree: read [Workspace and resume details](references/resume.md#workspace) first; it owns the command order including worktree handoffs. Reuse this topic’s branch (one umbrella = one branch); a different topic’s branch never hosts these commits. Offer or adopt only after checking existing worktrees, then wait for the user.\n\n## First run\n\n1. **Parse the design doc** — read every `### R<n>:` heading with its `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags and the feature-level `### Feature review` tag. Requirements run in **listed order**. The `## Feature acceptance` section is the E2E you gate on first; a trivial doc skips steps 5–6.\n2. **Create the progress file** beside the design at `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md`, reading [Progress format](references/progress-format.md) first. Start at `Feature phase: e2e-written` (trivial doc: `implementing (0/N)`); `Setup: pending` when the design has `## Setup`, otherwise `Setup: n/a`.\n3. **Setup pre-flight** *(only if the design doc has a `## Setup` section)* — install dependencies, apply migrations, seed data, then run the suite. **⏸ CHECKPOINT: setup** — present results and wait for approval, then set `Setup: done`.\n4. **Commit the design docs** — `git add docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ && git commit -m \"docs: add design doc\"`, scoped to the topic folder so another topic’s drafts never ride it.\n5. **Write the feature-acceptance E2E test (red)** — encode the `## Feature acceptance` section as a real test, run it, confirm it **fails**. If it passes immediately, probe why before proceeding — the behavior may already exist, or the test may be asserting too little — and if the expected behavior looks wrong, **stop and present** rather than implementing against a wrong spec. Iterate to green; fixing the implementation is the default, and you **stop and present only when you are genuinely blocked** (nothing makes it pass, or the E2E itself is wrong).\n6. **Notice, not a stop — report the E2E and continue.** Post 1–2 plain-language lines stating **what the E2E proves** (\"this test proves that …\") plus its failing output, then go straight into the implement phase **without waiting for approval** — the `## Feature acceptance` text was approved during brainstorm.\n\n## Resume and progress\n\n`Feature phase` is one of: `e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`.\n\n**Done cell:** `⬜` not started · `🔄` in progress · `✅` done · `❌` failed · `⏭` skipped. A row is **terminal** when its Done cell is `✅`, `❌`, or `⏭` — resolved, not necessarily passed. Unlocked: may edit code to apply smell fixes.\"\n---\n\n# Code Review\n\nReview the code just implemented — one tagged requirement, or the whole feature at the feature-level review. **Unlocked** — you may edit code to apply smell fixes; flag everything else as a follow-up.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Identify the scope** — in the feature-gate flow (the default) you review the **whole feature diff** at the feature-level review (`git diff $FEATURE_BASE...HEAD`, `$FEATURE_BASE` being the parent of the first Commit-column entry; see the executing skill's packet recipe), with every design-doc acceptance criterion and the `## Feature acceptance` E2E in scope. Invoked per-requirement (`Review: inline` on a tagged requirement, or inline-completing a missing delegated role when the tag is `parallel`), the scope is that requirement alone — read its acceptance criteria from the design doc and use `git log --oneline -5` plus `git diff` to see what changed. Invoked standalone — no invoking skill, no design doc, no packet — review the span the user names (the working-tree diff, or the branch's commits against its parent): tracing, smell fixes, and the hazard check run as usual, while spec alignment has no criteria to key on — say so and judge the diff against its stated intent rather than manufacturing a coverage table. When the invoking skill already assembled a packet (the feature packet, or the requirement-scoped `<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`), work from the packet — it is the scope of record; re-derive nothing it states.\n\n2. **🔍 Code tracing** — trace the new or changed code paths end-to-end against the acceptance criteria and the feature E2E (a trivial design doc has no feature E2E — its acceptance criteria alone are the spec). For each path, determine whether data flows correctly from entry to the asserted outcome. Note any branch the tests do not exercise, any dead branch, or any path where the trace breaks.\n\n3. **📐 Spec alignment** — for each acceptance criterion, point to the code and the test that satisfy it. A criterion with no covering code or no test is a **gap**. Code that does more than the criteria specify is **scope creep** — flag it.\n\n   **Open the report with a coverage table** — one row per requirement in scope, keyed by the design doc's `### R<n>:` headings (R# = n; the whole design doc at the feature-level review, just the tagged requirement when invoked per-requirement):\n\n   | R# | Verdict | Evidence |\n   |----|---------|----------|\n   | 1 | <verdict> | file:line (code), file:line (test) |\n\n   Verdict per requirement: `covered | gap | scope-creep` — `covered` = every criterion has covering code and a test; `gap` = a criterion lacks code or a test; `scope-creep` = the code does more than the criteria specify; findings elaborate on every non-`covered` row, and an all-`covered` table needs no elaboration.\n\n4. **🧹 Code smells — fix these directly:** review the changed code and affected files against the requirement and feature scope, then fix what you find.\n   - Shallow modules (interface nearly as complex as implementation)\n   - Duplication\n   - Missing seams or premature abstraction\n   - Poor naming, magic values, dead code\n   Apply the fix, re-run the full suite (must stay green), and commit. Only a smell that requires a refactor large enough to risk the requirement is **flagged** instead of applied.\n\n5. **⚠️ Production hazard check** — audit the changed code against the high-risk hazards. For each, write `[SAFE]` (1-line justification) or `[TRIGGERED]` (concrete mitigation):\n   1. **Unbounded operations** — multi-key deletions/scans (`KEYS`, raw `SCAN` loops), full-table loads filtered in memory\n   2. **Missing indexes** — hot queries on unindexed columns (table scans under load)\n   3. **Unbounded concurrency** — unthrottled fan-out (`Promise.all` without batch limits)\n   4. **Long-running transactions** — holding DB connections/locks across slow external calls\n   5. **Query/command interpolation** — raw variables merged into SQL or shell (injection)\n   6. **Unrestricted uploads / temp flooding** — uploads to local temp without limits or `finally` cleanup\n   7. **Silent swallowing loops** — background workers catching/suppressing exceptions without logging/back-off\n   Also check the design's `## Production-risk areas`, if any.\n\n6. **Report** — summarize: tracing findings, spec gaps, smells fixed (with commits), hazards `[TRIGGERED]`. Non-trivial findings become follow-up items — the user decides whether to address now or defer.\n7. **Mark done** — the review never edits the progress file. A clean pass hands back so the executing loop can set the requirement's Done cell `✅` (the row was left `🔄` while under review) and write its execution-summary row; findings leave the row `🔄` for another pass. (At the feature-level review every row is already terminal — verify none regressed and move on.) Already-terminal rows of other requirements never regress. Done means reviewed, not just committed.\n\n## Principles\n\n- **Tracing and spec alignment are the core** — they catch what tests miss: untested branches, missing criteria, scope creep.\n- **Fix smells in place; flag everything else.** Keep the review scoped — the goal is polish on the requirement that just landed, not a redesign pass.\n- **Be proportional** — a one-function change doesn't need the depth of a batch pipeline; a `Review: inline` tag was a deliberate call at design approval — keep the review focused and don't second-guess it.\n\n## After the review\n\nReturn to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` — the next requirement, or the ship checkpoint when every requirement is done. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.\n- Optional first line: `// @options: {\"max_output_tokens\": 10000, \"timeout_ms\": 60000}`\n\nGlobals:\n- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.\n- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.\n- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.\n- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /Users/yinlootan/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.\n\nNested tools:\n\n### `read`\nRead the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.\n\n- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { read(args: {\n  // Maximum number of lines to read\n  limit?: number;\n  // Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)\n  offset?: number;\n  // Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)\n  path: string;\n}): Promise<string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: \"image\"; }>; };\n```\n\n### `bash`\nExecute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.\n\n- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { bash(args: {\n  // Shell command to execute\n  command: string;\n  // Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)\n  timeout?: number;\n}): Promise<{\n  exit_code: number;\n  // Full output, when truncated\n  full_output_path?: string;\n  // Combined stdout and stderr, possibly truncated\n  output: string;\n  truncated: boolean;\n  wall_time_seconds: number;\n}>; };\n```\n\n### `edit`\nEdit a single file using exact text replacement. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.\n\n- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)\n- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls\n- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.\n- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { edit(args: {\n  // One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.\n  edits: Array<{\n    // Replacement text for this targeted edit.\n    newText: string;\n    // Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.\n    oldText: string;\n  }>;\n  // Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)\n  path: string;\n}): Promise<string>; };\n```\n\n### `write`\nWrite content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.\n\n- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.\n\ncodemode tool declaration:\n```ts\ndeclare const tools: { write(args: {\n  // Content to write to the file\n  content: string;\n  // Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)\n  path: string;\n}): Promise<string>; };\n```","parameters":{"type":"object","required":["code"],"properties":{"code":{"type":"string","description":"Raw JavaScript source."}}},"constrainedSampling":{"type":"grammar","variants":{"openai_lark":"\nstart: options_source | plain_source\noptions_source: OPTIONS_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE\nplain_source: SOURCE\n\nOPTIONS_LINE: /[ \\t]*\\/\\/ @options:[^\\r\\n]*/\nNEWLINE: /\\r?\\n/\nSOURCE: /[\\s\\S]+/\n"}}}]}}

+{"type":"message","id":"19d85af2","parentId":"b7077c9e","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:54:04.195Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_63j0owDW5ZzGRQP1zm7A2961","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.5 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"==> text 1/2 <==\n---\nname: pwk-brainstorming\ndescription: \"Use this before any creative work — creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores intent and design, then writes the single buildable design doc (requirements with acceptance criteria + review tags) that pwk-executing-tasks builds from. Use this skill whenever the user describes something they want to build, change, or improve, even if they don't say 'brainstorm' — phrases like 'I want to add X', 'let's build Y', 'we need a way to Z', or 'help me design' all apply.\"\n---\n\n# Brainstorming\n\nRead-only exploration of source code; every file you create or edit goes under `docs/plans/`. An approved ADR goes to `docs/adr/` — outside the writable boundary, so the human writes it or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`, and the design phase never unlocks it. The design doc is the **single buildable artifact**: each requirement carries its own acceptance criteria and review tags, and the executor builds straight from it. Source-writing happens in `pwk-executing-tasks`.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Proportionality: trivial vs non-trivial\n\nClassify the change at the start.\n\n- **Trivial** — a typo or obvious bugfix with no open design questions, a config or version bump, a single-function change, or anything the human flags as trivial. Skip steps 3–6: read the design-format reference, run the validator in step 7, and write a **minimal** design doc in one turn — an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach), one `### R1:` block with criteria and tags, an optional `## Production-risk areas` line, and deliberately **no `## Feature acceptance`** (a trivial slice ships on the full existing suite; no E2E is manufactured). Hand off to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks`. The guard still enforces read-only — trivial compresses the phase to one turn, it does not skip it.\n- **Non-trivial** — open design questions, multiple approaches, cross-module impact, or new behavior. Run the full process below.\n\nWhen unsure, ask: \"This looks trivial — fast-path it, or full brainstorm?\" Default to full.\n\n## Scope and granularity\n\n**One design doc = one PR; one requirement = one testable slice within it.** Most work is a single design doc; several requirements serving one cohesive outcome do not force an umbrella.\n\nA large request with distinct testable outcomes that need separate design/execute cycles becomes an **umbrella** of vertical slices with one-line scopes and a build order, approved before you write an overview or design. A layers-only split (database, API, UI) is not vertical — each slice delivers testable behavior. Design only the current slice, grounded in implemented code, not speculative sibling designs; the umbrella still ships as one PR on one branch, finalized once.\n\n**One folder per topic:** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/`, holding `<leaf>-design.md`, `<leaf>-progress.md`, and `<leaf>-review-packet*.md`; `<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic, and more than one leaf adds `overview.md`. The folder is the creation, discovery, and disposal unit.\n\n**Umbrella trigger:** before proposing a new umbrella, or when discovery finds an `overview.md` beside this design, read [references/umbrella.md](references/umbrella.md) — it owns the status-free roster, the first/later-slice procedures, and header-only predecessor reporting. Build order is advisory, not a gate, and an existing roster means the split is already decided; design the current slice against it.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Check git state** — `git status` + `git log --oneline -5`. Uncommitted work? Ask the user what to do first.\n2. **Discovery** *(skip in a brand-new repo with no `docs/plans/`)* — first verify the repo root: run `pwd` (or your shell's equivalent) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; mismatch → report both paths and stop; never `cd` (a worktree root counts). Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md`, `*-progress.md`, and `overview.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; report in-flight topics and any active umbrella, each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`; design-only topics report `design` — no body ingest). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   If the idea continues an existing topic, ask whether to extend it or start fresh. An `overview.md` **beside the design doc** means the split is already decided — read it for the roster and design this part’s `<leaf>-design.md` against it.\n3. **Understand the idea** — **PRD brief.** With source material (a PRD, ticket, or spec — pasted text, a path, a URL), open with a brief before any question: **Background** (the problem, why now, who is affected — each product claim cites its PRD section), **Current situation** (what the code does today — each claim cites `file:line`), **The delta** (what must change, each line naming a requirement candidate, and what stays untouched). Zero-context rule: plain meaning first, the pointer second — quote non-English domain terms with a plain-English gloss and mark anything uncited `(interpretation: …)`. Unreadable source material: report the blocker, ground on code only, name the gap. The human corrects the brief before frontier rounds; confirmed facts weave into the design doc, with no sidecar file. No source material, no brief. Then read only enough code, docs, and commits to ground the design, and **check `docs/lessons.md`**.\n\n   Ask questions in **frontier rounds** — the frontier is every question whose prerequisites are settled. Build the tree by walking every checklist dimension (*Goal & scope · Data & state · Behavior & edge cases · Errors & failure · Integration · Non-functional*), print `— nothing to ask` for empty groups, and ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question (`Q1`, `Q2`, …) with your recommended answer (`➡️ <recommendation>`) so the human confirms, strikes, or corrects each in one reply. A question that depends on another still-open one waits for a later round; recompute the frontier after each round.\n\n   **Facts vs. decisions:** anything answerable from the codebase, docs, or tools is looked up — recon scout or inline — never asked of the human; a pending lookup holds only its downstream questions while the rest of the frontier is asked now. **Runnable facts:** an unknown observable by running something — behavior, timing, output, layout — is settled by a bounded sketch, never asked of the human and never guessed: an inline interpreter or a file under `docs/plans/<topic>/`, no installs, no source writes. Record it where it lands as `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` and list it in the round summary so the human can strike it; a sketch result that would set business behavior still passes the assumption gate; inconclusive or blocked → record `INCONCLUSIVE` plus one line of what ran, and the question returns to the human with the result attached. A cheaper read beats a run when reading can decide, and only decisions are asked.\n\n   Major approvals stay single-decision — one question each, never batched: approach selection (step 5), umbrella split, design approval, ADR offer. The interview ends when the frontier is empty — every branch visited, nothing left silently assumed — not when you feel you understand. Then present a short summary and ask: \"Should I proceed, or is there more?\" The human decides when to move on.\n4. **(skipped on trivial changes)** **Codebase recon** — for a non-trivial topic with prior art, request the host’s `codebase-recon` capability using the logical `pwk-recon-scout` role: a fresh-context, read-only, bounded worker given the topic, one-line intent, and repo root. Use its 5-section map (Relevant files, Existing patterns, Call sites, Test layout, Gotchas) as grounding for steps 5–6 instead of reading those files inline; the scout reports observations only, never design recommendations. No compatible capability, or constraints it cannot enforce → report `Scout: unavailable` and do the same recon inline, preserving the five-section map and `file:line` citations; never omit recon silently.\n5. **Explore approaches** — propose 2–3, leading with your recommendation, and sketch the concrete interface (types, signatures, example caller) for each so the comparison is grounded in code rather than abstractions.\n6. **Present the design** in one pass, organized into sections (architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing) — the human comments on any section; re-present only revised sections.\n\n   **Assumptions to confirm first** — before presenting, sweep the drafted design: every unconfirmed assumption it would bake in (business rules, defaults, edge-case resolutions) re-opens as a numbered question with your recommended answer, for one reply. An honest empty gate (\"no unconfirmed assumptions\") when the draft is clean — never invent items. Hard rule: no business behavior enters the design doc on the agent's assumption; confirmed facts are woven into existing sections, with no new template section.\n\n   Identified a significant architectural decision? Offer an ADR in `docs/adr/`, only when all three hold: **hard to reverse**, **surprising without context**, **a real trade-off**. Format: title + 1–3 sentences of context/decision/why. ADRs are permanent institutional memory — never archived or rotated. (Guard note: the human writes the approved ADR or briefly runs `/pwk-guard off`; you never write it while the design phase is gated.)\n7. **Write the design doc** — validate its structure before handing off. Read [references/design-format.md](references/design-format.md) first for the exact format, tag defaults, risk/Setup rules, and audit; requirement blocks carry acceptance criteria plus `### Checkpoints` / `### Review` tags. Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`. Write `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md`, creating the topic folder when absent. It is descriptive, not a task list — the executor builds directly from it.\n\n   **Completion gate:** Test observable behavior through the public interface. Audit every requirement’s criteria, tags, and risk notes — each appears exactly once. A criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; a criterion with no nameable probe sends the requirement back for splitting or rephrasing, and design-doc criteria never name tests — the probe materializes at execution. For non-trivial work, finish with an end-to-end `## Feature acceptance` as the primary enforced spec. If writing a scenario step would require inventing behavior, that invention goes back through the assumption gate: an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement, not permission to guess. Keep the design descriptive, not a task list. It is the single buildable artifact; no separate implementation plan.\n\n## Trivial format\n\nA trivial design has an `In short:` one-liner (what + why + approach), a single `### R1:` block with acceptance criteria and tags, and optional `## Production-risk areas`. It has no `## At a glance`, `## Requirements`, or `## Feature acceptance`; its ship gate is the full existing suite, not a manufactured E2E. The block rules below cover it.\n\n```markdown\n# Design: <topic>\n\nIn short: <what + why + approach>\n\n### R1: <name>\n<observable behavior>\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given <state>, When <action>, Then <observable outcome>.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n```\n\n## Non-trivial format\n\n**Open with `## At a glance`** — the human's two-minute digest, immediately before `## Requirements`: (1) a 2–4 sentence plain-language summary of what is wrong or needed, what will be built, and the key approach; (2) **Key decisions** — one line each: decision + why, with a `(rejected: <alternative> — <reason>)` clause only when the fork was real (never manufactured); (3) a table `| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |`, exactly one row per requirement, where **R# = the requirement's block number in the `## Requirements` section below** — the ID every later digest keys on. Plain language only: no jargon, no Given/When/Then — those live in the requirement blocks. An umbrella overview gains no at-a-glance section; its roster serves that role.\n\nThen **`## Requirements`** — one `### R<n>: <name>` block per requirement, each one testable behavior:\n\n```markdown\n## Requirements\n\n### R1: <name>\n<one-line testable behavior — what the feature produces or changes, through its public interface>\n\n**Acceptance criteria** — Given/When/Then criteria defining \"done\". Test observable behavior — what the feature produces or changes through its public interface; not implementation steps. Cover edge and error cases.\n- Given … When … Then …\n- Given … When … Then … (edge case)\n\n### Checkpoints: none | full\n### Review: skip | parallel | inline\n\n### Production-risk notes\n- <only when the requirement touches a risk area>\n\n### R2: <name>\n…\n```\n\nBlock rules:\n\n- **No test-name lists.** The criteria are the test spec: the executor writes and names the tests red-green from them, so the doc holds no test-name lists and no R#-to-section map — the block structure is the map.\n- **Tag every requirement** — `### Checkpoints` (`none` = no per-requirement stop, the default; `full` = tests + complete stops) and `### Review` (`skip` = the default; `parallel` = four delegated reviewers; `inline` = one `pwk-code-review` pass). Missing tags default to `none` / `skip`; flag `full` only where complex logic or the feature's main part makes a human look worth the stop.\n- **Nothing is tagged silently here; only the human tags a slice for review.** A requirement touching a production-risk area carries its `### Production-risk notes` and is flagged `⚠ production-risk` in the At-a-glance Risk column — display-only, derived: `⚠ production-risk` if and only if the block carries non-empty notes, never an input; `auto` reads the underlying risk content, never the display column. Its written `### Review` value stays `skip` unless the human sets it — propose the tag in prose; an explicit human tag always wins, both ways.\n- **No per-requirement spec stop, by design** — the criteria were approved at design time; re-checking mid-execution asks a question already answered.\n- **Production-risk notes** — risks involving schema migrations, new dependencies, external APIs, or seed data also get a `## Setup` section (dependencies, migrations, seed data, and how to verify setup worked) between `## Requirements` and `## Feature acceptance`.\n- **Ordering** — dependencies come earlier; the executor runs blocks in listed order with no dependency graph. Aim for vertical slices that merge cleanly on their own.\n\nThen the narrative sections the executor reads as context — problem, approaches considered, architecture, components, data flow, error handling. Head the fork record exactly `## Approaches considered` — finalizing's learning sweep reads it by that name — and **record every real fork and why each loser lost**; the executor needs the reasoning and finalize harvests it for ADRs.\n\nTouches a production-risk area (DB schema/migrations, auth, external APIs, concurrency/batch, uploads/large data flows, Redis/caching/queues)? Add a brief `## Production-risk areas` **immediately after the last requirement block** — inside the `### R1 → ## Feature acceptance` span, so the review packet carries it verbatim — and mirror the risks into each touched block's `### Production-risk notes`. `pwk-code-review` audits it (per reviewed slice, and always at the feature review); finalize's learning sweep reads it.\n\n**End with `## Feature acceptance`** — one or more end-to-end `Given/When/Then` scenarios proving the requirements *compose* into the feature. It is the feature's definition-of-done and the **primary enforced spec**: `pwk-executing-tasks` writes it as the E2E test first and gates on it. The section carries the feature-level `### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline` tag — the one whole-feature review; default `auto`, which resolves on the design's own production-risk content to `parallel` (all four reviewers) when the design has any — a non-empty `## Production-risk areas` section, or a non-empty `### Production-risk notes` on any requirement — and to `inline` (one pass) otherwise. An explicit `parallel` or `inline` is written as-is, never resolved. If a scenario step would require inventing behavior, the invention goes back through the assumption gate — never silently into the scenario; an unwritable step means an unspecified requirement.\n\n```markdown\n## Feature acceptance\n\n- Given <starting state>, When <trigger>, Then <end-to-end outcome the feature promises>.\n\n### Feature review: auto | parallel | inline — the one whole-feature review; leave `auto` unless the human says otherwise.\n```\n\nExample (rate limiting): \"Given a new API consumer with no prior usage, When they exceed 100 requests/minute for 3 consecutive minutes, Then they're throttled, a `rate_limited` event is emitted, and further requests return 429.\"\n\n**Audit before finishing:** every requirement block has acceptance criteria and both tags, and each requirement appears **exactly once** — none dropped, none duplicated. Non-trivial docs carry a `## Feature acceptance` section as the primary enforced spec; a trivial doc ends after its `### R1:` block and ships on the full suite. Production-risk areas appear in the blocks that touch them. The probe test: a criterion is ready only when its `Then` names an outcome a command can observe — a run, a grep, or an assertion; one with no nameable probe goes back for splitting or rephrasing, and criteria never name tests. A fact settled by a sketch carries its proof where it lands — `(settled by sketch: <what ran> → <result>)` — woven into the section it confirms, never a new template section.\n\n## Structural validator contract\n\nRun `scripts/validate-design.py` as directed in the main skill. It reads UTF-8 Markdown without modifying it; headings, tags, and labels inside backtick or tilde fenced examples do not count, so close every fence. Real requirements use unique sequential `### R1: <name>`, `### R2: <name>`, … headings with nonempty names. Each block needs a standalone `**Acceptance criteria**` label in its main body, before any tag or risk-note heading (an explanatory suffix after an em dash, dash, or colon is allowed), with nonempty criteria before the next heading or bold label. A bare bullet or content borrowed from risk notes is not a criterion section.\n\nWrite each selected tag as one value, not the template's pipe-separated alternatives. Missing optional tags retain `Checkpoints: none`, `Review: skip`, and `Feature review: auto`. Non-trivial designs require nonempty `## Feature acceptance` scenarios before their feature-review tag. Only the minimal trivial shape above receives the no-Feature-acceptance exception.\n\nThe helper checks structure, not meaning: it does not prove Given/When/Then quality, testability, edge/error coverage, good slicing, risk classification, confirmed assumptions, or human approval. Those remain the agent's audit and the human's judgment. Structural success does not complete the design gate by itself.\n"}],"details":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_2lKGBN8Em788MyZXeCvo6155/1","name":"read","args":"{\"path\":\"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-brainstorming/references/design-format.md\"}","status":"ok","durationMs":11.464375000010477}]},"isError":false,"durationMs":115,"timestamp":1791978916760,"nestedCalls":{"calls":[{"id":"call_00_2lKGBN8Em788MyZXeCvo6155/1","name":"read","status":"ok","arguments":{"path":"/Users/yinlootan/src/pwk-probe-kit-candidate/skills/pwk-brainstorming/references/design-format.md"},"durationMs":11}],"complete":true}}}

The filter lives on the existing `summarize(text, { since })` seam so it stays directly testable; the CLI shim only parses the flag and reports errors.\n\n**Key decisions**\n- Filter inside `summarize` via an optional options object, since parsed and validated there — keeps one tested seam and a dumb CLI shim. (rejected: separate exported `parseSince`/`filterBySince` helpers — two more public surfaces for a 22-line script; rejected: filter in the CLI only — logic outside the tested seam)\n- Unparseable `--since` throws rather than yielding an empty summary — a typo'd date must not look like \"no activity\".\n- Validate with `Date.parse` + `NaN` check rather than a strict ISO gate — matches \"unparseable is an error\", already rejects `nonsense`, `\"\"`, `2026-13-45`; accepts zone-less datetimes in host-local time. (rejected: strict ISO regex gate — rejects forms the requirement doesn't call invalid)\n- Boundary inclusive (`time >= since`) — the request excludes entries *older* than the date, so an entry exactly at it is kept.\n- Entries with a missing or unparseable `time` are dropped when `since` is given — they cannot be shown to fall in the window — but still counted when it is absent.\n- `first`/`last` keep their existing lexicographic computation — out of scope, no behavior change.\n\n| R# | Requirement in one line | Risk |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R1 | `summarize(text, { since })` keeps only events at or after `since`, and throws on an unparseable `since` | |\n| R2 | The CLI accepts `--since <date>` / `--since=<date>` and exits 1 with a stderr message on an unparseable date | |\n\n## Requirements\n\n### R1: Window filter in `summarize`\n`summarize(text, { since })` counts only events whose `time` is at or after `since`; with no `since` it behaves exactly as today; an unparseable `since` throws.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given a `since` between two events' times, When `summarize` runs, Then only the later event is counted and appears in `first`/`last`.\n- Given an event whose `time` equals `since`, When `summarize` runs, Then that event is counted (inclusive boundary).\n- Given events with no `time` and with an unparseable `time`, When `since` is set, Then neither is counted.\n- Given the same events, When `since` is omitted, Then counts and `first`/`last` are unchanged from current behavior.\n- Given an unparseable `since` such as `\"nonsense\"`, When `summarize` runs, Then it throws an `Error` naming the bad value.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n\n### R2: `--since` CLI flag\nThe CLI forwards `--since` to `summarize` and turns an invalid date into a nonzero exit with a stderr message.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given a JSONL file and `--since <date>`, When the script runs, Then stdout is the filtered summary JSON.\n- Given `--since=<date>` in the same invocation, When the script runs, Then the result matches the space-separated form.\n- Given an unparseable `--since` value, When the script runs, Then stderr carries the invalid-date message, the exit code is `1`, and no summary JSON is printed.\n- Given `--since` as the final argument with no value, When the script runs, Then it exits `1` with the same invalid-date message.\n- Then list `docs/plans` recursively, excluding docs/plans/completed/, for `*-design.md` (topic docs live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` folders — archived work is not in flight). Use whatever recurses in your harness; one example: `find docs/plans -name '<suffix>' -not -path '*/completed/*'`; take each topic’s `Feature phase:` line header-only (`grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' <file>`). With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every phase extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   No doc → ask for `/skill:pwk-brainstorming`; several → ask which. Start at `Feature phase: e2e-written` (trivial doc: `implementing (0/N)`); `Setup: pending` when the design has `## Setup`, otherwise `Setup: n/a`.\n3. **Setup pre-flight** *(only if the design doc has a `## Setup` section)* — install dependencies, apply migrations, seed data, then run the suite. **⏸ CHECKPOINT: setup** — present results and wait for approval, then set `Setup: done`.\n4. **Commit the design docs** — `git add docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/ && git commit -m \"docs: add design doc\"`, scoped to the topic folder so another topic’s drafts never ride it.\n5. **Write the feature-acceptance E2E test (red)** — encode the `## Feature acceptance` section as a real test, run it, confirm it **fails**. Iterate to green; fixing the implementation is the default, and you **stop and present only when you are genuinely blocked** (nothing makes it pass, or the E2E itself is wrong).\n6. **Notice, not a stop — report the E2E and continue.** Post 1–2 plain-language lines stating **what the E2E proves** (\"this test proves that …\") plus its failing output, then go straight into the implement phase **without waiting for approval** — the `## Feature acceptance` text was approved during brainstorm.\n\n## Resume and progress\n\n`Feature phase` is one of: `e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`.\n\n**Done cell:** `⬜` not started · `🔄` in progress · `✅` done · `❌` failed · `⏭` skipped. This reference owns the unchanged progress artifact schema.\n\n2. **Create the progress file** `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md`, beside the design doc it belongs to (`<leaf>` is `<topic>` for a single-part topic; an umbrella part uses its roster slug). Keep the blank lines between the header fields: the blank lines are load-bearing, because CommonMark merges consecutive plain lines into one paragraph.\n\n   ```markdown\n   # Progress: <topic>\n\n   Design: docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md\n\n   Branch: <branch>\n\n   Setup: n/a\n\n   Started: <ISO timestamp>\n\n   Last updated: <ISO timestamp>\n\n   Feature phase: e2e-written\n\n   <!-- a trivial design doc (no `## Feature acceptance`) starts at `implementing (0/N)` -->\n\n   ## Requirements\n   | # | Done | Requirement | Per-req ceremony | Commit |\n   |---|------|-------------|-----------------|--------|\n   | 1 | ⬜ | <requirement name> | — | — |\n\n   ## Execution summary\n   | R# | Requirement | How it was built | Deviated? | Evidence |\n   |----|-------------|------------------|-----------|----------|\n   | 1 | <requirement name> | | | |\n\n   ## Deviation records\n\n   <!-- One short paragraph per design-decision reversal -->\n\n   ## Code digest\n\n   <!-- Written once, after the feature review passes; never back-filled per requirement. -->\n\n   ### Summary\n   ### Flow\n   - **Spine** — `<entry point> -> [R1] <step> -> [R2] <step> -> <outcome>`\n   - **Branches**\n     - `<condition> -> <outcome>` [R2]\n     - `<changed behavior> — was: <previous behavior>`\n   - **Side effects** — reads: `<what>` · writes: `<what>`\n   ### Gotchas\n   - <one real risk per bullet>\n   ### Key files\n   - `<file>` — <what shifted inside it>\n   ```\n\n   The `## Code digest` is filled once, at the write point in the ship checkpoint — never back-filled per requirement. Fill rules: plain language, R# anchors where natural, no test names. `### Summary` is 2–3 sentences: what the code now does differently, and why. `### Flow` uses `A -> B -> C` arrow chains, one spine or branch per bullet line. `### Gotchas` lifts real risks from the review findings, one real risk per bullet — `[ALERT]` only for reviewer-confirmed issues, never invented; with none, write `none beyond review findings`. `### Key files` is capped at 5 pivotal files, one bullet each.\n\n   **Flow shape** — the ship stop's navigable map, the one digest section carrying structure:\n   - **Spine** — the happy path, each hop named by symbol — no line numbers, no file paths (those go stale). Tag each hop `[R<n>]`, so coverage verdicts trace into the code.\n   - **Branches** — every alternative and error path as `condition -> outcome`; a bare spine reads as \"no edge cases\". Put ⚠️ on the surprising ones, and a `was: <previous behavior>` clause on each requirement whose behavior changed — skip it for purely additive ones.\n   - **Inline worked values** — a non-obvious mapping shown concretely (`` `implementing (2/5)` -> `execute 2/5` ``).\n   - **Side effects** — what is read and written, only for I/O, network, or migrations; otherwise omit the bullet.\n   - **Cap: roughly 15 lines.** A longer Flow gets the ship checkpoint's `/skill:pwk-walkthrough` offer instead.\n\n   `Feature phase` is one of: `e2e-written`, `implementing (k/N)`, `reviewing`, `ship-paused`, `done`.\n\n   The `Setup:` header slot takes one of `Setup: pending | done | n/a` — the header starts `Setup: pending` when the design doc has a `## Setup` section, else `Setup: n/a`; the setup checkpoint flips it to `done` on approval. The phase line stays `e2e-written` through the setup stop, and the E2E is written after setup.\n\n## Progress file\n\nUpdate the matching row directly, never via pattern matching (which corrupts the table). Update `Last updated` and `Feature phase` on every change.\n\n**Row vocabulary (canonical — this file owns it):**\n\n- **Done cell:** `⬜` not started · `🔄` in progress · `✅` done · `❌` failed · `⏭` skipped. A row is **terminal** when its Done cell is `✅`, `❌`, or `⏭` — resolved, not necessarily passed. +{"type":"message","id":"4e34ea97","parentId":"22f3612b","timestamp":"2026-10-14T11:59:12.630Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_00_ET_0F8M2CnYTD7jRTrQu7pf1436","toolName":"codemode","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.1 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"text","text":"==> text 1/3 <==\nprogress updated\n==> text 2/3 <==\n=== review.md ===\n# Review mechanics and packet helper\n\nRead before any review, packet refresh, or digest write.\n\n## Assemble evidence\n\n**Assemble the review packet first** — once, by script, so that no packet byte passes through model output. The Commit column fixes both spans: feature base = `git rev-parse <first Commit-column entry>^`, the parent of the first recorded commit; a requirement packet spans the previous requirement's last commit (exclusive) to this one's last commit (inclusive), R1's exclusive bound being its own parent. No `merge-base` guessing. Commits landing mid-review → re-run the recipe before spawning a replacement role, so the packet matches HEAD:\n\nUse the installed skill directory, not a repository checkout; a missing runtime or helper (`python3 --version` ≥ 3.9) → report it and stop, with no auto-install or fallback.\n\n```sh\npython3 \"<executing-skill-dir>/scripts/build-review-packet.py\" \\\n  --project \"<repo-root>\" \\\n  --design \"docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-design.md\" \\\n  --progress \"docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-progress.md\" \\\n  --scope feature\n```\n\nFor an opt-in requirement review, the same invocation with `--scope requirement --requirement 2` (substitute the number): destination `<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`, versus the feature packet's `<design doc's directory>/<leaf>-review-packet.md`. Requirement-suffixed packets never overwrite each other or the feature packet.\n\n`--project` resolves from the caller's cwd and must name the Git worktree root; design/progress paths are absolute or relative to it and must be matched leaf files in one active `docs/plans/<topic>/` folder. The helper derives the destination and refuses a symlink; to pass arguments programmatically, use a list, never shell interpolation.\n\nThe packet retains, in order: `## Commits`, `## Changed files`, `## Acceptance criteria (verbatim from the design doc)`, `## Feature acceptance (verbatim)` (empty for a trivial design), `## Production-risk notes (verbatim, if any)`, `## Diff`.\n\nCriteria and production-risk content stay verbatim, including every line of multiple risk blocks; a fenced template heading never routes extraction. Feature criteria span from the first real requirement to Feature acceptance (or document end); a requirement packet covers only its own block, keeping design-level production-risk areas as context. The helper excludes generated `*-review-packet*.md` files from diff/stat, including committed packets.\n\nA Commit cell is one immutable hexadecimal ID or an ordered whitespace-separated list — preserve the first ID, append review-fix IDs in order. Only terminal failed/skipped rows may lack a commit, and requirement assembly never guesses a bound across such a row. Anything missing, malformed, or non-ancestral → correct the record from evidence and rerun. The helper never edits progress, commits, or approves, replacing a packet only after all parse/Git work succeeds. A nonzero exit is failure, not evidence: report stderr and stop delegation.\n\nAfter late fixes, commit, append the IDs to the selected row, and refresh the packet; feature packets refresh HEAD automatically. Re-run the helper before any replacement reviewer, and before digest writing if stale or missing. Then re-green the full suite + E2E and finish the checkpoint.\n\n## Delegate or review inline\n\n- **`parallel`** (the `auto` resolution when risk content is present) — request the host's `parallel-review` capability for four fresh-context, read-only roles: `pwk-spec-reviewer`, `pwk-tracing-reviewer`, `pwk-smell-reviewer`, `pwk-hazard-reviewer`. Spawn each with a **one-liner** pointing at the packet file, role framing last — the checklist name (`spec alignment`, `code tracing`, `code smells`, `production hazards`), e.g. `Read docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/<leaf>-review-packet.md. Your role: spec alignment.` The packet never appears in spawn arguments. Require independent execution and one collected outcome per role; the contracts live in `agents/pwk-*-reviewer.md`. Reviewers only report — you apply smell fixes (full suite + E2E green, commit) and flag trace/spec/hazard findings for the human.\n- **`inline`** — perform `/skill:pwk-code-review` over the whole diff as a single pass.\n- **Fallback** — no compatible parallel-review capability, unprovable read-only/fresh-context/bounded constraints, or failed delegation → perform the missing review work inline. Retain successful delegated reports; never mark the feature fully reviewed while a required role is missing.\n==> text 3/3 <==\n=== pwk-code-review SKILL.md ===\n---\nname: pwk-code-review\ndescription: \"Review a completed requirement's code — trace the logic, check spec alignment against the acceptance criteria, fix code smells, and run a production hazard check. Runs as the feature-level review in pwk-executing-tasks (whole feature diff), or per-requirement when tagged. Unlocked: may edit code to apply smell fixes.\"\n---\n\n# Code Review\n\nReview the code just implemented — one tagged requirement, or the whole feature at the feature-level review. **Unlocked** — you may edit code to apply smell fixes; flag everything else as a follow-up.\n\nAny command or tool recipe in this skill is an example, not the requirement — when your host grants a better tool for an operation (a sandboxed batch executor — e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0 — a structured file API), use the better tool and treat the recipe as a fallback; the only exact exceptions are this kit's `scripts/` helpers and plain `git` invocations, whose deterministic output is the point.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Identify the scope** — in the feature-gate flow (the default) you review the **whole feature diff** at the feature-level review (`git diff $FEATURE_BASE...HEAD`, `$FEATURE_BASE` being the parent of the first Commit-column entry; see the executing skill's packet recipe), with every design-doc acceptance criterion and the `## Feature acceptance` E2E in scope. Invoked per-requirement (`Review: inline` on a tagged requirement, or inline-completing a missing delegated role when the tag is `parallel`), the scope is that requirement alone — read its acceptance criteria from the design doc and use `git log --oneline -5` plus `git diff` to see what changed. Invoked standalone — no invoking skill, no design doc, no packet — review the span the user names (the working-tree diff, or the branch's commits against its parent): tracing, smell fixes, and the hazard check run as usual, while spec alignment has no criteria to key on — say so and judge the diff against its stated intent rather than manufacturing a coverage table. When the invoking skill already assembled a packet (the feature packet, or the requirement-scoped `<leaf>-review-packet-r<N>.md`), work from the packet — it is the scope of record; re-derive nothing it states.\n\n2. **🔍 Code tracing** — trace the new or changed code paths end-to-end against the acceptance criteria and the feature E2E (a trivial design doc has no feature E2E — its acceptance criteria alone are the spec). For each path, determine whether data flows correctly from entry to the asserted outcome. Note any branch the tests do not exercise, any dead branch, or any path where the trace breaks.\n\n3. **📐 Spec alignment** — for each acceptance criterion, point to the code and the test that satisfy it. A criterion with no covering code or no test is a **gap**. Code that does more than the criteria specify is **scope creep** — flag it.\n\n   **Open the report with a coverage table** — one row per requirement in scope, keyed by the design doc's `### R<n>:` headings (R# = n; the whole design doc at the feature-level review, just the tagged requirement when invoked per-requirement):\n\n   | R# | Verdict | Evidence |\n   |----|---------|----------|\n   | 1 | <verdict> | file:line (code), file:line (test) |\n\n   Verdict per requirement: `covered | gap | scope-creep` — `covered` = every criterion has covering code and a test; `gap` = a criterion lacks code or a test; `scope-creep` = the code does more than the criteria specify; findings elaborate on every non-`covered` row, and an all-`covered` table needs no elaboration.\n\n4. **🧹 Code smells — fix these directly:** review the changed code and affected files against the requirement and feature scope, then fix what you find.\n   - Shallow modules (interface nearly as complex as implementation)\n   - Duplication\n   - Missing seams or premature abstraction\n   - Poor naming, magic values, dead code\n   Apply the fix, re-run the full suite (must stay green), and commit. Only a smell that requires a refactor large enough to risk the requirement is **flagged** instead of applied.\n\n5. **⚠️ Production hazard check** — audit the changed code against the high-risk hazards. For each, write `[SAFE]` (1-line justification) or `[TRIGGERED]` (concrete mitigation):\n   1. **Unbounded operations** — multi-key deletions/scans (`KEYS`, raw `SCAN` loops), full-table loads filtered in memory\n   2. **Missing indexes** — hot queries on unindexed columns (table scans under load)\n   3. **Unbounded concurrency** — unthrottled fan-out (`Promise.all` without batch limits)\n   4. **Long-running transactions** — holding DB connections/locks across slow external calls\n   5. **Query/command interpolation** — raw variables merged into SQL or shell (injection)\n   6. **Unrestricted uploads / temp flooding** — uploads to local temp without limits or `finally` cleanup\n   7. **Silent swallowing loops** — background workers catching/suppressing exceptions without logging/back-off\n   Also check the design's `## Production-risk areas`, if any.\n\n6. **Report** — summarize: tracing findings, spec gaps, smells fixed (with commits), hazards `[TRIGGERED]`. Non-trivial findings become follow-up items — the user decides whether to address now or defer.\n7. **Mark done** — the review never edits the progress file. A clean pass hands back so the executing loop can set the requirement's Done cell `✅` (the row was left `🔄` while under review) and write its execution-summary row; findings leave the row `🔄` for another pass. (At the feature-level review every row is already terminal — verify none regressed and move on.) Already-terminal rows of other requirements never regress. Done means reviewed, not just committed.\n\n## Principles\n\n- **Tracing and spec alignment are the core** — they catch what tests miss: untested branches, missing criteria, scope creep.\n- **Fix smells in place; flag everything else.** Keep the review scoped — the goal is polish on the requirement that just landed, not a redesign pass.\n- **Be proportional** — a one-function change doesn't need the depth of a batch pipeline; a `Review: inline` tag was a deliberate call at design approval — keep the review focused and don't second-guess it.\n\n## After the review\n\nReturn to `/skill:pwk-executing-tasks` — the next requirement, or the ship checkpoint when every requirement is done. with no\n`since` it behaves exactly as today; an unparseable `since` throws.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given a `since` between two events' times, When `summarize` runs, Then only the later event is counted and appears as both `first` and `last`.\n- Given an event whose `time` equals `since`, When `summarize` runs, Then that event is counted (inclusive boundary).\n- Given events with no `time` and with an unparseable `time`, When `since` is set, Then neither is counted.\n- Given the same events, When `since` is omitted, Then counts and `first`/`last` are byte-for-byte the current behavior.\n- Given an unparseable `since` such as `\"nonsense\"`, When `summarize` runs, Then it throws an `Error` naming the bad value.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n\n### R2: `--since` CLI flag\nThe CLI forwards `--since` to `summarize` and turns an invalid date into a nonzero exit with a\nstderr message.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- Given a JSONL file and `--since <date>`, When the script runs, Then stdout is the filtered summary JSON.\n- Given `--since=<date>` in the same invocation, When the script runs, Then the result matches the space-separated form.\n- Given an unparseable `--since` value, When the script runs, Then stderr carries the invalid-date message, the exit code is `1`, and no summary JSON is printed.\n- Given `--since` as the final argument with no value, When the script runs, Then it exits `1` with the same invalid-date message.\n- Given no `--since`, When the script runs, Then output is unchanged from current behavior.\n\n### Checkpoints: none\n### Review: skip\n\n## Approaches considered\n\n- **Chosen — optional options object on the existing seam.** `summarize(text, { since })` parses\n  and validates `since` itself. With a sandboxed batch executor (e.g. `codemode` on pi ≥ 1.0.0) the listing and every topic’s `Feature phase:` extraction are one call, returning only the summary lines (adapt the paths to the verified root when your cwd differs):\n\n   ```javascript\n   const designs = (await tools.bash({ command: \"find docs/plans -name '*-design.md' -not -path '*/completed/*' | sort\", timeout: 15 })).output.trim();\n   const files = designs ? designs.split('\\n') : [];\n   const shellq = (s) => \"'\" + s.replace(/'/g, \"'\\\\''\") + \"'\";\n   const heads = await Promise.all(files.map(d =>\n     tools.bash({ command: \"grep -m1 '^Feature phase:' \" + shellq(d.replace('-design.md', '-progress.md')), timeout: 15 }).then(r => r.output.trim() || 'design')));\n   return text(files.map((d, i) => d + ' — ' + heads[i]).join('\\n') || 'no in-flight topics');\n   ```\n\n   More than one topic in flight? --- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/evals/skill-slimming/usage.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
+
+/** Provider-exported usage lines: one JSON object per line, one line per request. */
+export function parseUsageJsonl(text, source = "<usage>") {
+  const records = [];
+  for (const [index, line] of text.split(/\r?\n/).entries()) {
+    if (!line.trim()) continue;
+    let record;
+    try {
+      record = JSON.parse(line);
+    } catch (error) {
+      throw new Error(`${source}:${index + 1}: invalid JSON (${error.message})`);
+    }
+    for (const field of ["trialId", "inputTokens", "outputTokens", "totalTokens"]) {
+      if (!(field in record)) throw new Error(`${source}:${index + 1}: missing ${field}`);
+    }
+    for (const field of ["inputTokens", "outputTokens", "totalTokens"]) {
+      if (!Number.isSafeInteger(record[field]) || record[field] < 0) {
+        throw new Error(`${source}:${index + 1}: ${field} must be a non-negative integer`);
+      }
+    }
+    if (record.totalTokens !== record.inputTokens + record.outputTokens) {
+      throw new Error(`${source}:${index + 1}: totalTokens does not equal inputTokens + outputTokens`);
+    }
+    records.push(record);
+  }
+  return records;
+}
+
+export function recomputeUsage(records) {
+  return records.reduce(
+    (sum, record) => ({
+      inputTokens: sum.inputTokens + record.inputTokens,
+      outputTokens: sum.outputTokens + record.outputTokens,
+      totalTokens: sum.totalTokens + record.totalTokens,
+    }),
+    { inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, totalTokens: 0 },
+  );
+}
+
+export function readUsageJsonl(path) {
+  return parseUsageJsonl(readFileSync(path, "utf8"), path);
+}
diff --git a/tests/evals/skill-slimming/validate.mjs b/tests/evals/skill-slimming/validate.mjs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..39a7d65
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/evals/skill-slimming/validate.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,174 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env node
+/**
+ * Validator for the skill-slimming fidelity/cost probe (skill-slimming-2 R5).
+ *
+ * Reads a recorded probe report and refuses it unless every fact in it can be
+ * recomputed from the raw provider output. It never invokes a provider, a model,
+ * or the network, and it never edits the report.
+ *
+ * Usage: node validate.mjs <report.json>
+ * Exit 0 = accepted (both commits distinct, six trials complete, every assessment
+ * carried with evidence, token totals recomputed, no candidate regression). Exit 1 =
+ * rejected, naming each fault.
+ *
+ * The direction of the cost comparison is a *finding*, not a validity property: the
+ * report also validates when the candidate median is higher, and the validator prints
+ * the direction so the reader sees which way it went. Only structural faults and
+ * unverifiable numbers reject.
+ */
+import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
+import { dirname, isAbsolute, resolve } from "node:path";
+import protocol from "./protocol.json" with { type: "json" };
+import { parseUsageJsonl, recomputeUsage } from "./usage.mjs";
+
+const REQUIRED_ASSESSMENTS = protocol.assessments;
+const VERDICTS = protocol.verdicts;
+const tokensOf = (usage) => [usage?.inputTokens, usage?.outputTokens, usage?.totalTokens];
+
+function median(values) {
+  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
+  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
+  return sorted.length % 2 ? sorted[mid] : Math.round((sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2);
+}
+
+const spread = (values) => Math.max(...values) - Math.min(...values);
+
+const trialIds = (condition) =>
+  Array.from({ length: protocol.trialsPerCondition }, (_, index) => `${condition}-${index + 1}`);
+
+export function validateReport(report, absoluteReportPath) {
+  const errors = [];
+  const reportDir = dirname(resolve(absoluteReportPath));
+  const located = (path) => (isAbsolute(path) ? path : resolve(reportDir, path));
+  const evidenceExists = (path, label) => {
+    if (typeof path !== "string" || !path.trim()) {
+      errors.push(`${label} is missing`);
+      return;
+    }
+    if (!existsSync(located(path))) errors.push(`${label} does not exist: ${located(path)}`);
+  };
+
+  if (!report || typeof report !== "object") return { errors: ["report must be an object"], stats: null };
+
+  for (const condition of protocol.conditions) {
+    const commit = report.commits?.[condition];
+    if (typeof commit !== "string" || !/^[0-9a-f]{7,64}$/i.test(commit)) {
+      errors.push(`${condition} commit must be an explicit git hash`);
+    }
+  }
+  if (report.commits?.baseline && report.commits.baseline === report.commits.candidate) {
+    errors.push("baseline and candidate commits must differ");
+  }
+
+  const trials = new Map((report.trials ?? []).map((trial) => [trial.trialId, trial]));
+  const totals = Object.fromEntries(protocol.conditions.map((condition) => [condition, []]));
+
+  for (const condition of protocol.conditions) {
+    for (const id of trialIds(condition)) {
+      const trial = trials.get(id);
+      if (!trial) {
+        errors.push(`missing trial ${id}`);
+        continue;
+      }
+      evidenceExists(trial.evidence?.transcript, `${id} transcript`);
+      evidenceExists(trial.evidence?.usage, `${id} usage file`);
+
+      for (const name of REQUIRED_ASSESSMENTS) {
+        const assessment = trial.assessments?.find((entry) => entry.name === name);
+        if (!assessment) {
+          errors.push(`${id}: missing assessment verdict for ${name}`);
+          continue;
+        }
+        if (!VERDICTS.includes(assessment.verdict)) {
+          errors.push(`${id}: assessment ${name} has verdict "${assessment.verdict}" (expected ${VERDICTS.join("|")})`);
+        }
+        if (!assessment.evidence) errors.push(`${id}: assessment ${name} has no evidence pointer`);
+        else evidenceExists(assessment.evidence, `${id} ${name} evidence`);
+      }
+
+      if (typeof trial.evidence?.usage === "string" && existsSync(located(trial.evidence.usage))) {
+        try {
+          const measured = recomputeUsage(
+            parseUsageJsonl(readFileSync(located(trial.evidence.usage), "utf8"), trial.evidence.usage),
+          );
+          const recorded = trial.usage ?? {};
+          if (tokensOf(recorded).join(",") !== tokensOf(measured).join(",")) {
+            errors.push(
+              `${id}: recorded totalTokens ${recorded.totalTokens} (input ${recorded.inputTokens}, output ${recorded.outputTokens}) does not match recomputed ${measured.totalTokens} (input ${measured.inputTokens}, output ${measured.outputTokens})`,
+            );
+          }
+          if (Number.isSafeInteger(measured.totalTokens)) totals[condition].push(measured.totalTokens);
+        } catch (error) {
+          errors.push(`${id}: ${error.message}`);
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  for (let index = 0; index < protocol.trialsPerCondition; index += 1) {
+    const candidate = trials.get(`candidate-${index + 1}`);
+    const baseline = trials.get(`baseline-${index + 1}`);
+    if (!candidate || !baseline) continue;
+    for (const name of REQUIRED_ASSESSMENTS) {
+      const before = baseline.assessments?.find((entry) => entry.name === name)?.verdict;
+      const after = candidate.assessments?.find((entry) => entry.name === name)?.verdict;
+      if (before === "pass" && after === "fail") {
+        errors.push(`candidate-${index + 1} regresses ${name} against baseline-${index + 1}`);
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  const complete = protocol.conditions.every((condition) => totals[condition].length === protocol.trialsPerCondition);
+  let stats = null;
+  if (complete) {
+    stats = Object.fromEntries(
+      protocol.conditions.map((condition) => [
+        condition,
+        { totals: totals[condition], median: median(totals[condition]), spread: spread(totals[condition]) },
+      ]),
+    );
+    stats.direction = stats.candidate.median < stats.baseline.median ? "lower" : "higher-or-equal";
+    stats.delta = stats.candidate.median - stats.baseline.median;
+  } else {
+    errors.push("cannot compare: the two conditions do not each have complete recomputed totals");
+  }
+
+  return { errors, stats };
+}
+
+const isCli = process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === new URL(`file://${resolve(process.argv[1])}`).href;
+if (isCli) {
+  const target = process.argv[2];
+  if (!target) {
+    console.error("usage: node validate.mjs <report.json>");
+    process.exit(1);
+  }
+  let result;
+  try {
+    result = validateReport(JSON.parse(readFileSync(target, "utf8")), target);
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error(`report cannot be read: ${error.message}`);
+    process.exit(1);
+  }
+  if (result.stats) {
+    const { baseline, candidate } = result.stats;
+    console.log("condition  trials              median total tokens  spread");
+    console.log(
+      `baseline   ${baseline.totals.join(", ")}${" ".repeat(Math.max(1, 20 - baseline.totals.join(", ").length))}${baseline.median}${" ".repeat(19)}${baseline.spread}`,
+    );
+    console.log(
+      `candidate  ${candidate.totals.join(", ")}${" ".repeat(Math.max(1, 20 - candidate.totals.join(", ").length))}${candidate.median}${" ".repeat(19)}${candidate.spread}`,
+    );
+  }
+  if (result.stats) {
+    const { baseline, candidate, direction, delta } = result.stats;
+    console.log(
+      `finding: candidate median ${candidate.median} vs baseline median ${baseline.median} -> ${direction} (${delta >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${delta})`,
+    );
+  }
+  if (result.errors.length) {
+    for (const error of result.errors) console.error(`✖ ${error}`);
+    process.exit(1);
+  }
+  console.log("✓ probe report accepted");
+}
diff --git a/tests/skill-budgets.test.ts b/tests/skill-budgets.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a68e23d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/skill-budgets.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
+import { cpSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
+import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
+import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
+
+/**
+ * R1 — the ratchet's two quieter teeth: an unbudgeted file and a restated rule must both
+ * fail the gate. The feature E2E covers the loud case (a file past its budget); these are
+ * what stop the corpus from creeping back in unnoticed.
+ */
+const repoRoot = dirname(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
+const KIT_PATHS = [
+  "skills",
+  "agents",
+  "extensions/workflow-guard.ts",
+  "AGENTS.md",
+  "README.md",
+  "docs/lessons.md",
+  "docs/oversight-model.md",
+  "docs/developer-usage-guide.md",
+  "docs/workflow-phases.md",
+];
+const KIT_TESTS = ["skill-lint.mjs", "markers.mjs", "prescription-sweep.mjs"];
+
+function copyKit(prefix: string): string {
+  const kit = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
+  for (const rel of KIT_PATHS) {
+    const target = join(kit, rel);
+    mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
+    cpSync(join(repoRoot, rel), target, { recursive: true });
+  }
+  mkdirSync(join(kit, "tests"), { recursive: true });
+  for (const name of KIT_TESTS) cpSync(join(repoRoot, "tests", name), join(kit, "tests", name));
+  return kit;
+}
+
+function runSkillLint(cwd: string) {
+  const result = spawnSync("node", [join(cwd, "tests", "skill-lint.mjs")], { encoding: "utf8" });
+  return { status: result.status, output: `${result.stdout}${result.stderr}` };
+}
+
+describe("skill word budgets (R1)", () => {
+  it("fails on a markdown file under skills/ that no budget covers", () => {
+    const kit = copyKit("pwk-slim-unbudgeted-");
+    try {
+      const rel = "skills/pwk-status/references/brand-new.md";
+      mkdirSync(dirname(join(kit, rel)), { recursive: true });
+      writeFileSync(
+        join(kit, rel),
+        "# Brand new\n\nA file the budget table has never seen, long enough to be prose an agent would load and pay for.\n",
+      );
+      const { status, output } = runSkillLint(kit);
+      expect(status, "an unbudgeted file must fail the gate").not.toBe(0);
+      expect(output).toContain(rel);
+    } finally {
+      rmSync(kit, { recursive: true, force: true });
+    }
+  });
+
+  it("fails when a file states the same long sentence twice", () => {
+    const kit = copyKit("pwk-slim-restated-");
+    try {
+      const rel = "skills/pwk-status/SKILL.md";
+      const sentence = "Match the phase header line and route the session from the first nonterminal requirement row.";
+      const file = join(kit, rel);
+      writeFileSync(file, `${readFileSync(file, "utf8")}\n\n${sentence}\n\n${sentence}\n`);
+      const { status, output } = runSkillLint(kit);
+      expect(status, "a restated rule must fail the gate").not.toBe(0);
+      expect(output).toContain(rel);
+      expect(output).toContain("restated");
+    } finally {
+      rmSync(kit, { recursive: true, force: true });
+    }
+  });
+});
